If the trustee is a partnership, corporation or banking association, this requirement applies to that part of every meeting of the partners or directors at which trust affairs are discussed.

3.

All records of the trust are public records and shall be kept in a place which is identified by documents recorded in the Office of the County Recorder of each county in which the instrument creating the trust is recorded.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1410)

article: ARTICLE VIIA. - TRUSTS FOR FURTHERANCE OF PUBLIC FUNCTIONS
section_name: Trustees: Eligibility and status; standard of care; exemption from personal liability.
citation: Section 7A.040 - Trustees: Eligibility and status; standard of care; exemption from personal liability.
full_text:
1.

The trustee or trustees under such an instrument or will may be two or more natural persons or a partnership, corporation, national banking association or state banking association, and such trustee or trustees shall be an agency of the State and the regularly constituted authority of the beneficiary for the performance of the functions for which the trust has been created.

2.

The provisions of NRS 164.050 relating to the standard of care for a trustee in investing and managing trust property apply to the trustee or trustees of a trust created by a written instrument or will pursuant to this chapter.

3.

No trustee or beneficiary shall be charged personally with any liability whatsoever by reason of any act or omission committed or suffered in the performance of such trust or in the operation of the trust property; but any act, liability for any omission or obligation of a trustee or trustees, in the execution of such trust, or in the operation of the trust property, shall extend to the whole of the trust estate, or so much thereof as may be necessary to discharge such liability or obligation, and not otherwise.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1410)

article: ARTICLE VIIA. - TRUSTS FOR FURTHERANCE OF PUBLIC FUNCTIONS
section_name: Annual audit of trust funds, accounts, fiscal affairs: Requirements; distribution of copies; expenses.
citation: Section 7A.050 - Annual audit of trust funds, accounts, fiscal affairs: Requirements; distribution of copies; expenses.
full_text:
1.

The trustee or trustees of every trust created for the benefit and furtherance of any public function with the City as the beneficiary thereof shall cause an audit to be made of the funds, accounts and fiscal affairs of such trust, such audit to be ordered within 30 days of the close of each fiscal year of the trust.

2.

The audits required by subsection 1 shall be certified with the unqualified opinion of a certified public accountant or a public accountant notwithstanding any lesser requirement by any instrument under which the trust may have covenanted for an audit to be made or furnished. One copy of the annual audit shall be filed with the Legislative Auditor of the Legislative Counsel Bureau and one copy with each beneficiary of the trust not later than 90 days following the close of each fiscal year of the trust.

3.

If a copy of the required audit is not filed with the Legislative Auditor of the Legislative Counsel Bureau within the time provided, the Legislative Auditor is authorized to employ, at the cost and expense of the trust, a certified public accountant or a public accountant to make the required audit.

4.

The necessary expense of such audits, including the cost of typing, printing and binding, shall be paid from funds of the trust.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1411)

article: ARTICLE VIIA. - TRUSTS FOR FURTHERANCE OF PUBLIC FUNCTIONS
section_name: Franchise not required for acquisition, ownership or operation of trust property.
citation: Section 7A.060 - Franchise not required for acquisition, ownership or operation of trust property.
full_text:
No franchise is required for the acquisition, ownership or operation of any properties of a trust created for the benefit and furtherance of any public function.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1411)

article: ARTICLE VIIA. - TRUSTS FOR FURTHERANCE OF PUBLIC FUNCTIONS
section_name: Approval of certain contracts and resolutions required.
citation: Section 7A.070 - Approval of certain contracts and resolutions required.
full_text:
The trustees shall not enter into contracts for the acquisition or construction of buildings or public improvements or for the acquisition or disposal of trust properties by purchase, lease, gift, bequest or devise or any other lawful means until such contract is first approved by the City Council by ordinance. The City Council shall so approve the resolution providing for the issuance of bonds or other securities to be issued by the trustees and proposed terms of sale thereof but is not required to approve the award of such bonds to the purchaser thereof if such bonds are sold in compliance with the resolution of issuance and terms of sale.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1411)

article: ARTICLE VIIA. - TRUSTS FOR FURTHERANCE OF PUBLIC FUNCTIONS
section_name: Approval of financing method, underwriters by state board of finance.
citation: Section 7A.080 - Approval of financing method, underwriters by state board of finance.
full_text:
The State Board of Finance shall first review and approve the method of finance proposed by any trust created pursuant to the former provisions of NRS 242B.010 to 242B.100, inclusive, or the provisions of this article, and must approve the underwriter or financial institution preparing and offering the proposed issue for sale, as to the financial responsibility of such underwriter or financial institution, before such issue may be offered or sold.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1411)

article: ARTICLE VIIA. - TRUSTS FOR FURTHERANCE OF PUBLIC FUNCTIONS
full_text:
1.

The provisions of the State Securities Law, the Local Government Securities Law, the University Securities Law, or of any other general, special or local statute relating to the issuance of public securities or other debt obligations do not apply to a trust created for the benefit and furtherance of any public function.

2.

All bonds issued by any trust created for the benefit and furtherance of any public function must:

(a)

Be sold at public or private sale, as determined by the trustees and approved by the City Council. If the bonds are offered at public sale, but no satisfactory bids are received from responsible bidders at the public sale, the bonds may be sold at private sale.

(b)

Be secured:

(1)

By property, real or personal or both, having a market value equal to at least twice the principal amount of the bonds sold; or

(2)

By gross revenues from an existing revenue producing facility equal to at least one and one-half times the average annual debt service payable on the bonds.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1412; A—Ch. 596, Stats. 1995 p. 2216)

article: ARTICLE VIIA. - TRUSTS FOR FURTHERANCE OF PUBLIC FUNCTIONS
full_text:
Except as otherwise provided in section 7A.090, no statute, general, special or local, requiring competitive bidding applies to a trust created for the benefit and furtherance of a public function.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1412)

article: ARTICLE VIIA. - TRUSTS FOR FURTHERANCE OF PUBLIC FUNCTIONS
full_text:
Any trust created for the benefit and furtherance of a public function may be terminated by agreement of the trustee, or if there is more than one, then all of the trustees, and the governing body of the beneficiary, with the approval of the Governor of the State of Nevada; but such trust shall not be terminated while there exists outstanding any contractual obligations chargeable against the trust property, which, by reason of such termination, might become an obligation of the beneficiary of such trust.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1412)

1.

The City Council shall annually, at the time prescribed by law for levying taxes for State and County purposes, levy a tax at a rate allowable under applicable provisions of the Nevada Revised Statutes upon the assessed value of all real and personal property within the City except as provided in the Local Government Securities Law and the Consolidated Local Improvements Law, as amended from time to time. The taxes so levied shall be collected at the same time and in the same manner and by the same officers, exercising the same functions, as prescribed in the laws of the State of Nevada for collection of state and county taxes. The revenue laws of the State shall, in every respect not inconsistent with the provisions of this Charter, be applicable to the levying, assessing and collecting of the municipal taxes.

2.

In the matter of equalization of assessments, the rights of the City and the inhabitants thereof shall be protected in the same manner and to the same extent by the action of the County Board of Equalization as are the State and County.

3.

All forms and blanks used in levying, assessing and collecting the revenues of the State and counties shall, with such alterations or additions as may be necessary, be used in levying, assessing and collecting the revenues of the City. The City Council shall enact all such ordinances as it may deem necessary and not inconsistent with this Charter and the laws of the State for the prompt, convenient and economical collecting of the revenue.

(Ch. 266, Stats. 1971 p. 420; A—Ch. 266, Stats. 2013 p. 1217)

The City Council may pass and enact all ordinances necessary to carry into effect the revenue laws in the City and to enlarge, fix and determine the powers and duties of all officers in relation thereto.

(Ch. 266, Stats. 1971 p. 420)

1.

There is hereby created a System of Civil Service, applicable to and governing the employment of all employees of the City except Executive Officers, department directors, senior department directors, division heads, assistant city attorneys, any other attorney employed by the Office of the City Attorney, assistants to the City Manager, the Municipal Court Administrator, any elected officer, any employee that reports directly to an elected officer, any probationary employee, any temporary employee, and any other employee excluded from the System by ordinance.

2.

The System of Civil Service must be administered by a Civil Service Board composed of five persons appointed by the City Council.

3.

The Board shall prepare regulations governing the System of Civil Service to be adopted by the City Council. The regulations must provide for:

(a)

Examination of potential employees.

(b)

Procedures for recruitment and placement.

(c)

Classification of positions.

(d)

Procedures for promotion, disciplinary actions and removal of employees.

(e)

Such other matters as the Board may deem necessary.

4.

Copies of the regulations governing the System of Civil Service must be distributed to all employees of the City.

5.

An employee of the City who is included in the System of Civil Service and accepts a position that is excluded from the System pursuant to subsection 1 does not retain any rights or privileges within the System.

(Ch. 266, Stats. 1971 p. 421; A—Ch. 334, Stats. 1977 p. 630; Ch. 596, Stats. 1995 p. 2218; Ch. 108, Stats. 2003 p. 604; Ch. 266, Stats. 2013 p. 1217)

If any portion of this Charter is held to be unconstitutional or invalid for any reason by the decision of any court of competent jurisdiction, such decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining portion of this Charter. The Legislature hereby declares that it would have passed the Charter and each portion thereof, irrespective of the portion which may be deemed unconstitutional or otherwise invalid.

(Ch. 266, Stats. 1971 p. 422)

citation: Section 10.020 - Effect of enactment of charter.
full_text:
1.

All rights and property of every kind and description which were vested in the City prior to the enactment of this Charter shall be vested in the same municipal corporation on the effective date of this Charter. No right or liability, either in favor of or against such corporation existing at the time of becoming incorporated under this Charter, and no action or prosecution shall be affected by such change, but it shall stand and progress as if no change had been made.

2.

Whenever a different remedy is given by this Charter, which may properly be made applicable to any right existing at the time of such City so becoming incorporated under this Charter, such remedy shall be cumulative to the remedy before provided, and used accordingly.

3.

All ordinances and resolutions in effect in the City prior to the effective date of this Charter shall, unless in conflict with the provisions of this Charter, continue in full force and effect until amended or repealed.

4.

The enactment of this Charter shall not effect any change in the legal identity of the City.

5.

The enactment of this Charter shall not be construed to repeal or in any way affect or modify:

(a)

Any special, local or temporary law.

(b)

Any law or ordinance making an appropriation.

(c)

Any ordinance affecting any bond issue or by which any bond issue may have been authorized.

(d)

The running of the statute of limitations in force at the time this Charter becomes effective.

(e)

Any bond of any public officer.

(Ch. 266, Stats. 1971 p. 422)

section_name: General definitions and rules of construction.
citation: 1.03.010 - General definitions and rules of construction.
full_text:
The following definitions and rules of construction shall apply to this Code and to all ordinances unless the context requires otherwise.

Generally.

(1)

When provisions conflict, the specific shall prevail over the general. All provisions shall be liberally construed so that the intent of the city council may be effectuated. The provisions of this Code and all proceedings under it are to be liberally construed to affect its purposes and to promote justice.

(2)

Words and phrases shall be construed according to the common and approved usage of the language, but technical words, technical phrases and words and phrases that have acquired peculiar and appropriate meanings in law shall be construed according to such meanings.

(3)

Grammatical errors shall not vitiate, and a transposition of words and clauses may be resorted to when the sentence or clause is without meaning as it stands.

(4)

Scrivener's errors shall be ignored.

Charter. The term "charter" means the charter of the City of Henderson, Nevada.

City. The term "city" means the City of Henderson, Clark County, Nevada.

City council. The terms "city council" and "council" mean the City Council of the City of Henderson, Nevada.

Code, ordinance. The term "ordinance" means city ordinance. The term "Code" means the Henderson Municipal Code, as designated in this section. References to the Code are to the Code, as amended. References to ordinances are to ordinances as amended.

Computation of time. In computing any period of time prescribed or allowed the day of the act, event, or default from which the designated period of time begins to run shall not be included. The last day of the period so computed shall be included, unless it is a Friday, a Saturday, a Sunday, or a legal holiday day, in which event the period runs until the end of the next day which is not a Friday, Saturday, a Sunday, or legal holiday, or, when the act to be done is the filing of a paper with the city, a day on which weather or other conditions have made the city office in which the paper is to be filed inaccessible, in which event the period runs until the end of the next day which is not one of the aforementioned days. When the period of time prescribed or allowed is less than 11 days, intermediate Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays shall be excluded in the computation.

Conjunctions. In a provision involving two or more items, conditions, provisions or events, which items, conditions, provisions or events are connected by the conjunction "and," "or" or "either….or," the conjunction shall be interpreted as follows unless the context clearly required that the words "and" and "or" be interchangeable:

(1)

"And" indicates that all the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply.

(2)

"Or" indicates that the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply singly or in any combination.

(3)

"Either...or" indicates that the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply singly but not in combination.

County. The term "county" means Clark County, Nevada.

Delegation of authority. A provision that authorizes or requires a city officer or a city employee to perform an act or make a decision authorizes such officer or employee to act or make a decision through subordinates.

Gender. The masculine gender includes the feminine and neuter genders.

Health department. The term "health department" means the Southern Nevada Health District.

Includes. The term "includes" does not limit a term to a specified example.

Joint authority. Words giving a joint authority to three or more persons give such authority to a majority of all such persons.

May. The term "may" confers a right, privilege or power.

May not. The term "may not" states a prohibition and has a prohibitory effect and abridges or removes a right, privilege or power.

Must. The term "must" is to be construed as imposing a requirement.

NRS. The abbreviation "NRS" refers to the Nevada Revised Statutes, as now or hereafter amended.

Number. Words in the singular include the plural. Words in the plural include the singular.

Oath. A solemn affirmation is the equivalent to an oath and a person shall be deemed to have sworn if such person makes such an affirmation.

Officers, departments, etc. References to officers, departments, boards, commissions, committees or employees are to city officers, city departments, city boards, city commissions, city committees and city employees.

Owner. The term "owner," as applied to property, includes any part owner, joint owner, tenant in common, tenant in partnership, joint tenant or tenant by the entirety of the whole or part of such property.

Person. The term "person" means any natural person, any form of business or social organization and any other nongovernmental legal entity including, but not limited to, a corporation, partnership, association, trust or unincorporated organization. The term does not includes a government, governmental agency or political subdivision of a government to the maximum extent permitted by law.

Personal property. The term "personal property" means any property other than real property.

Premises. The term "premises," as applied to real property, includes land and structures.

Property. The term "property" includes real property, personal property and mixed property.

Public place. The term "public place" includes any street, sidewalk, park, cemetery, school yard, body or water or watercourse, public conveyance, or any place for the sale of merchandise, public accommodation or amusement.

Real property. The term "real property" or "real estate" means property consisting of land and all appurtenances to the land, including buildings and other improvements, fixtures and vegetation erected upon, affixed to, planted in or growing upon the land, and any interest, estate, benefit, right or privilege in such property.

Sale. The term "sale" includes any sale, exchange, barter, or offer for sale.

Shall. The term "shall" imposes a duty to act.

Shall not. The term "shall not" imposes a prohibition against acting.

Sidewalk. The term "sidewalk" means that portion of the street between the curb line and the adjacent property line intended for the use of pedestrians.

Signature of subscription by mark. The term "signature" or "subscription by mark" include a mark when the signer or subscriber cannot write, such signer's or subscriber's name being written near the mark by a witness who writes his own name near the signer's or subscriber's name; but a signature or subscription by mark can be acknowledged or can serve as a signature or subscription to a sworn statement only when two witnesses so sign their own names thereto.

State. The term "State" means the State of Nevada.

Street. The term "street" shall mean the entire width between the boundary line of every way publicly maintained when any part thereof is open to the use of the public for vehicular traffic.

Tenant or occupant. The terms "tenant" and "occupant," as applied to premises, include any person holding a written or oral lease, or who actually occupies the whole or any part of such premises, alone or with others.

Tenses. The present tense includes the past and future tenses. The future tense includes the present tense.

Week. The term "week" means a period of seven consecutive days.

Will. The term "will" imposes a duty to act.

Writing. The term "writing" includes any form of recorded message capable of comprehension by ordinary visual means.

Year. The term "year" means a calendar year.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

Title 1 - GENERAL PROVISIONS

Except when otherwise expressly directed by law or ordinance, upon any violation of any ordinance of the City of Henderson, the city manager, the police chief, the fire chief and authorized assistants, the managing inspector and authorized assistants, and all other authorized officers, inspectors and employees charged with the enforcement of city ordinances may prepare, sign and serve on the accused person a written citation to appear in the municipal court to answer such charge or complaint. title: Title 1 - GENERAL PROVISIONS
chapter: Chapter 1.05 - PENALTIES AND REMEDIES FOR CODE VIOLATIONS
full_text:
(a)

In this chapter "violation of this Code" means any of the following:

(1)

Doing an act that is prohibited or made or declared unlawful, an offense, a violation or a misdemeanor by ordinance or by rule or regulation authorized by ordinance.

(2)

Failure to perform an act that is required to be performed by ordinance or by rule or regulation authorized by ordinance.

(3)

Failure to perform an act if the failure is prohibited or is made or declared unlawful, an offense, a violation, or a misdemeanor by ordinance or by rule or regulation authorized by ordinance.

(b)

In this chapter "violation of this Code" does not include the failure of a city officer or city employee to perform an official duty unless it is specifically provided that the failure to perform the duty is to be punished as provided in this chapter.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

title: Title 1 - GENERAL PROVISIONS
chapter: Chapter 1.05 - PENALTIES AND REMEDIES FOR CODE VIOLATIONS
full_text:
(a)

Except as otherwise provided by law or ordinance, a person convicted of a violation of this Code shall be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in the Henderson Detention Center for not more than six months, and/or by a fine of not more than $1,000.00.

(b)

In lieu of all or part of the punishment which may be imposed pursuant to subsection (a), the convicted person may be sentenced to perform a fixed period of community service pursuant to the conditions prescribed in NRS 176.087.

(c)

In all cases where a corporation is convicted of a violation of this Code, the corporation is punishable by a fine not exceeding $1,000.00 unless otherwise provided by law or ordinance.

(d)

A person violating any administrative provision of any chapter of this Code may be assessed a civil penalty not exceeding $500.00, or as otherwise provided in such chapter.

(e)

The commission of any act within the corporate limits of the city or the failure to perform any act within such corporate limits which is made a civil infraction by the laws of the state of Nevada is declared to be and shall constitute a civil infraction under this Code. Furthermore, all procedures and administrative protocol provided by specific statute as it relates to civil infractions is hereby enacted and in effect.

(f)

A person who is found to have committed a civil infraction shall be punished by a civil penalty of not more than $500.00 per violation unless a greater or lesser civil penalty is authorized by specific statute.

(Ord. No. 4152, § 1, 3-17-2026; Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

full_text:
A.

When a defendant pleads guilty, guilty but mentally ill or is found guilty of a misdemeanor, including the violation of any municipal ordinance, the municipal judge shall include in the sentence the sum of $10.00 as an administrative assessment for the provision of court facilities and render a judgment against the defendant for the assessment.

B.

This section does not apply to an ordinance regulating metered parking or an ordinance which is specifically designated as imposing a civil penalty or liability pursuant to NRS 268.019.

C.

The money collected for an administrative assessment for the provision of court facilities must not be deducted from the fine imposed by the municipal judge but such must be taxed against the defendant in addition to the fine. The money collected for such an administrative assessment must be stated separately on the court's docket and must be included in the amount posted for bail. If the defendant is found not guilty or the charges are dismissed, the money deposited with the court must be returned to the defendant. If the judge cancels a fine because the fine has been determined to be uncollectible, any balance of the fine and the administrative assessment remaining unpaid shall be deemed to be uncollectible and the defendant is not required to pay it. If a fine is determined to be uncollectible, the defendant is not entitled to a refund of the fine or administrative assessment he has paid and the municipal judge shall not recalculate the administrative assessment.

D.

If the municipal judge permits the fine and administrative assessment for the provision of court facilities to be paid in installments, the payments must be applied in the following order:

1.

To pay the unpaid balance of an administrative assessment imposed pursuant to NRS 176.059;

2.

To pay the unpaid balance of an administrative assessment for the provision of court facilities pursuant to this section; and

3.

To pay the fine.

E.

The money collected for administrative assessments for the provision of court facilities in municipal courts must be paid by the clerk of the court to the director of finance on or before the fifth day of each month for the preceding month. The director of finance shall deposit the money received in a special revenue fund. The city may use the money in the special revenue fund only to:

1.

Acquire land on which to construct additional facilities for the municipal court;

2.

Construct or acquire additional facilities for the municipal court;

3.

Renovate or remodel existing facilities for the municipal court;

4.

Acquire furniture, fixtures and equipment necessitated by the construction or acquisition of additional facilities or the renovation of an existing facility for the municipal court. This paragraph does not authorize the expenditure of money from the fund for furniture, fixtures or equipment for judicial chambers;

5.

Acquire advanced technology for use in the additional or renovated facilities;

6.

Pay debt service on any bonds issued pursuant to subsection 3 of NRS 350.020 for the acquisition of land or facilities or the construction or renovation of facilities for the municipal court.

Any money remaining in the special revenue fund after five fiscal years must be deposited in the municipal general fund for the continued maintenance of court facilities if it has not been committed for expenditure pursuant to a plan for the construction or acquisition of court facilities or improvements to court facilities. The finance director shall provide, upon request by a municipal court, monthly reports of the revenue credited to and expenditures made from the special revenue fund.

(Ord. 1723, § 1, 1997)

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
full_text:
A.

The city manager shall have general supervision and oversight over all departments and offices of the city, excluding the municipal court and the offices of executive officers appointed by the city council pursuant to the Henderson City Charter.

B.

From time to time the city manager may:

(1)

Establish new departments, combine existing departments, or make other adjustments to the departments. Any such action by the city manager shall be effective immediately or when directed by the city manager.

(2)

Establish and adjust divisions, offices or other units within the various departments of the city, as well as offices and other units that are independent of those departments.

C.

Pursuant to Henderson City Charter, Section 1.090(3), the city manager shall appoint the following executive officers, subject to ratification of the city council:

(1)

Chief of police.

(2)

Assistant city manager.

(3)

Fire chief.

(4)

Chief financial officer.

D.

Pursuant to Henderson City Charter, Section 1.090(2), the city manager must appoint any newly established executive officer not otherwise listed in the Henderson City Charter that the city council may establish as it deems necessary for the operation of the city.

E.

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
full_text:
A.

The city manager shall have charge and supervision over all accounts and records of the city, and may inspect, or cause to be inspected, all financial records or accounts required to be kept in any of the offices or departments of the city. The city manager, or his designee, shall examine or cause to be examined, and report to the city council upon, all bills, accounts and payrolls of the city.

B.

The city manager shall direct the department of finance to develop a city financial management policy that is approved by the city council. The financial management policy shall include the elements to design, maintain and administer a reliable revenue system to support desired city services pursuant to state and federal laws.

C.

In coordination with the city attorney, the city manager shall submit to the city council for approval a city fiscal signature policy. The city fiscal signature policy shall include the signatory requirements for agreements and payments approved and executed by either the city council, the city manager, department directors or other city employees depending on the type of agreement or payment.

D.

The city manager shall direct the department of finance to develop an annual budget for the city each fiscal year, pursuant to state law.

(1)

Once the annual budget is approved and appropriated by the city council, the city manager has the authority to manage the city budget within the appropriated amounts approved by the city council.

(2)

The city manager has the ability to re-direct funds within the appropriated budget unless the re-direction would require the appropriated budget to be augmented with additional funds outside the appropriated budget. The city manager shall manage all city funds pursuant to all state and federal laws and any rules or ordinances applicable to a particular city fund.

(3)

Any augmentation to the approved annual budget requires city council approval.

(Ord. No. 3123, § 1, 2-18-2014)

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
section_name: City manager human resources and benefits duties.
citation: 2.10.040 - City manager human resources and benefits duties.
full_text:
A.

The city manager shall develop and maintain an administrative personnel policy manual that includes certain city personnel policies that establish an orderly system of personnel administration within the city.

(1)

The city manager may issue administrative personnel policies and directives in consultation with the director of human resources and the city attorney.

(2)

All city administrative personnel policies and directives shall comply with state and federal employment laws, the City of Henderson Charter, and where applicable, Henderson civil service rules or the terms of any collective bargaining agreement entered into by the city.

B.

The city manager or their designee shall act as the city's management representative for any collective bargaining units recognized by the city pursuant to NRS Chapter 288.

C.

The city manager shall manage and administer the benefit plans and programs of the city including, but not limited to, any: city funded health plans; paid time off and or sick leave programs for employees; disability and life insurance benefits for employees, and; any other benefits that city may provide. The city manager shall administer the benefit plans and programs of the city in compliance with state and federal employment laws, the City of Henderson Charter, and where applicable, Henderson civil service rules or the terms of any collective bargaining agreement entered into by the city.

(1)

The city manager may make additions or modifications to city benefit plans if the costs of such additions or modifications do not require augmentation of the city council approved annual budget.

(2)

If a city manager addition or modification to city benefit plans require an augmentation to the city council approved annual budget the augmentation must be approved by the city council before the addition or modification becomes effective.

D.

The city manager, in consultation with the director of human resources, may make modifications to city job descriptions.

E.

The city manager, in consultation with the director of human resources, may make modifications to the salary ranges or classification of city job positions pursuant to state and federal law.

F.

The city manager, in consultation with the director of human resources, the chief financial officer and the city attorney, may approve any change in salary, compensation or benefits for any city employee.

G.

The city manager, with the approval of the city attorney, may approve and execute any employment related settlement or severance agreement, including any agreement related to a city council approved reduction-in-force, early retirement or enhanced severance program.

H.

The city manager may approve any new positions within the city, or other modifications to the city employee staff compliment, if such changes do not require augmentation of the city council approved annual budget.

(Ord. No. 3123, § 1, 2-18-2014)

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
full_text:
As used in this chapter:

Coordinator means the emergency management coordinator for the city.

Disaster means a severe or prolonged emergency for which assistance is, or may be, needed to supplement the efforts and capabilities of the city to protect or avert the threat of damage to life, property, the environment, critical systems, and/or infrastructure.

Emergency means a natural or human-caused incident or set of incidents, occurring or threatened to occur, that requires responsive action by the city to protect or avert the threat of damage to life, property, the environment, critical systems, and/or infrastructure. An emergency includes, but is not limited to, an incident involving a(n) active assailant, air quality issue, chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, or explosives hazard, oil spill, civil disturbance, cybersecurity, drought, fire, flood, landslide, debris flow, geohazard, infectious disease, impact on infrastructure, severe weather, terrorism, and/or impact on transportation.

Emergency management means the management and coordination of prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery activities for emergencies and disasters, other than functions for which military forces are primarily responsible.

Emergency operations plan means the emergency response plan for the city that complies with any applicable requirements in NRS 239C.250 and NRS chapter 414, is prepared at the direction of the city manager, with input from the Henderson emergency management council in accordance with section 2.24.040, and is adopted by city council.

Human-caused means caused by human activity, including but not limited to incidents of a chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, explosive, or technological (including cyber) nature, whether accidental or intentional.

Local organization for emergency management has the same meaning as the term "local organization for emergency management" in NRS chapter 414.

Mitigation means activities designed to reduce or eliminate risks to persons, property, the environment, critical systems, and/or infrastructure or to lessen the actual or potential effects or consequences of an emergency or disaster.

Next lawful meeting means the first regular or special meeting of the city council at which the desired action may be duly noticed and taken in accordance with NRS chapter 241, without utilizing the emergency provisions under such chapter.

Preparedness means the range of deliberate, critical tasks and activities necessary to build, sustain, and improve the operational capability to prevent, protect against, mitigate against, respond to, and recover from emergencies and disasters.

Prevention means actions to avoid an incident or to intervene to stop an incident from occurring, including but not limited to actions to protect lives, property, the environment, critical systems, and infrastructure.

Recovery means the development, coordination, and execution of plans or strategies to restore impacted communities and city operations and services.

Response means efforts to minimize the short-term direct effects of an incident threatening or harming life, property, the environment, critical systems, and/or infrastructure.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 1, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 2, 1993)

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
full_text:
The emergency management coordinator for the city shall be appointed by the city manager and shall be responsible for emergency management in accordance with the state's plan and program for emergency management and for the organization, administration and operation of the local plan for emergency management subject to the direction and control of the city manager. Under that direction and control, the coordinator shall be empowered to function with the duties and responsibilities described in section 2.24.030.

(Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 3, 1993)

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
full_text:
A.

The emergency management coordinator shall be the "director" of the local organization for emergency management established by the city pursuant to NRS 414.090 and shall take the oath required pursuant to NRS 414.150 upon assuming the duties of emergency management coordinator. In the absence of the emergency management coordinator or vacancy in that position, each person designated under section 2.24.110 to fill the position of emergency management coordinator shall take the oath required pursuant to NRS 414.150 before that person assumes the duties of emergency management coordinator.

B.

The emergency management coordinator is authorized to petition, acquire and accept funds from the United States Government or any agency or office thereof, or from the State of Nevada, for emergency management purposes, as provided in the provisions of NRS 414.130.

C.

The emergency management coordinator, in collaboration with other public and private agencies within the state, may develop or cause to be developed, agreements for mutual aid or assistance in case of emergency or disaster for which the city requires such assistance. Those agreements shall be approved by the city council, shall be consistent with the state's plan and program for emergency management, and shall provide that in time of emergency or disaster each local organization for emergency management shall render assistance in accordance with the provisions of such agreements.

D.

The emergency management coordinator shall perform and exercise other such functions, powers and duties as are necessary to promote and secure public safety and protection within the territorial limits of the city and, in addition, shall conduct such functions outside the territorial limits of the city as may be required pursuant to the provisions of NRS chapter 414.

E.

The emergency management coordinator is responsible for responding to emergencies and disasters as they may occur at any time. The police communications dispatch center will be advised when the emergency management coordinator will not be available during off hours, annual leave and holidays. In order to relieve the emergency management coordinator and to temporarily assume the continuous coverage of responsibility, qualified back up employees are designated by title in section 2.24.110, Continuity of government. In order for the emergency management coordinator to respond at all hours, the emergency management coordinator shall be assigned a city take-home vehicle, in which all necessary emergency equipment, radios, publications, check lists, marked clothing, etc., will be available and ready for use. The vehicle will be used solely by the emergency management coordinator and operated in accordance with the applicable city directive. The vehicle will be used solely by the emergency management coordinator and operated in accordance with all applicable city policies and directives.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 2, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, §§ 4—7, 1993)

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
full_text:
A.

There is created the Henderson emergency management council ("EMC") which shall consist of the following:

1.

The emergency management coordinator, or their designee, who shall serve as chair of the EMC;

2.

The emergency management officer, who shall serve as vice chair of the EMC and act as chair in the absence of the emergency management coordinator; and

3.

Department heads of various departments, as appointed by the city manager, who may have key emergency responsibilities to the city government.

B.

The emergency management coordinator may invite organizations that may provide support or information during an emergency to be members of the EMC. That organization shall designate one or more people to represent it on the EMC. Those organizations and representatives shall keep all confidential information disclosed to them confidential, shall not disclose confidential information in any manner to any individual or business entity without prior written authorization from the emergency management coordinator, and are presumed to agree to these confidentiality obligations by virtue of the organization being a member of the EMC. "Confidential information" means oral or written information concerning (1) the city's emergency planning, operations or preparedness provided to the EMC, (2) the emergency operations plan, other confidential emergency response plan(s), and any confidential incident response plan(s), and/or (3) drafts of those plans.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 3, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3580, § 1, 5-21-2019; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 8, 1993)

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
full_text:
The EMC is established for the purpose of making recommendations to the city manager with respect to matters involving emergency management. The EMC shall make recommendations for the adoption of an emergency operations plan in compliance with the requirements of NRS chapters 239C and 414 and the adoption or approval of any and all mutual aid plans and agreements that are deemed necessary for the implementation of such emergency operations plan. The duties of such EMC shall also include a continuing study of the need for revisions to the emergency operations plan. The EMC shall meet upon the call of the chair.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 4, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 9, 1993)

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
full_text:
A.

In accordance with NRS 241.020(2) and (5), charter sections 2.050 and 3.010, and the emergency operations plan, the mayor, mayor pro tempore, or a majority of the members of the city council may call an emergency meeting. If it is determined that an emergency or disaster exists, the city council shall declare in writing that a state of emergency exists and shall publicize, by a method deemed appropriate by city council, the existence of the emergency or disaster. If circumstances prohibit timely action by the city council, then the mayor, mayor pro tempore, city manager, or emergency management coordinator may issue a declaration of state of emergency and seek the ratification of that declaration by a majority of a quorum of the city council at the next lawful meeting. If the city council fails to ratify that declaration of state of emergency at the next lawful meeting, then that declaration shall automatically terminate when that next lawful meeting adjourns.

B.

The city council or city manager shall terminate the declaration of state of emergency when the emergency or disaster no longer exists or the threat of an emergency has passed.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 5, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 10, 1993)

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
full_text:
The operational emergency management organization of the city shall consist of officers and employees of the city designated by the emergency management coordinator, as well as all volunteer workers. The functions and duties of this organization shall be distributed among such divisions, services and special staff as the city manager shall prescribe. The operational emergency management organization is the "local organization for emergency management" established pursuant to NRS 414.090.

The emergency management coordinator, with the approval of city manager, shall set forth the form of organization, establish and designate divisions and services, assign functions, duties and powers, and designate officers and employees to carry out the provisions of this chapter. Insofar as possible, the form of organization, titles and terminology shall conform to the recommendations of the federal government and the recommendations of the emergency management agency of the State of Nevada. A specific directive creating this organization by name will be developed by the emergency management coordinator, approved by the city manager, and updated periodically in the emergency operations plan as necessary.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 6, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 11, 1993)

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL

citation: 2.24.080 - Emergency powers of city manager and emergency management coordinator.
full_text:
A.

At the inception of and during a disaster or emergency, the city manager or the emergency management coordinator:

1.

Shall implement the city's emergency operations plan and may direct and control such other city employees as are required to implement the plan from the emergency operations center (EOC) or other designated location(s);

May, through requisition or contract with private parties or other government entities, obtain necessary services, supplies and equipment needed to protect life and property and implement the plan; and may bind the city for the value thereof without being required to comply with the normal purchasing procedures, if compliance with those procedures would unreasonably hamper or impair the implementation the plan; and

May suspend the licensing requirements for persons whose services are required for implementation of the emergency operations plan.

The emergency powers granted the city manager and emergency management coordinator under this section may be revoked, limited or restricted by order of the city council.

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
section_name: Measures to maintain peace and order.
citation: 2.24.090 - Measures to maintain peace and order.
full_text:
If a declared state of emergency exists within the city, the city council may, if it deems it necessary to maintain peace and protect the public, take action and order and enforce the measures listed in this section. If circumstances prohibit the timely action of the city council, the city manager, mayor, mayor pro tempore, or emergency management coordinator may, under the same circumstances, order measures and take actions consistent with the items listed below and shall report their actions to the city council at its next lawful meeting. During the existence of a state of emergency, to the full extent permitted by law, including in the exercise of any delegation of authority by the Governor of the State of Nevada, the city council or, if authorized by the city council or in the event that circumstances prohibit the timely action of city council, the city manager, mayor, mayor pro tempore, or emergency management coordinator may:

A.

Establish a curfew for the area designated as an emergency area which fixes the hours during which persons other than officially authorized personnel may be upon the public streets or other public places;

B.

Prohibit or limit the number of persons who may gather or congregate upon any public street, public place or any outdoor place within the area designated as an emergency area;

C.

Barricade streets and roads, as well as access points onto streets and roads, and prohibit or restrict vehicular or pedestrian traffic in the area;

D.

Enter into contracts and incur obligations necessary to combat such an emergency or disaster, protect the health and safety of persons and property and provide emergency assistance to the victims of such an emergency or disaster to the full extent permitted under NRS chapter 332, NRS chapter 414, or other applicable law;

E.

Redirect funds for emergency use to the full extent permitted under NRS chapter 414 or other applicable law;

F.

Suspend standard procurement procedures to obtain necessary services or equipment to the full extent permitted under NRS chapter 332, NRS chapter 414, or other applicable law;

G.

Commit to mutual aid agreements; and

H.

Take such other actions and perform and exercise such other functions, powers and duties as are necessary to promote and secure the safety and protection of the civilian population.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 8, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 13, 1993)

title: Title 2 - ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL
full_text:
A.

To the extent necessary during or after the existence of a declared emergency or disaster and under the direction of the city manager, the director of the city's public works department may remove debris which threatens the public health or safety. Any action taken by the director under this section shall be reported by the city manager to the city council at its next lawful meeting. Under the direction and control of the city manager, the director may:

1.

Use the city departments, mutual aid agreements with other governmental entities or, if necessary, private resources; and

2.

Accept funds from the federal government or the state and utilize those funds for the purpose of removing such debris.

B.

Debris which exists on city-owned property may be removed at city expense, provided that the expense of removing any debris caused by the negligent or intentional act of any person may be recovered from that person.

C.

The public works director may order that debris which exists on privately owned property be removed by the owner of the property or the person responsible for the property at the owner's or other person's expense. Each order must specify the nature of the threat to the public and the minimum quantity of debris which must be removed to eliminate the threat. During an emergency, the order is effective when orally conveyed to the owner or other person responsible for the property.

D.

Upon the failure of a person to comply with an order described in this section, the public works director may remove or cause the removal of the debris. The owner of the property or the person responsible for the property is liable to the city for the costs incurred.

E.

When immediate emergency measures are determined necessary for protection of public health and safety, or public or private property, and oral or written authorization cannot be obtained from the owner or other person responsible for the property, the public works director may authorize the entry upon the public or private lands or waters and perform such tasks necessary to the emergency removal or clearance operations.

full_text:
A.

Catastrophic events can interrupt, paralyze and/or destroy the ability of local governments to carry out their legislative, executive and judicial functions. Therefore, it is imperative that a "continuity of government" (COG) be structured with the capability to preserve, maintain, and/or reconstitute its ability to function under the threat or occurrence of any emergency that could disrupt local government and public services.

B.

In order to continue governmental functions, it is necessary to establish replacements for key positions through three levels where possible. The following positions are considered key positions in emergency management, and any absences and vacancies will be filled by the person holding the title indicated or, if the title indicated does not correspond with an existing position, by the person holding the functionally equivalent position under a different title, in order as follows:
