title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
A.

For every person who carries on, practices, or professes to practice the business of palmistry, phrenology, life reading, fortunetelling, cartomancy, clairvoyance, clairaudience, crystal gazing, mediumship, prophecy, augury, divination or necromancy, and demands or receives a fee for the exercise or exhibition of his respective arts, directly or indirectly, or incidental to the conduct of any other business, either as a gift, donation, or otherwise, or who gives an exhibition thereof at any place where an admission fee is charged the license fee shall be $100.00 semiannually.

B.

Application for a psychic arts practitioner license shall be made to the division accompanied by a nonrefundable investigation fee deposit, as set forth in chapter 4.03, to conduct a police department criminal background investigation of the applicant. (See subsection 4.04.060(B)). No person shall be issued a psychic arts practitioner license unless such person meets all the qualifications provided for below:

1.

A psychic arts practitioner license shall be limited to areas permitting professional offices or any commercial or industrial use, and provided that the use is operated in compliance with title 19;

2.

A background investigation shall be conducted; and the results shall be furnished to the director who will make a determination on the finding of suitably of the applicant; and

3.

The division shall forward a recommendation to the council to approve or deny the license based on the finding of suitability and the application submitted; and

4.

The applicant shall be at least 18 years of age.

C.

No employee or other person shall assist the licensee in any audience or reading, except psychic healings, nor shall any mechanical device of any description whatsoever be used by the licensee in the conduct of any interview, audience or reading.

D.

A psychic arts practitioner license is a privileged license and may be suspended, limited or revoked, or other disciplinary action taken with respect thereto for the failure of the licensee to comply with the requirements of this section.

E.

Each licensee shall be responsible for the acts of their employees and agents committed during the course and scope of employment. Each licensee shall accordingly use adequate care in the selection of their employees and agents. In any license suspension, limitation or revocation proceedings, the fact that the licensee did not have actual knowledge of the events complained of shall be no defense and every licensee accepts their license subject to said condition.

F.

This section shall not be construed to apply to doctors, dentists, or other medical practitioners licensed by the appropriate board under Nevada Revised Statutes or to a person employed by such doctors, dentists, or other medical practitioners acting under their direction and control, who use any psychic arts as an aid in the treatment or as a supplementary form of treatment in the course of their profession.

G.

This section shall not be construed to apply to astrologers licensed under section 4.05.140.

(Ord. No. 3583, § 6, 6-4-2019; Ord. No. 3291, § 1, 10-6-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
Each applicant for a temporary sales or service permit shall pay a permit fee of $50.00. The permit shall be for a period not to exceed 14 calendar days and must be for one location. Further, except as otherwise provided herein, an applicant is limited to one temporary sales or service permit per calendar quarter.

A.

Each applicant shall furnish the following to the division no later than ten calendar days prior to the event:

1.

Written permission of the property owner or, in the case of a retail location, the written authorization of the store management;

2.

Proof of a State of Nevada sales tax permit, if applicable;

3.

Approval of the community development and services department; and

4.

Any other license or permit as may be required by any department of the city, the state, or the federal government.

B.

The requirement to submit applications for temporary sales or service permits ten calendar days prior to the scheduled event may be waived at the director's discretion.

C.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the director may issue temporary sales or service permits to an applicant in excess of the one permit per calendar quarter limit, in the following instances:

1.

For pumpkin sales lots, haunted houses, and Christmas tree sales lots.

a.

The temporary sales or service permit for these activities may exceed 14 days.

b.

In no case shall the sales or service permit exceed a period of 45 calendar days.

2.

For arts, crafts and business trade shows.

a.

For purposes of this chapter an arts, crafts and business trade show is an event with a minimum of 20 vendors wherein at least 50 percent of the vendors provide only handmade items, including, but not limited to, decorative items, clothing and food that has been created for sale by the craftsman.

b.

In no case may an applicant exempt from the restriction of one temporary sales or service permit per calendar quarter pursuant to subsection 4.05.375(C)(2) be granted more than 16 temporary sales or service permits in a single calendar year, and no more than two temporary sales or service permits in any single month.

3.

If a conditional use permit has been approved by the planning commission or council in excess of the stated limit of one per calendar quarter, but in no case shall an applicant be granted more than eight temporary sales or service permits in a single calendar year.

(Ord. No. 3483, § 1, 5-15-2018; Ord. No. 3291, § 1, 10-6-2015)

Editor's note— Ord. No. 3483, § 1, adopted May 15, 2018, changed the title of section 4.05.375 from "Temporary sales permit" to "Temporary sales or service permit." The historical notation has been preserved for reference purposes.

section_name: Division to cooperate with other regulatory agencies.
citation: 4.06.030 - Division to cooperate with other regulatory agencies.
full_text:
A.

The division shall cooperate with other public agencies concerned with the regulation and control of business licenses, and to that end may exchange with such agencies any and all types of confidential information, including, without limitation, information regarding licensees, their independent contractors, operations, agents and employees. When dealing with any gaming matter, the division may immediately inform the state gaming agencies of any investigation, hearing or other actions that the division, its officers or the director intends to take or is considering taking against a licensee.

B.

The division may enter into one or more agreements with the state gaming agencies such that duplication of effort shall be kept to a minimum; provided, however, that if the apparent violation is of such a character that action should be taken and if the state gaming agencies fail, refuse or decline to assume control of the investigation and hearing, then the division shall promptly investigate.

C.

The division may enter into one or more agreements with liquor and gaming boards in the incorporated and unincorporated cities and towns of Clark County so that overall regulation and control may be more effectively maintained.

D.

The division may enter into one or more agreements with state professional and/or occupational licensing boards so that overall regulation and control may be more effectively maintained.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
section_name: Complaint against license—Determination by city attorney.
citation: 4.06.040 - Complaint against license—Determination by city attorney.
full_text:
In addition to any action taken by the division for a violation of this title, the city attorney, or his designee, may investigate the violation(s) to determine whether there is cause for additional disciplinary action, such as suspension or revocation of the license, or suspension or revocation of a conditional use permit pursuant to title 19.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
full_text:
If the city attorney is satisfied that based upon the requirements of title 4 grounds exist for the revocation or suspension of a license or permit or for discipline of a licensee or permittee, the city attorney shall draft a complaint and notice of hearing, both of which shall be filed with the city clerk and served on the licensee, permittee, or registered agent either personally or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, at the address on file with the division. The complaint and notice of hearing shall be served at least 20 days prior to the hearing.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
full_text:
The notice of hearing shall be in substantially the following form, but may include other information:

YOU ARE HEREBY NOTIFIED that a hearing will be held before a duly appointed hearing officer at (insert place of hearing) on the (insert day) of (insert month), (insert year) at (insert time), upon the charges made in the complaint served upon you herewith. You may be present at the hearing and may be represented by counsel. You may present any relevant evidence, call witnesses and cross-examine all witnesses testifying against you.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
full_text:
The complaint shall be a written statement of charges that shall set forth the facts and/or omissions with which the licensee or permittee is charged. The complaint shall specify the code sections, regulations and/or provisions of law that the licensee or permittee is alleged to have violated or the hazard or threat to the public health, safety or welfare allegedly attributable to the licensee or permittee and the facts supporting such allegations.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
full_text:
A.

The licensee or permittee must, at least ten days prior to the scheduled hearing, file with the city clerk its answer responding to the charges made in the complaint and set forth any defenses it intends to raise, and serve a copy of the answer upon the city attorney and the appointed hearing officer.

B.

The answer to the complaint shall be signed and verified by the licensee or permittee, or his agent. The complaint and answer shall form the pleadings for the hearing. In connection with the complaint and hearing process, the licensee or permittee is the "respondent".

C.

The answer shall include the following:

To the hearing officer for the city council:

1.

The respondent admits the following facts set forth in the complaint.

2.

The respondent denies the following facts set forth in the complaint.

3.

The respondent believes the following defenses and explanations should be considered by the hearing officer for the city council.

4.

The respondent raises the following legal defenses.

5.

Upon the filing of an answer, the respondent shall be entitled to a hearing on the merits upon the issues denied by the answer.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

full_text:
A.

Failure of the respondent to answer within the time specified shall be deemed an admission of the allegations in the complaint. Thereupon, the hearing officer shall impose such disciplinary action as requested in the complaint, and shall give notice of such disciplinary action by mailing a true copy thereof by United States certified mail in a sealed envelope with postage thereon fully prepaid, addressed to the respondent at respondent's latest address of record.

B.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
section_name: Hearing officers—Appointment, qualifications, conflict of interest, disqualification.
citation: 4.06.100 - Hearing officers—Appointment, qualifications, conflict of interest, disqualification.
full_text:
A.

A hearing officer shall be appointed with regard to his or her qualifications to conduct administrative or quasi-judicial hearings and must:

1.

Be a resident of the State of Nevada;

2.

Be licensed to practice law in the State of Nevada and have at least ten years of experience practicing law;

3.

Have significant experience in the practice of administrative law or as a hearing officer or administrative law judge in contested cases;

4.

Not be affiliated or associated with the city in any other manner, such as for example, as agent, employee, fiduciary officer, or any other type of representative of the city.

B.

No person may act as a hearing officer in a matter in which he or she has a direct or substantial financial interest or other conflict of interest. For purposes of this chapter, "conflict of interest" means a pecuniary or personal interest sufficient to affect his or her independent judgment and the objective exercise of his or her public duty.

C.

Either the city or the respondent may move to disqualify a hearing officer prior to any hearing by filing a written motion and supporting affidavits of conflict of interest. Such a motion shall be served upon the city clerk, the non-moving party, and the city manager's office. The city manager or his designee shall rule upon the motion.

(Ord. No. 3417, § 1, 7-11-2017; Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
section_name: Hearing officers—Appointment to list and compensation.
citation: 4.06.110 - Hearing officers—Appointment to list and compensation.
full_text:
The city council may appoint individuals to a list of hearing officers based on their qualifications. Hearing officers shall be entitled to compensation from the city for the time reasonably expended in the process of preparing for, hearing and deciding the case at a rate to be set by the city manager with a maximum chargeable time of 20 hours per hearing. In the event that a hearing officer serves more than 20 hours on any given hearing, he may submit to the city manager a written statement requesting additional compensation and setting forth reasons therefor. The city manager may authorize such additional compensation at the set rate if the city manager is satisfied that the additional hours of service were justified and necessary. As a condition to receiving payment, the hearing officer must submit an itemized invoice for services rendered to the city manager within 30 days after the hearing officer's decision is served upon the parties.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
full_text:
Upon the filing of a complaint by the city attorney:

A.

The city manager or designee on behalf of the city council shall select a hearing officer from the appointed list, or engage an attorney to act as a hearing officer if there is not a current list or the number of attorneys on the list is insufficient for any reason, and provide the selected hearing officer with a copy of the complaint.

B.

The city manager or designee shall obtain written verification from the selected hearing officer that there is no conflict of interest or other reason precluding the hearing officer from serving on the particular matter assigned.

C.

If a hearing officer is able to serve on the case, the city manager or designee shall obtain a hearing date and other information to be included in the notice of hearing pursuant to section 4.06.140. If the selected hearing officer cannot hear the case within the time parameters set forth in section 4.06.140, the city manager shall select another hearing officer and follow the procedure set forth in subsections (1) and (2) of this section.

D.

If a hearing officer does not accept the appointment within five days of his selection, the hearing officer shall be discharged and another hearing officer selected pursuant to the provisions of this section. A hearing officer discharged pursuant to this section will not be entitled to be compensated for any costs or fees associated with the case from which the hearing officer was discharged.

(Ord. No. 3417, § 1, 7-11-2017; Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
full_text:
The hearing officer shall preside over hearings determining allegations of violations of title 4 and possess all the powers of the city council in determining such matters including but not limited to:

A.

Coordinating with the city manager's office to set the time and date of the hearing.

B.

Hearing any motions, stipulations or orders upon which the parties agree and addressing any administrative details.

C.

Continuing a hearing based on good cause shown by one of the parties to the hearing or if the hearing officer independently determines that good cause exists.

D.

Issuing a subpoena for witnesses, documents, and other evidence as requested by the parties and in accordance with chapter 4.06.

E.

Imposing disciplinary action, including but not limited to suspension or revocation of the business license or permit.

(Ord. No. 3417, § 1, 7-11-2017; Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

full_text:
A.

All hearings shall be held at city hall or other city-owned facility within the city of Henderson.

B.

Upon the appointment of a hearing officer to hear the case, the hearing officer shall coordinate with the city manager's office to set the time and date for the hearing which will be included in the notice of hearing to be served upon the respondent with the complaint. title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
full_text:
The following procedures shall apply at all hearings conducted pursuant to this title:

A.

The proceedings at the hearing shall be reported either stenographically and/or by audio recorder.

B.

Oral evidence shall be taken upon oath or affirmation administered by the hearing officer.

C.

Each party to a hearing shall have the right:

1.

To call and examine witnesses;

2.

To introduce exhibits relevant to the issues of the case;

3.

To cross-examine opposing witnesses on matters relative to the issues of the case;

4.

To impeach any witness regardless of which party called the witness to testify; and

5.

To offer rebuttal evidence.

D.

If the respondent does not testify on respondent's own behalf, respondent may be called and examined as if under cross-examination.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
full_text:
A.

The hearing need not be conducted according to technical rules relating to evidence and witnesses. Any relevant evidence may be admitted, subject to the provisions of this section.

B.

Irrelevant, immaterial or unduly repetitious evidence must be excluded. Effect shall be given to the rules of privilege recognized by law. Objections to evidentiary offers may be made and must be noted in the record. Subject to the requirements of this subsection, when a hearing will be expedited and the interests of the parties will not be prejudiced substantially, any part of the evidence may be received in written form.

C.

Every witness shall declare, by oath or affirmation, that he or she will testify truthfully.

D.

Notice may be taken of judicially cognizable facts and of generally recognized technical or scientific facts within the specialized knowledge of the city's departments and divisions. Parties must be notified of the material noticed and afforded an opportunity to contest the material so noticed. The experience, technical competence and specialized knowledge of the city's departments and divisions may be utilized in the evaluation of the evidence.

E.

The hearing officer shall have the authority to regulate the course of the hearing, hold conferences for the settlement or simplification of issues, dispose of procedural requests, and rule upon offers of proof and questions of relevance.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
full_text:
A.

Except as otherwise provided in this section, in any hearing pursuant to this title, the hearing must proceed as follows:

1.

The hearing officer shall call the hearing to order.

2.

The parties and their representatives shall be introduced for the record.

3.

The hearing officer shall consider any preliminary motions, offers of settlement, stipulations or orders and shall address any administrative details regarding the hearing.

4.

The hearing officer:

a.

Shall ask the parties if they want any witness excluded from the hearing.

b.

Shall instruct any witness who is excluded from the hearing not to discuss the case during the course of the hearing.

c.

Shall allow the respondent to remain in the hearing.

d.

May, on its own motion, exclude any witness from the hearing.

5.

The city may present a brief opening statement of the charges, explaining the theory of the case and what the evidence will show;

6.

The respondent or respondent's attorney may present a brief opening statement;

7.

The city will present evidence, subject to cross-examination by the respondent's counsel and the hearing officer;

8.

The respondent or respondent's counsel may present evidence, subject to cross-examination by the city and the hearing officer;

9.

The hearing officer may question a witness at any time during the hearing. If a witness is questioned by the hearing officer, the party who called the witness may request permission to ask further questions, limited to the area addressed by the hearing officer. When the party who called the witness has asked those questions, the other party may request permission to ask further questions, limited to the area addressed by the hearing officer.

10.

After the city and respondent have presented their cases, the hearing officer may allow the city and respondent to call rebuttal witnesses. If the city or respondent, or both, call one or more rebuttal witnesses, each rebuttal witness must be sworn in and questioned in the same manner as other witnesses.

11.

Closing statements may be made at the conclusion of the evidence by both parties. These statements may include summaries of the evidence and legal arguments. The city will present its closing statement first, and then the respondent may present its closing argument. If the respondent makes a closing statement, the city may make a final closing argument.

12.

Either party may recommend specific disciplinary action to the hearing officer at the appropriate time.

B.

The hearing officer may deviate from the order of the hearing set forth in subsection (1) if the hearing officer:

1.

Upon a showing of good cause, deems it appropriate; or

2.

Deems it necessary to expedite or ensure the fairness of the hearing.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

The hearing shall be reported and/or recorded by any means determined appropriate by the hearing officer. If any party desires the hearing transcribed by a certified court reporter, that party must make the necessary arrangements and bear the costs thereof.

The written decision shall contain findings of fact, conclusions of law, a determination of the alleged violations presented and the disciplinary action to be imposed. title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
section_name: Attorney's fees and costs incurred by city.
citation: 4.06.270 - Attorney's fees and costs incurred by city.
full_text:
A.

The hearing officer may order respondent to pay reasonable attorney's fees and costs that are incurred by the city as part of its investigative, administrative and disciplinary proceedings against the respondent if the hearing officer enters a final order in which it finds that the respondent has violated any provision of this title.

B.

As used in this section, "costs" means:

1.

Costs of an investigation.

2.

Costs for photocopies, facsimiles, long distance telephone calls and postage and delivery.

3.

Fees for court reporters at the hearing.

4.

Fees for expert witnesses and other witnesses at the hearing.

5.

Fees for necessary interpreters at the hearing.

6.

Fees for service and delivery of process and subpoenas.

7.

Expenses for research, including, without limitation, reasonable and necessary expenses for computerized services for legal research.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION
full_text:
A.

Within ten days after service of an order of the hearing officer, any party aggrieved may petition for reconsideration. Such petition shall not be granted except upon a showing that:

1.

There is additional evidence that is material, unavailable at the time of the original hearing, necessary and reasonably calculated to change the decision of the hearing officer; or

2.

Granting the petition is necessary to correct a manifest error of law or fact; or

3.

Granting the petition is necessary to prevent manifest injustice.

Any petition based on the unavailability of evidence shall be supported by an affidavit or declaration of the moving party or the moving party's counsel showing with particularity the materiality and necessity of the additional evidence and the reason why it was not introduced at the hearing.

B.

The petition shall be served upon the non-moving party and the hearing officer. The hearing officer shall provide the non-moving party an opportunity to respond to the petition either in writing or at a hearing scheduled by the hearing officer.

C.

After the granting of a petition, the hearing officer may modify his or her decision and order. Any such modification must be made in writing within 30 days of the filing of the petition for rehearing and must be served on the parties, either personally or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

full_text:
As an alternative to criminal prosecution for a violation of any provision of title 4, the city may impose a civil penalty in accordance with the provision of this chapter.

(Ord. No. 3303, § 1, 10-20-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
A.

A civil penalty under this chapter shall be imposed by the issuance of a notice of violation by the city. The notice of violation must contain, at a minimum, the following information:

1.

The name and address (if known) of the person or entity responsible for the violation;

2.

A brief description of the violation and a reference to the applicable ordinance or code citation(s);

3.

The location, date and time of the violation;

4.

The name of the person issuing the notice of violation;

5.

The amount of the civil penalty; and

6.

Information advising of the manner and time for responding to the notice of violation.

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
A.

The individual or licensee, referred to herein as the "person" per section 4.04.010, cited must respond to a notice of violation within the time prescribed by section 4.07.060 of this chapter in one of the following ways:

1.

Admit responsibility for the commission of the violation and liability by paying the amount of the civil penalty; or

2.

Appeal the notice of violation, or civil penalty by submitting a written request for an administrative hearing to the division. The request for hearing must contain the following information:

a.

The name of the person on the notice of violation;

b.

The current address and contact telephone number of the person;

c.

The notice(s) of violation(s) which the person wishes to dispute at the hearing;

d.

The basis or facts supporting the appeal; and

e.

The requested relief.

B.

After receipt of a person's written request for a hearing, the division shall set a hearing date and provide notice of the hearing to the person requesting it at least 14 days before the date of the hearing, unless a shorter time period is agreed to in writing by the division and the individual. The notice shall state the date, time, and location of the hearing, and shall include a short explanation of the hearing process.

C.

The business operations manager of the department, or authorized designee (the "presiding officer"), shall preside over hearings conducted pursuant to this chapter except under the following circumstances:

1.

If the city attorney initiates a disciplinary action for suspension or revocation of a business license, an appeal hearing under this chapter may be held in conjunction with the disciplinary action hearing, presided over by a hearing officer appointed pursuant to chapter 4.06;

2.

If the business operations manager determines that the circumstances so warrant, the business operations manager may refer an appeal under this chapter to the city manager's office. Upon receiving a referral, the city manager may appoint an assistant city manager or the director (or designee) of another city department as the presiding officer for the referred appeal hearing.

D.

The presiding officer shall conduct the hearing, direct the order of the proceedings, and hear all evidence presented relevant to the subject notice of violation and appeal. The hearing shall be conducted informally and shall not be constrained by evidentiary or procedural rules applicable to public hearings or judicial proceedings. The hearing shall provide an opportunity for the parties to present witness statements or testimony and other evidence regarding the subject notice of violation for the purpose of dispensing a fair and speedy resolution. The presiding officer may question witnesses, allow rebuttal testimony, limit the time of the hearing to a reasonable length, limit the presentation of immaterial or unduly repetitious evidence, and record the hearing.

E.

If the person requesting a hearing fails to appear at the hearing without having first sought and obtained a continuance of the hearing, the presiding officer may enter a decision upholding the violation and the full amount of the civil penalty scheduled to be reviewed. The burden of proving any defense shall be upon the person raising such defense.

F.

Upon the conclusion of the hearing, the presiding officer shall consider all evidence presented and shall issue a decision to uphold, reverse, or modify the disputed violation and/or citation. Written notice of the decision shall be issued no later than 30 days following the conclusion of the hearing. The decision shall clearly state one of the following:

1.

That the notice of violation is upheld, including a short statement of findings explaining the basis for the decision, and providing a deadline and any conditions for the payment of any civil penalty;

2.

That the notice of violation is reversed, including a short statement of findings explaining the basis for the decision; or

3.

That the notice of violation and/or penalties are modified, including a short statement of findings explaining the basis for the decision, and providing a deadline and any conditions for any modified compliance obligations and payments of any civil penalty.

G.

Any decision by the presiding officer pursuant to this chapter shall be a final determination.

H.

The city attorney may file a petition in a court of competent jurisdiction, including the Henderson municipal court for the entry of a civil judgment against the person in an amount equal to that stated in the written decision if the city attorney determines this action to be necessary to enforce the decision. Service of such petition on the defendant must be made by certified mail, return receipt requested, restricted delivery, addressed to the defendant at the defendant's last known address, or in any other manner which is authorized by law. An affidavit or declaration of mailing, a signed, returned receipt, or other evidence of service of the civil judgment shall be filed upon such service of the petition.

(Ord. No. 3936, § 1, 1-3-2022; Ord. No. 3303, § 1, 10-20-2015)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
All auction sales shall be conducted as follows:

A.

Each day before the commencement of the auction, the licensee or permittee shall announce the terms of the sale.

B.

The licensee or permittee, at each time a bid is announced or accepted, shall give some description of the person making the bid, and also point out or designate the location of the bidder on the premises.

C.

No licensee or permittee, his agents, employees, or the owner, or other person on his behalf, shall make any false or misleading statement concerning the ownership kind, character, quality, condition, make, size, price, or other fact pertaining to any article sold or offered for sale.

D.

No licensee or permittee, his employee, or the owner, or other person on his behalf, shall act as a by-bidder, or what is commonly known as a "capper" or "booster," or make or accept any false or misleading bid, or falsely pretend to buy or sell any article, or conspire with any person to make a false or fictitious bid; and no licensee or permittee, his employee, or the owner of the articles, or other person acting on his behalf, shall bid or purchase at such sale, unless, at the time such bid is made, the permittee shall announce, in such tone and manner as to be plainly heard and understood in all parts of the room in which the sale is being conducted, that such bid is for the benefit of the permittee, his employee or owner, as the case may be.

E.

Each article offered for sale shall be sold as offered, if a bid be made by more than one bona fide bidder, before another article is offered for sale, and without any unreasonable delay. There shall be no reserved price on any article unless, at the time the article is offered for sale, the licensee or permittee shall announce the reserved price in such tone and manner as to be plainly heard and understood in all parts of the room in which the sale is being conducted. If any article is offered for sale and two or more bids are made thereon, and such article is afterwards withdrawn from sale for the reason that the highest bidder did not equal the reserved price as announced, there shall not be the same or another article of the same kind or class offered for sale until four other sales have been made, or for one hour, whichever is the longer time.

F.

No free drawing shall be conducted, nor gifts be given, nor any form of entertainment be given for the encouragement of attendance at such sale, or for any other purpose.

G.

Upon request of any person who has bid upon an article offered for sale, the licensee or permittee shall allow such bidder a reasonable opportunity to examine such article, and such bidder may thereafter withdraw his bid at any time before the licensee or permittee declares the article sold.

H.

The licensee or permittee shall allow any police officer, the director or his designee, during regular business hours, to examine any article held for sale by auction or offered for sale, at any time before such article is delivered to the purchaser.

I.

No person other than the licensee or permittee shall cry the sale of any article at said auction sale.

full_text:
The following words, terms, and phrases, and their derivations, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

A.

Canvasser means any natural person who is not in the business of selling goods and who makes or attempts to make personal contact with a resident at his residence, without prior specific invitation or appointment from the resident, for the primary purpose of (1) distributing or attempting to distribute a handbill or flyer advertising a noncommercial item, cause, event or service or (2) making or attempting to make noncommercial surveys for research purposes, analysis, opinion polls and any similar work.

B.

Charitable purpose is defined to mean any benevolent, philanthropic, patriotic, religious or eleemosynary group, partnership, association or corporation which solicits and collects funds for charitable purposes and is classified in one of the categories defined in Section 501 of the United States Internal Revenue Code as being exempt from payment of federal income tax as evidenced by the organization's 501 registration number or is duly organized pursuant to Nevada Revised Statutes Chapters 81, 82, 84 or 86.

C.

Peddler means any natural person other than a mobile food vendor who goes upon the premises of any private residence in the city, not having been invited by the resident or occupant thereof, carrying or transporting goods, wares, merchandise or personal property of any nature and offering or attempting to offer the same for sale. "Peddler" does not include a natural person who distributes handbills or flyers for a commercial purpose, advertising an event, activity, good, or service that is offered to a resident for purchase at a location away from his residence or at a time different from the time of visit.

D.

Solicitor means any natural person other than a mobile food vendor who goes upon the premises of any private residence in the city, not having been invited by the resident or occupant thereof, for the primary purpose of taking or attempting to take orders for the sale of goods, merchandise, wares or other personal property of any nature for future delivery, or for services to be performed in the future. "Solicitor" includes any natural person who distributes a handbill or flyer advertising a commercial event, good, or service. This definition also includes any natural person who, without invitation, goes upon private residential property for the primary purpose of requesting a donation for political, charitable, religious purposes or other noncommercial purpose, even if incidental to such purpose the solicitor offers or provides goods or services.

Any person or entity who employs, contracts, or otherwise engages another to conduct soliciting, peddling, or canvassing activities, is responsible for the acts or omissions of his employees or agents committed during the course of employment or performance of activities governed by this chapter. In any suspension, limitation, or revocation proceeding, the fact that the distributing service or person who employed, contracted, or engaged another did not have actual knowledge of the violation shall be no defense.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
chapter: Chapter 4.12 - DOOR-TO-DOOR SOLICITORS, PEDDLERS AND CANVASSERS
full_text:
It shall be unlawful for any natural person, while canvassing, peddling or soliciting, to enter upon any residential premises or to knock on the door, window or any other part of the residential structure, or ring the bell of any residential premises, or to do any other act calculated to attract the attention of anyone inside of the premises, where the owner, resident, occupant or person legally in charge of the premises has posted, at the entry, or any of the points of ingress to the premises, a sign with visible and legible letters at least three-fourths of an inch in height bearing the words "No Trespassers," "No Canvassers," "No Peddlers," "No Solicitors," or words of similar import. A sign containing any of these or similar phrases is deemed to prohibit all activities governed by this chapter. This regulation shall apply to all groups of structures or complexes such as apartments, condominiums or private gated communities, which have posted such a sign or signs with letters at least one and one-half inches in height at the entrance(s) or other point(s) of ingress regardless of whether any individual particular residence is posted.

This section shall not apply, however, when the solicitor, peddler or canvasser has, despite the signage, been specifically invited by the owner, resident, occupant or person legally in charge of the premises.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
Whenever used in this chapter, the words and terms shall have the meaning ascribed to them pursuant to title 4, unless a different meaning clearly appears in the definitions or context:

Activated alarm system means an alarm system which has been set, or turned on; in which condition it will emit a noise, turn on lights, dial a telephone or send a signal to a monitoring station, or any other means of signaling, when the alarm has been activated.

Alarm condition means that a situation exists, determined by an alarm monitoring business, or other means, which is used to summon emergency response personnel.

Alarm system means any mechanism, equipment or device which is designed to detect an unauthorized entry into any building or onto any property, or to direct attention to a crime in progress, or to signal an emergency of any kind, and to signal the above occurrence either by a local or audible alarm or by a silent or remote alarm. Alarm systems shall not include alarms installed in motor vehicles.

Alarm systems business means any person engaging in the business of planning, installing, servicing, maintaining, repairing or replacing, or monitoring alarm systems in the city. "Alarm systems business" shall also mean any person acting as a contractor or subcontractor for or with an alarm systems business as described.

Applicant means any person who has requested, or is about to request, licensing as an alarm systems business, or any person who has requested, or is about to request, a building permit to install an alarm system at a particular location in the city.

Building director means the director of the building department of the city or his designee.

Emergency response personnel means, but is not limited to, the police and fire departments and ambulance services.

Employee means a person who is employed by an alarm systems business and who plans, sells, installs, services, maintains, repairs, monitors or replaces alarm systems in the city. (See [section] 4.18.190.)

False alarm means an actual alarm signal transmitted in the absence of an alarm condition which results in emergency response personnel being dispatched to the location of the alarm.

Local or audible alarm means an alarm, which, when activated, emits a loud noise at or near the protected area without notifying an alarm monitoring station.

Manually activated alarm means an alarm system which is activated manually, and which transmits a signal to an alarm monitoring station indicating an emergency or a crime in progress.

Responder means a private patrol business, licensed in accordance with the provisions of NRS and the city, or the owner of the home, business, structure or facility experiencing an alarm condition.

User means a person, who owns, or is in control of the premises protected or intended to be protected by an alarm system.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
As the city's population has grown, more residential and commercial property owners are turning to privately monitored security alarm systems to provide additional protection for their properties. Commensurate with the growth in the number of private alarm systems installed within the City of Henderson there has been a corresponding increase in the number of false alarm reports received by the police department. In response to the proliferation of alarm systems and the city council's concern for the public's best interest from a safety standpoint as it relates to the increased incidents of false alarms, it is necessary that rules and regulations be adopted to control the licensing and operation of alarm systems businesses and the establishment of a process whereby the city can recoup the expenses incurred in responding to the ever increasing number of false alarms.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
All persons, except an alarm user as defined in this chapter, shall be licensed and subject to regulation, and the license may be suspended, limited, or revoked for violation of the provisions of this chapter, the laws of the State of Nevada, other ordinances of the city, or for any other cause deemed sufficient by the council in the exercise of its sole discretion. In conformity with the policy of this chapter, the following persons are declared not to be qualified to hold a license under the provisions of this chapter:

(1)

A person who has been convicted of a crime involving theft, fraud, dishonesty, receiving or possessing stolen property, any narcotics violation whatsoever or any sex offense;

(2)

A person whose license, whether issued under the provisions of this chapter, or those ordinances or statutes of any other agency lawfully engaged in the licensing or regulation of alarm systems businesses, has been revoked for cause;

(3)

A person who, at the time of renewal of any license issued under this chapter, would not be eligible for such license upon a first application;

(4)

A partnership, limited partnership or association, unless all of the members of such partnership, limited partnership or association are qualified to obtain a license;

(5)

A corporation, unless it is incorporated in the State of Nevada, or unless it is a foreign corporation which is qualified under Nevada law to transact business in Nevada;

(6)

A corporation, if an officer or director thereof would not be eligible to receive a license for any reason which would disqualify an individual applicant.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
It is unlawful for any person to conduct any alarm systems business as described in this chapter without first having obtained a license therefor.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
Whenever a person desires to conduct any alarm systems business in the city, such person shall make application in writing to the division to obtain a license therefor; and, such application shall contain the following:

(a)

The name and residence address of the applicant; and

(b)

The classification of the license sought, the business address for which the license is sought where the operation will be conducted; and

(c)

The names and residential addresses of all persons owning an interest in and managing the business, together with a statement as to the percentage of the business owned by each individual. Each license applicant shall designate on the application form the name of an agent residing within the county who is responsible for the conduct of the business and authorized to immediately answer to the council or its agents should inquiry or action be deemed necessary; and

(d)

A consent for police department and division investigation of the applicant's background, including, but not limited to, financial background, employment history, and criminal record. In all cases where the applicant for an alarm systems license, is a corporation, the names and residential addresses of the officers or directors of the corporation shall be listed on the application. In all such cases, the director or the chief of police shall determine who of the principal officers and directors of such corporation shall require background investigations.

(e)

All applicants for an alarm systems license shall state for each person interested in the business, his name, and place of residence, whether or not he is a legal resident of the United States, whether or not he has been convicted of a crime which would be considered a felony under the laws of the State of Nevada, or any misdemeanor crime, other than minor traffic offenses, and any other information the division may required.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
All applications shall contain such information as the council or its authorized officers by rule or regulation not inconsistent with law prescribe. Each licensee shall designate on the application form the agent residing within the county who is responsible for the conduct of the business and authorized to immediately answer to the council or its agents should inquiry or action be deemed necessary.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
All applicants for an alarm systems license shall state for each person interested in the business, his name and place of residence, whether or not he is a legal resident of the United States, whether or not he has been convicted of a crime which would be considered a felony under the laws of the State of Nevada, or any misdemeanor crime, other than minor traffic offenses, and any other information the division may require, all to be set forth in the application.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
No investigation shall be made of any applicant for an alarm systems license prior to the payment by the applicant, and receipt of such fee, by the division, and no license shall be issued until all appropriate fees are paid.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
Any person applying for an alarm systems license is required to deposit with the division an investigation fee as determined by the police department fees schedule for each person required to be licensed. (See chapter 4.03).

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
Even though an applicant is denied a license after investigation, no part of the investigation fees deposited shall be returned to the applicant.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
If any applicant withdraws his application prior to the beginning of an investigation, all fees deposited shall be returned to the applicant.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
In the case of a corporate licensee, any and all changes in the officers or directors of such corporation shall be reported to the division within 30 days of the appointment or election of such officers and directors. Such officers or directors shall be required to qualify for a license as required by this chapter.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
(a)

Upon receipt of the results of the background investigation from the police department, the director will approve or deny the application. If the application is denied, the applicant may appeal such denial to the council. (See section 4.04.210.)

(b)

The license fee for an alarm systems business shall be $65.00 semiannually, payable in advance, and shall be renewed semiannually.

(Ord. 1961, § 3, 1999; Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
section_name: Bond required, new business—Alternative of certificate of deposit, requirements based on actual false alarms of business—Exemptions.
citation: 4.18.140 - Bond required, new business—Alternative of certificate of deposit, requirements based on actual false alarms of business—Exemptions.
full_text:
The bond required by this chapter is conditioned upon the licensee to fully comply with the requirements of payment of all license fees, and fees for false alarms, due the city.

A.

No new license shall be issued to conduct any alarm systems business until the applicant files a surety bond with the division in the amount of $10,000.00, with surety from a company licensed to do business in the State of Nevada. The bond shall be taken in the name of the city, and legal action on the bond may be brought by the city to recover delinquent license fees and/or fees for false alarms.

B.

Every new alarm systems business shall maintain such surety bond in full force and effect during the first year of licensure under this chapter, and upon failure to do so, its license shall be suspended until such bond is renewed; and

C.

After one year of licensure, in lieu of the bond described in A above, the licensee may deposit with the division, a certificate of deposit in the amount of $3,500.00. The certificate of deposit shall be made payable to the licensee and the city jointly, shall be non-negotiable by the licensee without the signature of the city, but shall be negotiable by the city individually.

All alarm systems businesses which participated in the council-directed computerized alarm tracking system for a period of three months prior to the passage of this ordinance may submit a certificate of deposit in lieu of the bond requirement.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
section_name: Licensee responsible for the acts of employees.
citation: 4.18.150 - Licensee responsible for the acts of employees.
full_text:
Every licensee shall be responsible for the acts of his employees committed during the course and scope of employment. In any license suspension, limitation or revocation proceedings, the fact that the licensee did not have actual knowledge of the events complained of shall be no defense, and every licensee hereunder accepts his license subject to said condition.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
A.

Those licensees, responders and users not in conformity with the provisions of this chapter at the date of adoption of the ordinance codified in this chapter, shall have a period of 90 days from the effective date of the ordinance to conform to the requirements thereof.

B.

Any alarm systems business which is unable to comply with any debt due the city for false alarms as imposed by this chapter within the 90-day period, may apply for an additional 90-day extension. Such request shall be made in writing to the division prior to the end of the first 75-day period, shall be signed by the licensee, and shall include a detailed explanation of the reasons for requesting an extension.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
The council may deem that any activity on the part of the licensee or employees, or a person previously found suitable, which is contrary to the public health, safety, morals, good order, or general welfare of the residents of the city or which violates any ordinance or regulation of the city or the State of Nevada is grounds for disciplinary action which may result in a suspension, limitation or revocation of the alarm systems license. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, each of the following reasons are declared to be a basis for disciplinary action:

A.

Conviction of the licensee of any crime involving theft, fraud, dishonesty, receiving or possessing stolen property, any narcotics violation or any sex offense; or

B.

Conducting an alarm systems business in an unlawful manner or in a manner detrimental to the public health, safety or welfare; or

C.

Each licensee who violates any provision of title 4 of the Henderson Municipal Code; or

D.

Each licensee who knowingly fails to report or conceals from the council a full disclosure of the names of all persons having an interest in the ownership of, or receiving any remuneration whatsoever under a license in which he has an interest; or

E.

Each licensee who knowingly fails to report or conceals from proper authority any information which it is his duty to supply under any statute, ordinance or regulation of the state or the city; or

F.

Each licensee who, for conduct subsequent to the issuance of a license, becomes ineligible to hold an alarm systems license as set out in the statutes, ordinances and regulations of the state or city; or

G.

Each licensee who made a misrepresentation of a material fact in his application to obtain a license; or

H.

Each licensee whose alarm systems license in any place in the State of Nevada has been revoked for cause; or

I.

Each licensee who employs a person without a registration card as required by this chapter.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
section_name: Alarm systems business located out of local area—Requirement of a resident agent.
citation: 4.18.180 - Alarm systems business located out of local area—Requirement of a resident agent.
full_text:
Any alarm systems business not physically located in the County of Clark shall conform to the following provisions:

A.

The resident agent shall be a full-time employee, not a subcontractor, of the alarm systems business; and

B.

The resident shall reside within a 50-mile radius of the city. For purposes of this subsection, the point from which the 50-mile radius shall be measured, is from the city hall of the city; and

C.

The resident agent shall possess a master technician's card in accordance with NRS, or have two years of electronics schooling or work experience, and four years experience in the alarm systems business; and

D.

The resident agent shall physically sign the monthly false alarm billing statement received from the city.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
section_name: Application for electrical permit required—Permit not assignable or transferable.
citation: 4.18.200 - Application for electrical permit required—Permit not assignable or transferable.
full_text:
(a)

No person shall install, operate, maintain or engage another person to install, operate or maintain an alarm system at a particular location unless a building permit (electric) as required by city ordinance, or the Uniform Building Code, has been applied for and issued.

(b)

No permit issued under this section shall be assignable or transferable.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text: The building director is authorized to make inspections of alarm systems that have been installed within the city for the purpose of determining whether said systems are being maintained in conformity with the provisions of this chapter. The building director shall request the owner or lessee of the premises on which the alarm system is installed, or any other person who may lawfully give his consent, to admit the building director onto the premises for the purpose of making an inspection of the alarm system.

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
section_name: Sirens not to be audible outside premises.
citation: 4.18.220 - Sirens not to be audible outside premises.
full_text:
It is unlawful to install or maintain any alarm system which, upon activation, emits an audible sound, that could reasonably be confused with the siren emitted by an emergency vehicle. The audible warning system of an emergency vehicle is not a siren by this definition.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
section_name: Instructions as to the operation of the system—User responsibility for maintenance.
citation: 4.18.230 - Instructions as to the operation of the system—User responsibility for maintenance.
full_text:
(a)

It shall be the responsibility of all alarm systems users to see that all employees and persons regularly using the premises on which the alarm is installed be instructed in the proper operating procedures to avoid false alarm signals.

(b)

No alarm system business licensed under this chapter shall sell or refer to any interior alarm button, intended to be depressed manually, as a "panic alarm." Any button installed in an alarm system, intended to be depressed manually for the purpose of summoning emergency personnel, shall be referred to as a "manually activated alarm" and instructions shall be given that it is not to be used unless there is an actual emergency.

(c)

It shall be the responsibility of the alarm system user to cause the system to be maintained in reliable operating condition.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
section_name: Response alarms condition — False alarms — Exceptions.
citation: 4.18.240 - Response alarms condition — False alarms — Exceptions.
full_text:
(a)

When the alarms systems business, or responder, notifies emergency personnel of an actual alarm condition, it shall provide the following information:

(1)

The name of the party reporting the alarm condition; and

(2)

The time, address and phone number of the alarm condition, and the type of alarm; and

(3)

The precise location of the alarm (if there is more than one floor), the type of alarm; and

(4)

The name and description of the responder (uniformed, armed or not armed) at the location and a description of the vehicle driven by the responder, if known; and

(5)

The type of instrumentation, or verification, used to determine that an alarm condition exists, if any.

(b)

In the event that a false alarm condition exists, it shall be the responsibility of the alarm system user to comply with the requirements regarding the notification of responsible persons who will render all necessary service and assistance to restore the alarm to normal condition or to reset the alarm.

(c)

For purposes of this subsection, the alarm systems business, and/or user, may contract with a licensed security or private patrol business to perform the function of the responder. Such responder business shall be required to conform to the provisions of this chapter as if an actual licensee when engaged in the alarm responder business.

(d)

Alarm systems businesses that request police response to an alarm condition shall maintain a record of all emergency personnel calls stating the time, date, and location of the alarm, and if the alarm is not caused by an actual crime in progress, shall state the corrective action taken to prevent the reoccurrence of the false alarm. This record shall be maintained for a period of six months, and shall be made available for inspection by the police department or division at any time during normal business hours.

(e)

All alarm systems maintained by any licensed alarm systems business shall terminate in an office of a licensed alarm system business. The alarm systems business, having reason to believe there is an alarm condition, will immediately notify emergency personnel. For purposes of notifying the emergency personnel, the maximum equipment allowed shall be a telephone line to the emergency services personnel switchboard.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
section_name: Audible alarm system cutoff — Automatic dialing systems.
citation: 4.18.250 - Audible alarm system cutoff — Automatic dialing systems.
full_text:
(a)

Every alarm system which uses an audible alarm device to attract the attention of the public shall be equipped with an automatic 20 minute cutoff device, or shall be silenced manually by the user or his representative within 20 minutes after activation.

(b)

This section shall also apply to all alarm systems currently installed or being installed.

(c)

This section does not preempt section 4.18.230 which makes it unlawful for siren type alarms to be audible outside the premises wherein the alarm is installed.

(d)

Alarm devices which automatically dial telephone numbers must be monitored at an interim monitoring station, unless authorized by the director.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
The sensory mechanisms used in connection with alarm systems shall be adjusted to suppress false alarms so that the device will not be activated by impulses due to transient pressure changes in water pipes, short flashes of light, wind noises such as rattling or vibrating of doors and windows, vehicular noises adjacent to the installation or other forces unrelated to genuine alarms. This section shall also apply to all alarm systems currently installed or being installed.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
section_name: Fee for false alarms—Accounting, method of billing and collection.
citation: 4.18.270 - Fee for false alarms—Accounting, method of billing and collection.
full_text:
All false alarms shall be billed monthly to the alarm systems business, or, in the absence of an alarm systems business, the user, at a rate determined by council resolution.

(a)

The emergency services personnel shall maintain a monthly, computer-generated record of all alarms occurring in the city. Said record shall be available for review by an alarm systems business, or a user, by appointment, through the appropriate emergency services office; and

(b)

False alarms, which are attributed to an alarm systems business, shall be invoiced to said business monthly, and payment shall be made to the City within 30 days of the invoice date; and

(c)

False alarms, which are attributed to a user, shall be invoiced by notice of the total monthly charges due on the users monthly city utility bill;

(d)

False alarms occurring in multi-family dwelling units, not monitored by an alarm systems business, shall be invoiced through the multi-family dwelling city utility bill.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
(a)

Notice or billing from the city to any alarm system business or alarm user shall be deemed to have been given or rendered on the date such notice or billing is deposited in the United States mail, first class postage, prepaid, addressed to the alarm system business at its place of operation on file with the division or to the alarm user's residence address. A certificate of mailing signed by the person who mailed the notice shall be prima facie evidence of the fact that the notice was mailed.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
(a)

If an excessive number of false alarms occur at any alarm location, written notice shall be given by the police department to the alarm systems user responsible for the system to take corrective action within 14 calendar days to prevent future false alarms. An excessive number of false alarms shall be deemed to be:

(1)

More than three false alarms in any 30-day period; or

(2)

More than six false alarms in any 90-day period; or

(3)

More than eight false alarms in any 180-day period; or

(4)

More than 12 false alarms in any 360-day period.

(b)

If the corrective action is not accomplished and communicated in writing to the police department within 14 days by the alarm systems user, a duly authorized representative of the city may issue a misdemeanor citation to the alarm system user. Corrective action shall require written certification by the alarm systems user, that an inspection has been conducted and that the alarm system is safe and reliable.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
A.

Any alarm system user violating any of the terms and provisions of this chapter shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof shall be punished, not to exceed the maximum allowable fine under NRS, or by imprisonment not to exceed six months, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

B.

The minimum fine permissible under subsection A of this section shall be $250.00 plus court costs, but not to exceed the maximum allowable fine under NRS, or by imprisonment or both.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
section_name: Violation—Penalty—Alarm systems businesses—Licensed security and/or private patrol businesses.
citation: 4.18.310 - Violation—Penalty—Alarm systems businesses—Licensed security and/or private patrol businesses.
full_text:
Any person violating any of the terms and provisions of this chapter shall be deemed guilty of misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof shall be punished by a fine, not to exceed the maximum allowable fine under NRS, or by imprisonment in the city jail for a term not to exceed six months, or by both such fine and imprisonment; and shall subject the licensee to suspension, limitation or revocation of his license. Any person being adjudged guilty of a violation of this chapter, or any of the provisions or prohibitions thereof, may, in the discretion of the council, be denied a license thereafter.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

As used in the gaming regulations contained herein, the words and terms defined in this section have the meanings ascribed to them unless a different meaning clearly appears in the context. Any word or term not defined in this section which appears in the regulation shall have the definition ascribed by the Nevada Gaming Control Act and statutes ancillary thereto, and as defined by the regulations of the Nevada Gaming Commission unless a different meaning clearly appears in the context.

Condition means the action of the council relating to the issuance of a license or resulting from a disciplinary hearing whereby terms are imposed upon the licensee with which it must comply in order to avoid a license revocation or suspension.

Control means the direct or indirect possession of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of an entity whether through the ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise.

Game or gambling game shall have the same meaning as contained in NRS 463.0152.

Gaming device shall have the same meaning as contained in NRS 463.0155 as may be amended or renumbered.

Limited gaming means an establishment which maintains a minimum of 75 to a maximum of 199 slot machines or gaming devices licensed and available for play, and which may have a maximum of nine live games. This category of gaming is only available for issue to applicants for a change of ownership of an existing limited gaming location.

Live game means any game or gambling game as defined in NRS 463.0152, as may be amended or renumbered, save [and] except for slot machines.

Nonrestricted gaming shall have the same meaning as "nonrestricted license" and "nonrestricted operation" as contained in NRS 463.0177 as may be amended or renumbered. This license is limited to a resort hotel or other specific nonconforming establishments as defined in section 4.32.350.

Premises means a tract of land, on which a gaming establishment is located and all buildings, improvements, parking lots, and personal property located thereon, which are connected and operated in such an integral manner as to form a part of the same operation or complex as the gaming establishment, whether or not under separate ownership or lease.

Quarter or calendar quarter means a period of three consecutive months commencing on the first day of January, April, July, or October, in any year.

Race book shall have the same meaning as contained in NRS 463.01855, as may be amended or renumbered.

Resort hotel means a building or group of buildings kept, used, maintained, advertised, and held out to the public to be a hotel where sleeping accommodations are offered to transient guests, which has a minimum of 200 rooms used for sleeping accommodations, and which has a minimum of the following amenities, all of which are directly connected to the building or group of buildings upon the premises:

1.

One main bar with more than 30 permanent seats wherein alcoholic liquors are dispensed by the drink to customers at such bar; and

2.

One service bar wherein alcoholic liquors are prepared for service only at tables and not direct to customers at such bar; and

3.

Entertainment which includes at least one of the following:

a.

One facility with at least 25 seats wherein live entertainment is provided by at least one professional entertainer (musician or variety artist) on a regularly scheduled basis; or

b.

One facility with at least 300 seats wherein live entertainment is provided by at least one professional entertainer (musician or variety artists) on a semi-regular basis (at least six times per year).

4.

One restaurant with permanent seating capacity for more than 60 patrons that is open to the public 24 hours a day, seven days per week; and

5.

Room service to all rooms, including, without limitation, service of meals; and

6.

A recreational facility which includes at least one of the following:

a.

Four regulation tennis courts with locker rooms and attendant facilities;

b.

One swimming pool that is swimmable and adequate in relationship to the size of the resort hotel as approved by the city council;

c.

One regular golf course consisting of at least nine holes comprising at least 50 acres;

d.

One gymnasium with dimensions of at least 40 feet in width, 60 feet in length, and 20 feet in height and equipped with exercise equipment; or

e.

Any other type of recreational facility as approved by the city council.

7.

A gaming area within the building or group of buildings.

When determining whether a particular applicant complies with the resort hotel definition, the city council may consider:

1.

The physical layout of buildings and facilities; and

2.

The unity of title and ownership of the buildings or group of buildings; and

3.

The operation and management relationship of gaming to hotel administration; and

4.

The proximity of the proposed resort hotel to residential development.

Restrict, in regard to council action or for violation of law, means to limit the number and/or types of games, and/or slot machines or gaming devices, which may be operated, the hours and days games may be operated, and any other limitation or confinement placed upon a licensee's operation.

Restricted gaming shall have the same meaning as "restricted license" and "restricted operation" as contained in NRS 463.0189 as may be amended or renumbered.

Slot machine shall have the same meaning as contained in NRS 463.0191 as may be amended or renumbered.

Slot route operator or slot operator shall have the same meaning as contained in NRS 463.018 as may be amended or renumbered.

Sports pool shall have the same meaning as contained in NRS 463.0193 as may be amended or renumbered.

(Ord. No. 3104, § 1, 12-17-2013)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
A.

It is found and declared that the public health, safety, morals and welfare of the inhabitants of the city require the regulation and control of all persons engaged in, associated with, or in control of the profits of the business of gaming. All such persons, as hereafter defined in this chapter, shall be licensed and controlled so as to protect the public health, safety, morals, good order and general welfare of the inhabitants of the city and to assist the gaming industry to foster its stability and growth. It is further found and declared that the right to obtain such license is a privilege and that the operation of such gaming facility, when authorized by such license, is a privileged business subject to regulations, and that the license may be suspended, limited, or revoked for cause. The burden of proving qualification to receive or retain any license or finding of suitability is on the applicant.

B.

The council believes that the gaming industry is vitally important to the economy of the city and the general inhabitants thereof and that the continued growth and success of the gaming industry is dependent upon public confidence and trust that licensed gaming is conducted honestly and competitively and that the gaming industry is free from criminal and corruptive elements.

C.

These regulations define division procedure and regulate gaming operations within the jurisdiction of the council, but do not in any degree limit the general power of the council to grant or deny applications for licenses and to impose conditions, limitations and restrictions upon a license for cause after hearing, or to immediately suspend or limit a license in an emergency. These regulations are to be liberally interpreted so as to grant the council final discretion in all licensing matters.

(Ord. No. 4074, § 1, 4-15-2025; Ord. No. 3104, § 1, 12-17-2013)

title: Title 4 - BUSINESS REGULATIONS AND LICENSES
full_text:
