title: Title 5 - HEALTH AND SANITATION
full_text:
It shall be the duty of any person growing a tree, plant or shrub on his property to keep such tree, plant or shrub from encroaching upon or obstructing the abutting or adjacent streets, sidewalks and public parks, buildings and grounds by:

A.

Trimming or removing his tree, plant or shrub so as not to constitute, in the opinion of the building director or his code enforcement officer, a hazard to any member of the public or render unsafe in any manner whatsoever any public place and/or right-of-way;

B.

Treating or removing any tree, plant or shrub so diseased or insect-ridden as to constitute a hazard to the public or to any tree, plant or shrub in public places.

(Ord. 1234 (part), 1991)

title: Title 5 - HEALTH AND SANITATION
section_name: Authority to order the treatment, trimming or removal of trees, plants and shrubs.
citation: 5.28.020 - Authority to order the treatment, trimming or removal of trees, plants and shrubs.
full_text:
The building director or his code enforcement officer shall have the authority to order the treatment, trimming or removal of any tree, plant or shrub upon private property when he shall find such action necessary to public safety and/or health or to prevent the spread of disease or insects to public trees, plants or shrubs or any public place.

(Ord. 1234 (part), 1991)

title: Title 5 - HEALTH AND SANITATION
section_name: Procedure upon order to treat, trim or remove.
citation: 5.28.030 - Procedure upon order to treat, trim or remove.
full_text:
When the building director or his code enforcement officer shall find it warranted to order the treatment, trimming or removal of any tree, plant or shrub, as authorized in section 5.28.020, he shall serve a written order to correct the dangerous or unsafe condition upon the owner, lessee or occupant of the private property by one of the following methods of service:

A.

By making personal delivery of the order to the owner, lessee or occupant of the private property where the dangerous or unsafe condition exists or originates;

B.

By leaving the order with some person of suitable age and discretion upon the premises;

C.

By affixing a copy of the order to the door at the premises in violation;

D.

By mailing a copy of the order to the last known address of the owner of the premises, by certified mail, return receipt requested;

E.

Only if the above four methods of service are impractical, by publishing a copy of the order in a local newspaper once a week, for three consecutive weeks.

(Ord. 1234 (part), 1991)

title: Title 5 - HEALTH AND SANITATION
full_text:
When a person to whom an order is directed shall fail to comply within five days of service of the order, the building director may remedy the condition or contract with others for such purpose and charge the cost thereof to the person to whom the order is directed. The person remedying a condition hereunder shall be authorized to enter the premises for that purpose.

(Ord. 1234 (part), 1991)

title: Title 5 - HEALTH AND SANITATION
full_text:
When the city or other person with whom the city has contracted has effected the treatment, trimming or removal of any tree, plant or shrub pursuant to this chapter, the cost thereof, plus accrued interest at the rate of ten percent per annum from the date of the completion of the work shall be charged to the owner of the private property. Such charge shall constitute a lien upon the real property of such owner until such charge is paid, as well as constitute a debt of the record owner of the property and of the person occupying such premises to the city. The city may bring a civil action in any court of competent jurisdiction to recover such charge, or follow the lien procedures set forth in section 15.12.060(N)(3)(e).

(Ord. No. 3082, § 1, 11-5-2013; Ord. 1234 (part), 1991)

Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
The purpose of these rules is to establish methods, practices and procedures to ensure fair and effective human resources administration. The terms and conditions of employment for covered positions shall be governed by the civil service rules. As provided by the Henderson City Charter, the civil service rules set forth provisions that concern:

A.

Examination of potential employees;

B.

Procedures for recruitment and placement;

C.

Procedures for reductions in force;

D.

Procedures for disciplinary actions against, and the discharge of, employees; and

E.

Procedures for hearing employee appeals and taking final action.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
section_name: Persons covered under the civil service rules.
citation: 6.01.020 - Persons covered under the civil service rules.
full_text:
A.

Pursuant to the Henderson City Charter, the civil service rules are applicable to and govern the employment of certain non-represented full-time employees of the city who have successfully completed their probationary period. Pursuant to Section 24 and 26 of Senate Bill No. 440, a person holding any of the positions below, before, on or after October 1, 2013, is not covered by the civil service rules:

1.

Executive officers;

2.

Senior department directors;

3.

Department directors;

4.

Division heads (including assistant directors);

5.

Assistant city attorneys;

6.

Any other attorney employed by the office of the city attorney;

7.

Assistants to the city manager;

8.

The municipal court administrator;

9.

Any elected officer;

10.

Any employee that reports directly to an elected officer;

11.

Any probationary employee;

12.

Any employee covered under a collective bargaining agreement, unless otherwise stated in the collective bargaining agreements;

13.

Any seasonal or temporary employee;

14.

Any part-time employee;

15.

Volunteers (including but not limited to, reserve fire officers, reserve police, reserve marshals, who receive no regular salary from the city); and/or

16.

Independent contractors.

B.

Employees covered under the civil service rules have classified positions. The employees identified in subsection A. are considered to hold unclassified positions.

C.

The rules and regulations adopted in this title shall be made available to each employee holding a classified position. The civil service rules are maintained with the human resources department and the city clerk's office.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

full_text:
A.

The city manager, (or designee) and director of human resources (or designee) shall review the civil service rules on an annual basis. Proposed amendments shall be submitted to the civil service board who will then review and recommend the proposed amendments to the Henderson city council.

B.

The civil service rules are codified in the Henderson Municipal Code ("HMC"), title 6. The Henderson city council must adopt the civil service rules and any amendments thereto. If not otherwise specified, the civil service rules and amendments thereto, are effective after they are approved by the Henderson city council and published in accordance with the Henderson City Charter.

C.

The civil service rules are subject to change at any time pursuant to this section. These rules do not constitute a contract between employees in a classified position and the city.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

Employees covered under the civil service rules are required to follow all City of Henderson policies, procedures and directives, including the Henderson City Charter and all applicable sections of the HMC, unless a policy, procedure, or directive specifically excludes classified positions. If there is an inconsistency between the civil service rules and any of the City of Henderson policies, procedures and/or directives, then the civil service rules shall prevail.

B.

A department may establish rules regarding employee conduct and performance to promote the efficient and orderly operation of the department, as long as such rules are not inconsistent with the City of Henderson policies, procedures and directives, the HMC, the Henderson City Charter, or the civil service rules.

1.

Department rules and amendments related to employment practices must be approved by the director of human resources (or designee).

2.

Department rules shall be made available to the employees in the affected department.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
The City of Henderson is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions on the basis of merit. In accordance with applicable law, the city prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, age, national origin or ancestry, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, status as HIV positive, genetic information, gender identity and expression, or any other consideration protected by federal, state or local laws. All such discrimination is prohibited. The city's commitment to equal opportunity employment applies to all persons involved in the operations of the city and prohibits discrimination by any employee or agent of the city. For additional information, please refer to the City of Henderson's policies regarding its commitment to equal employment opportunities.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
To comply with applicable laws ensuring equal employment opportunities to qualified individuals with disabilities, the city will make reasonable accommodations for the known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified individual with a disability who is an applicant or an employee, unless undue hardship or a direct threat would occur as a result.

Any applicant or employee who requires an accommodation in order to perform the essential functions of the job they hold or desire to hold should contact human resources and request such an accommodation in accordance with the city's policies and procedures. Once an accommodation has been requested, the city will investigate these barriers or limitations and then identify what possible accommodations, if any, will help to eliminate the barrier(s) or limitation(s). If the requested accommodation is reasonable and will not impose an undue hardship or a direct threat, the city will make the accommodation in accordance with applicable law. The city may propose an alternative to the requested accommodation or substitute one reasonable accommodation for another, but the city retains the ultimate discretion to choose between reasonable accommodations.

The accommodation process is interactive, and it may take multiple conversations between the city and the requesting individual before an accommodation is reached. Employees are expected to fully cooperate in the accommodation process, including making every effort to provide management with current medical information. Employees who do not meaningfully cooperate in the accommodation process waive the right to accommodation. For additional information, please refer to the City of Henderson's policies and procedures that relate to accommodation requests.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
The city maintains a policy strictly prohibiting sexual harassment and harassment because of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, age, national origin or ancestry, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, status as HIV positive, genetic information, gender identity and expression, or any other consideration protected by federal, state or local laws. This policy applies to all persons involved in the operations of the city and prohibits such harassment by any employee or agent of the city, including supervisors and co-workers. The city's policies and procedures also prohibit harassment by visitors, clients, vendors or other service providers at our facilities. Prohibited harassment will not be tolerated. The city is committed to taking all reasonable steps to prevent such harassment from occurring. For additional information, please refer to the City of Henderson's policies on maintaining a harassment free workplace.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
Applicable law and the City of Henderson's policies and procedures prohibit retaliation against any employee for opposing, reporting or threatening to report prohibited discrimination or harassment, or for participating in any manner in an investigation, proceeding or hearing regarding prohibited discrimination or harassment. The city will not retaliate against employees who complain of prohibited discrimination or harassment and will not permit such retaliation by its employees. Complaints of prohibited retaliation should immediately be reported to the employee's supervisor and/or human resources in accordance with the City of Henderson's policies and procedures.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
section_name: Civil service board selection and composition.
citation: 6.02.010 - Civil service board selection and composition.
full_text:
A.

The civil service board shall be composed of five persons appointed by a majority vote of the city council.

B.

Members of the civil service board shall be appointed by vote of the City Council at a public meeting to serve for staggered terms lasting up to three years and may serve no more than three terms.

C.

The civil service board shall meet annually (or additionally, as needed), and by majority vote, select a chairperson and vice-chairperson for that calendar year or until the first meeting of the Board in the following year.

D.

A member of the civil service board may be removed immediately for good cause prior to the expiration of the term by a majority vote of the city council. Removal for good cause means that the basis for removal is not for any arbitrary, capricious, or illegal reason and is based on facts (1) supported by substantial evidence, and (2) reasonably believed to be true. City Council has the sole discretion to determine if good cause exists.

E.

A member of the civil service board shall automatically be removed if they miss more than two meetings in one calendar year period. A member may be removed by a majority vote of the city council if they fail to respond to communications related to their responsibilities on the civil service board.

F.

A member of the civil service board may resign from their position by submitting a written resignation letter to the director of human resources. The civil service board member should provide at least two weeks' notice to the director of human resources in order to allow for the city council to find a replacement.

G.

The director of human resources (or designee) will serve as secretary to the civil service board. The secretary of the board (or designee) shall have the authority to set the time and place of the annual regular meeting, and shall provide notice of such meeting in accordance with Nevada's Open Meeting Laws (set forth in Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 241). The secretary does not have any voting authority.

H.

Special meetings may be convened at the call of the chairperson, the secretary of the board, or by any two members of the civil service board after reasonable public notice and notice to the remaining members of the civil service board (in compliance with Nevada's Open Meeting Laws set forth in Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 241).

I.

The civil service board shall have the authority to hear appeals in the method provided by these rules from an employee who has requested an appeal that is receivable under these rules.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

The chairperson, or in the absence of the chairperson, the vice-chairperson, shall preside at all meetings of the civil service board. If neither the chairperson nor the vice-chairperson is present, the secretary shall preside over the meeting.

B.

No business may be transacted and no action may be taken unless a quorum is present. A quorum shall consist of a minimum of three members.

C.

Notice of all meetings shall be given in accordance with Nevada's Open Meeting Laws (set forth in Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 241).

(Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
section_name: Recusal of a civil service board member.
citation: 6.02.030 - Recusal of a civil service board member.
full_text:
A.

Civil service board members are responsible for complying with the HMC chapter 2.40, including the provisions regarding disclosing conflicts of interest and recusing themselves where appropriate.

B.

In compliance with HMC section 2.40.060, Civil service board members, even if they do not intend to recuse themselves, shall, prior to the beginning of the hearing, disclose on the record any facts that could reasonably create the appearance that their impartiality could be affected.

C.

Pursuant to HMC section 2.40.060, a civil service board member who has a conflict of interest in regard to a particular matter that would materially affect the independence of judgment of a reasonable person in their situation shall recuse themselves and abstain from voting on the matter.

D.

The employee or the city, prior to the beginning of a hearing, may ask for the disqualification of any civil service board member(s). The request may be based on the disclosures of a civil service board member, if any, or other facts relating to the particular civil service board member. If the employee or the city is relying on evidence from a third party, the evidence shall be presented in an affidavit.

E.

Before a civil service board member may be disqualified, upon the request of the employee or the city, the board must vote and approve of the disqualification. A member may be disqualified from the hearing by at least two votes from the civil service board members who have not been challenged.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

All classified positions are assigned an appropriate job description. The human resources department and department directors are responsible for the content of each job description.

B.

At a minimum, each job description shall include a reference to the following: (1) the job title; (2) essential functions; (3) minimum qualifications including physical requirements, education, training, experience, licenses, certifications, and/or special requirements; and (4) knowledge, skills and abilities. Job descriptions shall be deemed a summary of the essential work required but will not necessarily include all duties to be performed in a particular position.

C.

All new and revised job descriptions are effective upon the approval of the director of human resources (or designee).

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

The director of human resources shall recommend a compensation plan to the city manager. The city reserves the right to alter the compensation plan in accordance with the City Charter and the HMC, and any other relevant laws, policies and procedures.

B.

Compensation modifications that differ from the approved budget are subject to available funding.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
section_name: Annual pay adjustment and general increase compensation.
citation: 6.03.030 - Annual pay adjustment and general increase compensation.
full_text:
A.

Employees who have not been subject to a performance improvement plan or a return-to-work/last chance agreement in the previous 12 months and/or issued disciplinary action consisting of a suspension, may be eligible for an annual pay adjustment and general increase, provided said compensation is approved by the city and funded in the city's annual budget.

B.

If approved by the city, annual pay adjustment and general increase compensation is still subject to funding availability and is in no way guaranteed. Annual pay adjustment and general increase compensation may be paid in the form of a salary increase or as a one-time lump sum payment or both.

C.

Salary assignments, adjustments, and/or lump-sum bonus payments are not subject to appeal through these rules.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Editor's note— Ord. No. 4142, § 1, adopted January 6, 2026, changed the title of section 6.03.030 from "Pay-for-performance" to "Annual pay adjustment and general increase compensation." The historical notation has been preserved for reference purposes.

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

Vacancies may be filled from an existing eligibility list. If there is no eligibility list or the list is expired, the vacancy may be posted to create an eligibility list.

B.

The director of human resources (or designee) may elect to post internally/departmentally, city-wide, or as permitted in subsection 6.04.070(B) or externally, based upon the business needs of the city. The vacancy shall be posted for a minimum of seven calendar days or limited by a predetermined number of applications. Application materials must be completed in their entirety and submitted by the posted closing date and time.

C.

The posted vacancy shall specify the title and salary range of the vacant position, a brief summary of the position's essential duties, the minimum qualifications and the final date upon which employment applications shall be accepted, unless the posting is open and continuous.

D.

Probationary employees shall be eligible to apply for vacancies for which they are qualified. However, a new probationary period will apply if selected to fill the vacancy.

E.

The director of human resources (or designee) may choose to consider applicants who have applied to job postings for classifications within the same job series or job family (as determined by human resources), or for classifications in which the qualifications are sufficiently similar to conclude that the applicant on the eligibility list are likely to be competent for the vacancy in question. These classifications must be within the same or lower pay level as the posted position. The candidate must meet the minimum qualifications of that classification and may be required to pass any applicable assessments. Eligibility for consideration extends up to one year from the date of application or the date the eligibility list expires (whichever is later).

F.

Upon approval, a temporary and part-time employee who has worked at least 988 continuous hours (with no separation of employment) in that classification, meets the minimum qualifications of the position, and was hired through a competitive process into that temporary or part-time classification may have their position converted to a full-time position or may be placed into a vacant full-time position in the same classification, without the requirement to post the position. These transactions require approval from the director of human resources (or designee). If the change affects the staff complement (i.e., position conversions), additional approvals may be required.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Note— Former section 6.04.030.

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

For every posted vacancy, each candidate must complete the employment application materials and may be required to provide evidence of education, training, relevant experience or other requirements and certifications for the relevant classification.

B.

The city may reject application materials for any of the reasons below, including, but not limited to:

1.

The candidate does not have a legal right to work in the United States;

2.

The application materials are incomplete;

3.

The application materials are not submitted by the job posting deadline;

4.

The application materials do not demonstrate that the candidate meets minimum qualifications;

5.

The candidate was previously terminated for-cause (the city may consider the circumstances surrounding the for-cause termination and the time that has passed before making a hiring decision); and

6.

The candidate previously applied and was denied the position because they failed the background review process (the city shall consider the circumstances pertaining to the background failure, the time that has passed, and city policy before making a hiring decision).

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Note— Former section 6.04.010.

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
section_name: Application materials review and assessment process.
citation: 6.04.030 - Application materials review and assessment process.
full_text:
A.

Application materials will be reviewed for completeness, timeliness, and to determine if the candidate meets the minimum qualifications for the classification for which they applied.

B.

Assessment processes will be conducted and administered at the discretion of the city. The city reserves the right to modify the selection and assessment process in accordance with accepted legal, ethical and professional standards.

C.

The purpose of the assessment process is to evaluate candidates in order to identify those who are best qualified to continue in the recruitment process. Candidates will be evaluated on the information supplied in their application materials and may be given any combination of written, oral, physical agility or performance skills assessments in accordance with applicable federal and state laws and standards. Only the best-qualified candidates will be invited to move forward.

D.

The human resources department shall have full responsibility for the design, development, and administration of the assessment process to include contracting with a third party as required by statute or normal course of business.

E.

Candidates with disabilities who require accommodation in the assessment process shall contact the human resources department to request assistance prior to the closing date of the recruitment. Requests may be submitted in writing, by phone, or through another accessible method.

F.

Applicants may be disqualified if:

1.

The applicant fails to be on time for a scheduled assessment or complete an assessment by an established deadline. Exceptions may be made for emergency situations as determined by the human resources department;

2.

The applicant fails to follow instructions;

3.

The applicant has made a false statement or omission of any material fact, or attempted to or practiced any deception, misrepresentation or fraud in the application, assessment, and/or background process; and/or

4.

The candidate exhibited dishonesty, unacceptable and/or unprofessional behavior at any time during any part of the application, assessment, and/or background process as outlined in city policy.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Editor's note— Ord. No. 4142, § 1, adopted January 6, 2026, changed the title of section 6.04.030 from "Application review and assessment process" to "Application materials review and assessment process." The historical notation has been preserved for reference purposes.

Note— Former section 6.04.020.

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

Eligibility lists may be created through an application materials review and/or an assessment process.

B.

Candidates who pass either process shall be placed on an eligibility list, which may be ranked or unranked. Candidates who have successfully completed a scored assessment process shall be ranked in descending order based upon their overall performance. A hiring authority may elect to interview any candidate on the eligibility list(s).

C.

Eligibility lists shall be certified by the director of human resources (or designee). The director of human resources (or designee) may abolish an eligibility list for legitimate business purposes, such as but not limited to: an insufficient number of qualified candidates, and/or the job description, salary, and/or assessment for the position has significantly changed since the position was posted.

D.

The city may elect to consider candidates from an eligibility list for a period of 12 months from the date they were placed on the list.

E.

Eligibility lists may be extended upon approval of the director of human resources (or designee).

F.

Any person may be removed from an eligibility list for reasons listed below, or under extenuating circumstances as determined by the director of human resources:

1.

At the candidate's request;

2.

Separation from the city;

3.

Failure to respond to inquiries or notices from the city;

4.

Failing the background review process;

5.

If an offer has been rescinded;

6.

Falsification of their application materials; and/or

7.

If the city is aware of any factual information that indicates a person is unable or incapable of performing the functions of the job for which the person is applying (e.g., not attaining a certification as required by the minimum qualifications for the position).

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Editor's note— Ord. No. 4018, § 1, adopted April 2, 2024, changed the title of section 6.04.040 from "Certification of eligibility list" to "Eligibility lists." The historical notation has been preserved for reference purposes.

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
section_name: Selection, offers, and appointment of employment.
citation: 6.04.050 - Selection, offers, and appointment of employment.
full_text:
A.

Employment with the city is at the sole discretion of the city.

B.

Employment offers, whether to an internal or external candidate, shall be contingent upon the successful and timely completion of a background review process, which, depending on the position may include, but is not limited to, completion of employer forms and documents, a criminal background check, DMV records review, education and experience verifications, reference checks, credit check, drug screening, and physical and/or psychological examination.

C.

Candidates who fail to respond to the city's offer of employment within three business days shall be deemed to have declined the offer of employment; at which time it may be rescinded.

D.

Any person whose job offer has been rescinded by the city per this section shall be removed from an eligibility list, unless the candidate presents an explanation to the director of human resources (or designee) deemed to be satisfactory.

E.

Any person who declines a formal offer of employment per this section may request to remain on the eligibility list.

F.

A conditional offer may be rescinded if a candidate fails to fully cooperate with or fails any part of the background review process.

G.

If an individual who was previously employed with the city has an interest in being rehired to a previously held position, similar position of equal or lower pay, or lower-level position within the same job series, they may submit a request in writing to the director of human resources (or designee) within one year of their date of separation from the city. Rehires may be considered if there is a current vacancy, and if approved by the department director and the director of human resources. Rehired employees must meet the minimum qualifications of the position and may be required to take assessments. Rehires may be required to submit to background screenings prior to reemployment and a probationary/qualifying period may be required and/or adjusted based on prior time in service.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Editor's note— Ord. No. 4142, § 1, adopted January 6, 2026, changed the title of section 6.04.050 from "Selection and appointment of employment" to "Selection, offers, and appointment of employment." The historical notation has been preserved for reference purposes.

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
section_name: External candidates subject to a probationary period.
citation: 6.04.060 - External candidates subject to a probationary period.
full_text:
A.

Upon initial hire or rehire, an employee will be subject to a six-month probationary period. Probationary periods may be extended up to a period of six additional months upon the recommendation of a department director and approval of the director of human resources (or designee). If an employee is on any type of leave during their probationary period (exceeding four workdays) or is temporarily assigned to a light-duty position (exceeding four workdays, whether consecutive or inconsecutive), the city may also extend the probationary period.

B.

During the probationary period, a department director may recommend termination. The director of human resources (or designee) shall have the authority to approve or deny all recommended terminations. An employee who is terminated during the probationary period does not have appeal rights under these civil service rules.

C.

If an employee is transferred to or selected for a different city position while serving a probationary period, then the employee must start a new probationary period (the full six months, subject to extension) for the new position. The employee's original date of hire will remain their city seniority date.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
section_name: Internal classification changes, promotions and the qualifying period.
citation: 6.04.070 - Internal classification changes, promotions and the qualifying period.
full_text:
A.

Insofar as practicable and consistent with the best interest of the city, vacancies in a classified position may be filled by internal candidates from within the city.

B.

The city manager, in conjunction with the director of human resources, may authorize alternative internal recruitment and/or selection processes (e.g., assigning or appointing employees to a classified position, for which they are qualified) to facilitate modifications to the organizational structure, to enhance operational efficiencies, or to address any other legitimate operational concerns.

C.

With approval from the director of human resources (or designee), the city may elect to establish and utilize a transfer list to fill vacancies.

1.

Full-time non-probationary employees who are interested in transferring to the same classification in a different department who meet the requirements of the new position may elect to place themselves on the transfer list.

2.

Employees who are no longer eligible for transfer will be removed from the eligibility list.

D.

Employees who meet the minimum qualifications and want to compete in the recruitment process must submit completed application materials within the established timeframe.

E.

The application materials review and/or assessment process set forth in section 6.04.030 shall be used to determine which employees are eligible for selection, unless the vacancy is filled as a result of an alternative internal selection process as permitted by subsection 6.04.010(E), 6.04.010(F), or 6.04.070(B).

F.

Upon promotion, voluntary or involuntary demotion or transfer, employees will serve a six-month qualifying period. The qualifying period may be extended for up to six additional months upon the recommendation of the department director and approval of the director of human resources (or designee). If an employee is on any type of leave during their qualifying period (exceeding four workdays, whether consecutive or inconsecutive) or is temporarily assigned to a light-duty position (exceeding four workdays, whether consecutive or inconsecutive), the city may extend the qualifying period.

G.

An employee who has been promoted, voluntarily or involuntarily demoted, or laterally transferred shall be subject to the applicable performance standards of the new position. Failure to meet performance standards during the qualifying period may result in disciplinary action, up to and including suspension, a return to their former classification (if such a position is available), a demotion or transfer, or termination.

H.

An employee who is suspended or terminated for failure to meet performance standards during the qualifying period shall have the appeal rights afforded by these Rules and set forth in chapter 6.08. However, an employee who is offered the opportunity to return to their former classification or a similar classification (i.e., demoted), as a result of being issued disciplinary action for failure to meet the performance standards during a qualifying period, does not have any appeal rights under these rules.

I.

An employee who transfers from a classified position to an unclassified position or to a position covered under a collective bargaining agreement does not retain any rights or privileges under the civil service rules.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Editor's note— Ord. No. 4018, § 1, adopted April 2, 2024, changed the title of section 6.04.070 from "Internal transfers, promotions and the qualifying period" to "Internal classification changes, promotions and the qualifying period." The historical notation has been preserved for reference purposes.

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
section_name: Recruitment concerns/complaints regarding violations of this chapter.
citation: 6.04.080 - Recruitment concerns/complaints regarding violations of this chapter.
full_text:
A.

If a candidate covered under the civil service rules believes that the city violated chapter 6.04 of these rules, they may report such violations to the director of human resources, in writing, within seven calendar days from the date the candidate is notified of the hiring decision. The candidate's complaint must specifically identify the civil service rule allegedly violated and explain the reason why the candidate believes the rule was violated. Upon timely receipt of the complaint to the director of human resources, the director of human resources (or designee) will investigate the complaint. A decision by the director of human resources (or designee) shall be made within 14 calendar days of receipt of the complaint. If the investigation requires additional time, the candidate must be notified within 14 calendar days of receipt of the complaint that the complaint has been received but that the investigation will require additional time to conduct.

B.

If a candidate is submitting a complaint regarding the selection for a position within the human resources department, the complaint may be submitted directly to the city manager (or designee). The procedures for submitting a complaint to the city manager (or designee) are the same as for submitting a complaint directly to the director of human resources.

C.

The decision of the director of human resources (or designee) or the city manager (or designee) shall be final.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

An employee shall have abandoned their job if the employee fails to directly notify their supervisor of an absence from work for three consecutive workdays. Job abandonment shall also occur when an employee fails to return to work for three consecutive workdays after the employee's approved leave has expired without directly notifying their supervisor of the continuing absences and without satisfactory explanation.

B.

Before the city makes a determination that the employee has abandoned their job, the city shall attempt to contact the employee on two separate days using either the employee's last known home telephone number, cell phone number or email address provided to the city by the employee. If the attempts to reach the employee are unsuccessful, the city can conclude that the employee has abandoned their job, and the employee shall be immediately terminated.

C.

Employees who are terminated for job abandonment do not have appeal rights under these rules.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

An employee's notice of resignation or retirement shall be in writing and shall be submitted to their supervisor and/or department director. The notice shall indicate the effective date of resignation or retirement. The notice should be submitted at least two weeks prior to the effective date of the resignation or retirement.

B.

The notice of resignation or retirement shall be deemed accepted by the city upon receipt by the employee's supervisor and/or department director. The supervisor and/or department director will forward an employee's notice of resignation or retirement to the human resources department. Once a notice is received by the employee's supervisor and/or department director, the notice may not be withdrawn without the written approval of the director of human resources or designee.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

A department director may make recommendations to the city manager regarding a reduction-in-force if the department director believes layoffs are necessary by reason of shortage of work or funds, the elimination of a position, organizational changes, or for any other legitimate business or operational purposes.

B.

The city manager must approve all reductions-in-force.

C.

The city council must approve a reduction-in-force involving layoffs of five or more non-vacant positions.

D.

After a reduction-in-force has been approved by the city manager, the city manager (or designee) must inform the director of human resources as to the number of employees to be laid-off within each of the affected departments and classifications, and identify the reason (e.g., shortage of work, lack of funds, position elimination, organizational changes or any other legitimate business reason) for the lay-offs. Once this information is provided to the director of human resources, the human resources department shall administer the reduction-in-force according to city seniority within the following limitations:

1.

All probationary employees in the affected classification(s) shall be laid-off before employees covered under the civil service rules may be impacted by the reduction-in-force. Probationary employees shall not have displacement rights under these civil service rules.

2.

Once all probationary employees have been laid-off in the impacted classification(s) and department(s), then employees shall be selected for inclusion in the reduction-in-force in the inverse order of their city seniority within the affected classification(s) and department(s), with the last employee hired being the first selected for the reduction-in-force. An employee loses their city seniority status for the purposes of a reduction-in-force if they have received active discipline (as defined in HMC 6.07.050) in the form of a demotion, suspension, performance improvement plan and/or return-to-work/last chance agreement.

3.

Employees, other than employees serving their probationary period, selected for inclusion in the reduction-in-force shall have displacement rights.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A non-probationary employee selected for inclusion in a reduction-in-force is considered a displaced employee and shall have displacement rights. The displacement procedure shall be administered as follows:

A.

A displaced employee may displace an employee with the least city seniority within the same classification. Under no circumstances is a displaced employee entitled to displace an employee with greater city seniority than the displaced employee.

B.

If the displaced employee's classification does not exist outside of their department, or if the displaced employee does not have more seniority than a person in that classification in a different department, then the displaced employee may displace the least senior employee holding the same previously held classification that the displaced employee held within the prior ten years, as long as the displaced employee is still qualified to perform the previously held classification and the position is covered under the Civil Service Rules. If the displaced employee has held multiple previously held classifications during the prior ten years, they will displace the employee with the least city seniority status (as long as the displaced employee is still qualified to perform the previously held classification), in order of the most recently held job covered under the Civil Service Rules.

C.

A non-probationary employee holding a classified position who is displaced pursuant to this procedure, has the same displacement rights as a displaced employee.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

If a displaced employee does not have a previously held classification with the city, or has the least city seniority in the previously held classification, or is no longer qualified or eligible to hold the previously held classification, or the classification no longer exists, the displaced employee shall be laid-off and placed on a reinstatement list.

B.

The director of human resources (or designee) will advise the affected employees, within at least 30 calendar days (or the appropriate period of time required by law) of the employees' effective lay-off date. If the city is unable to provide timely notice, then the city shall pay the affected employees one month's wages (two pay periods) based upon the employee's base rate of pay for their regular work schedule earned in the prior two pay periods.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A laid-off employee shall be placed on a reinstatement list for the classification they held at the time of lay-off. The laid-off employee shall remain on a reinstatement list for the applicable classification for a period of 24 months or a period equal to the laid-off employee's length of employment, whichever is less.

A.

Laid-off employees on a reinstatement list will be ranked in order by their city seniority date for the classification they held at the time of being laid-off. Vacancies will then be offered to individuals on the reinstatement list for a particular classification in descending order of city seniority. A person must still be qualified to perform the essential functions of the job with or without an accommodation to be eligible for the position.

B.

A reinstatement list will have precedence over all other eligibility lists.

C.

An employee who is placed in a previously held classification as a result of being selected from the reinstatement list must meet the minimum qualifications as listed on the job description and successfully complete the background review process prior to beginning the previously held classification. Once the employee starts working with the city again, they may be required to serve a qualifying period of six months.

D.

Laid-off employees on a reinstatement list will be considered eligible for internal recruitments, for classified positions for which they are qualified, for a period of 24 months or a period equal to the employee's length of employment, whichever is less. Employees selected for a classified position as a result of the internal recruitment process, must successfully complete the background review process prior to beginning the new classified position. Once the employee starts working with the city again, they must serve a qualifying period of six months.

E.

Laid-off employees placed on a reinstatement list waive their reinstatement privileges if they fail to respond to a re-employment offer within 15 calendar days after the notice is mailed to the last known address. It is the laid-off employee's responsibility to update the city, in writing, of any changes to their contact information.

F.

Once a laid-off employee is removed from the reinstatement list, the laid-off employee no longer has rights under the civil service rules.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

Employees are required to adhere to the rules and procedures set forth in the civil service rules, as well as to applicable regulations or policies set forth in the City Charter, administrative policies and procedures, ethics rules, employee agreements, department rules and any other official city rules.

B.

Employee responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

1.

Learning their official job duties and performing accordingly;

2.

Completing assigned training, and/or acquiring and/or maintaining any license(s) registration(s), and/or certifications that are required of their position;

3.

Establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with supervisors, fellow employees and the public;

4.

Learning and adhering to city and departmental rules, regulations, and policies;

5.

Maintaining the ability to perform the essential functions of their position with or without a reasonable accommodation;

6.

Maintaining the level of performance required of their position;

7.

Communicating any concerns regarding their employment to their supervisor and/or human resources;

8.

Timely completion of all required self-evaluations;

9.

Attending work as scheduled, unless authorized to be absent, and taking responsibility for initiating and obtaining any necessary authorization for such absences;

10.

Obtaining approval from their immediate supervisor, department director, and the director of human resources to work a secondary job, including employment for third parties or self-employment, while employed by the city; and

11.

Participating and cooperating in investigations conducted by the city.

C.

In addition to the above, employees in supervisory positions are responsible for:

1.

Providing instruction and guidance to employees in the performance of job functions;

2.

Monitoring employee performance and timely completing performance evaluations;

3.

Maintaining an open-door policy with employees, which includes being accessible to their employees' concerns and questions;

4.

Communicating with employees about positive and negative performance;

5.

Documenting employee disciplinary matters and employee complaints; and

6.

Participating, cooperating, and potentially coordinating investigations related to employee disciplinary matters, employee complaints, and other personnel related matters.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

Performance evaluations are meant to be beneficial to both the employer and the employee. In addition to regular work related discussions and/or informal coaching and feedback, supervisors shall conduct formal performance evaluations for each employee under their supervision. All formal performance evaluations shall be completed in a timely manner, and in a manner approved by the director of human resources (or designee). The purpose of the performance evaluation is to review the employee's work performance, achievements, challenges, development goals, and/or define and set clear performance expectations where support is needed. Additionally, the performance evaluation will explain how the employee's job duties aligns with strategic and operational goals and initiatives for both the department and the organization. The performance evaluation also provides an opportunity for the employee to communicate any support they need from their supervisor and ask specific questions to help clarify their role or work.

1.

Supervisors should ensure newly hired employees understand the duties and performance expectations for the position and provide regular feedback during a new hire's probationary period or qualifying period. For employees who are not on a probationary period or qualifying period, supervisors shall conduct performance evaluations on an annual basis.

2.

Performance evaluations should recognize all aspects of an individual's job performance, including exceptional, acceptable and substandard performance. Supervisors should provide regular coaching and feedback to employees throughout the year and refer to such discussions in the formal performance evaluation.

3.

Employees subject to a performance improvement plan may require additional performance evaluations. Employees subject to a performance improvement plan will have clear actions and accountabilities detailed in the plan, which must be satisfied during the stated time period to avoid potential disciplinary action.

4.

Annual pay adjustment increases, general increases, and lump sum performance bonuses are not tied to the employees' yearly performance evaluations. An employee is not eligible for an annual pay adjustment increase, general increase or lump-sum performance bonus if they have received active discipline (as defined in subsection 6.07.050) in the form of a demotion, suspension, performance improvement plan and/or return-to-work/last chance agreement.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

If an employee is performing above and beyond their supervisor's expectations, the department director (or designee) may recognize such performance in writing.

B.

Documentation of an employee's exceptional performance shall be kept in the employee's personnel file.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
Supervisors are encouraged to provide employees regular coaching and feedback to assist employees in successfully performing their jobs. Coaching and feedback should be provided both with respect to positive and negative aspects of an employee's performance and/or conduct. The act of providing coaching and feedback to employees is not considered disciplinary action. Notes and/or other documentation relevant to any coaching and counseling may be recorded in a manner (or method) approved by the director of human resources (or designee), and are subject to standard retention/destruction schedules. If employees fail to act on their supervisors' coaching and feedback, the supervisor may take disciplinary action as set forth in chapter 6.07. This section shall not be construed to require coaching and feedback prior to disciplinary action being taken.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
City employees are expected to maintain certain behavior and performance standards. The following list of prohibited conduct is intended to provide examples of behavior that can result in disciplinary action. This list is not exhaustive—other acts of substance relating to misconduct or work performance of an employee may be considered grounds for disciplinary action.

A.

Incompetency or inefficiency in performance of duties;

B.

Insubordination, unprofessionalism, and/or failure to perform assigned duties;

C.

Failure to comply with the requirements set forth in a performance improvement plan;

D.

Failure to complete assigned training and/or acquire and/or maintain any license(s), registration(s) or certification(s) that are required of the employee's position;

E.

Failure to maintain the confidentiality of the city's non-public information;

F.

Failure to properly record employee's time—examples include but are not limited to, recording the work time of another employee (unless an employee is assigned to be a time-reporter) or allowing any other employee to record your work time (unless the employee reports time to an assigned time-reporter), recording false time records, manipulating time records, and not recording time worked or time off;

G.

Use of obscene, profane or abusive language and/or conduct, including malicious gossip;

H.

Careless, negligent or intentional misuse of city property, equipment, or funds, including use for personal reasons or incidents that result in damage or risk of damage to property;

I.

Violation of a safety rule or safety practice;

J.

Taking audio or video recordings of another employee without the explicit permission from all of the employees who are being recorded;

K.

Failure to follow established procedures in reporting a work related personal injury or damage to city property or city equipment;

L.

Failure to cooperate in an internal investigation;

M.

Excessive tardiness or absenteeism, being absent without leave or failing to report after leave of absence has expired, or abusing paid leave policies;

N.

Sleeping or malingering during work hours;

O.

Violation of the Civil Service Rules, HMC chapter 2.40, the Charter of the City of Henderson, administrative policies and procedures, and/or other city or departmental rules and regulations;

P.

Conviction for, or entering a plea of guilty or no contest to any felony or misdemeanor that is related to the employee's position, violates a city policy, creates a safety concern, and/or involves actions that may diminish the public's trust, whether the offense occurred on or off duty;

Q.

Discriminatory conduct, sexual harassment or harassment based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, covered veteran status, pregnancy, gender identity or expression, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information or any other basis made unlawful by any applicable law, ordinance or regulation (disciplinary action based on this provision may not be appealed to the civil service board);

R.

Engaging in disorderly conduct such as horseplay, scuffling and malicious mischief;

S.

Provoking or instigating a physical fight or fighting at any time while on duty or at any city facility or worksite;

T.

Being under the influence of, use, possession, sale, distribution, dispensing or manufacturing of intoxicating beverages, hallucinogens and/or controlled substances (not prescribed or prescribed but abused/misused); failing to report potential hazards of working while taking a prescribed medication; or use of illegal drugs while at work, or preceding duty so as to be detected by behavior, physical condition or testing while on duty;

U.

Refusal to be tested when there is a reasonable suspicion that the employee was under the influence of alcohol, controlled substances, hallucinogens, or illegal drugs while at work; or if the employee is required to be tested as a result of having a commercial driver's license;

V.

Verbal or physical conduct that is abusive, threatening, offensive or intimidating while on duty or at any city facility or work site;

W.

Acceptance or solicitation of a bribe, improper gift/gratuity, or any compensation intended to influence the employee in the performance of their assigned duties for the city;

X.

Improper use of one's employment with the city for the employee's personal or financial advantage or granting improper privilege to another;

Y.

Misappropriation, misuse, theft, negligent, careless or unauthorized use of city property or funds and/or damage to city property;

Z.

Failure to follow a return-to-work/last chance agreement (terminations based on a failure to comply with the terms of a return-to-work/last chance agreement are not appealable); or

AA.

Dishonesty.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

In conjunction with human resources, the department head (or their designee) may suspend an employee and/or place the employee on leave, with or without pay, pending an investigation of an alleged conduct violation. Suspensions pending investigations are appropriate where the presence of the employee is reasonably likely to:

1.

Be injurious to the employee, a fellow employee or the general public;

2.

Result in damage to property;

3.

Substantially impair management's ability to maintain decorum and discipline; and/or

4.

Hinder the investigatory process.

B.

If an employee has been suspended and/or placed on leave pending investigation, they may not return to work or any city facility until they have received permission from their department director (or designee). The employee may not perform any work for the city.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

Disciplinary actions. Employees may be subject to the following disciplinary actions if they violate these rules or any other city or departmental policy and procedure:

1.

Documented verbal warning;

2.

Written reprimand;

3.

Suspension and/or a demotion (if appropriate and available), and/or subjected to a performance improvement plan (discussed in subsection 6.07.030(B) or a return-to-work/last chance agreement (discussed in subsection 6.07.030(C); and/or

4.

Termination.

The foregoing enumeration of the types of discipline shall not be meant to set forth any necessary sequence of progressive discipline. The type of discipline issued depends upon the facts and circumstances of the incident. All suspensions, demotions, return-to-work/last chance agreements, performance improvement plans and terminations must be approved by the department director (or designee), and the director of human resources (or designee). Transferring positions or accepting a voluntary demotion will not prevent the employee from being disciplined for conduct that occurred prior to the transfer or voluntary demotion.

B.

Performance improvement plans. A Performance Improvement Plan ("PIP") will typically be used after the employee fails to improve their performance or after a failure to correct their behavior after receipt of documented verbal warning or written reprimand. A PIP is not considered to be a disciplinary action; however it may be utilized before or after disciplinary action has been taken. A performance improvement plan is not appropriate in all cases. A performance improvement plan may be appropriate if a supervisor believes that an employee's performance will significantly improve such that the employee will be able to successfully satisfy their job responsibilities at the conclusion of a performance improvement plan. It is the employee's responsibility to fully understand the provisions and requirements within the performance improvement plan. While it is anticipated that the employee will be successful in changing and correcting their substandard job performance, failure to remedy these deficiencies will lead to further disciplinary action, up to and including termination.

A performance improvement plan shall include the following provisions:

1.

Description of unacceptable performance. The supervisor should identify the job functions and/or behaviors that the employee is failing to satisfactorily perform and provide specific examples of the deficiencies.

2.

Timeframe. The plan should identify the specific period of time the employee is being given an opportunity to improve and demonstrate satisfactory performance. Performance improvement plans should last for a minimum period of three months. For extenuating circumstances, a supervisor may extend the timeframe of the plan.

3.

Description of acceptable level of performance. Identify the improvements that are required of the employee and provide suggestions as to how the employee can improve their performance.

4.

Consequences for failing to satisfy the terms and conditions. Clearly indicate that if the employee fails to improve their performance as outlined in the performance improvement plan, then the employee may be subject to termination.

5.

Signatures and date. Both the employee and supervisor should acknowledge the performance improvement plan.

6.

Follow-up. The supervisor should regularly (at least once a week) follow-up with the employee regarding their progress in carrying out the tasks identified in the performance improvement plan. The performance improvement plan may be updated or amended based on the follow-up meetings between the supervisor and the employee.

C.

Return-to-work/last chance agreements. If an employee comes forward to their supervisor and/or human resources business partner and discloses that they are struggling with addiction issues and rehabilitation is appropriate, the city, on a case-by-case basis and in its sole discretion, may require the employee to agree to the terms of a return-to-work/last chance agreement. The return-to-work/last chance agreement shall include a date certain for its start and completion dates. Failure to comply with the terms of a return-to-work/last chance agreement shall result in termination without any right of appeal under the civil service rules.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
section_name: Pre-disciplinary procedures (suspensions without pay, demotions, and terminations).
citation: 6.07.040 - Pre-disciplinary procedures (suspensions without pay, demotions, and terminations).
full_text:
A.

Investigation. A human resources business partner, or a supervisor in conjunction with the human resources business partner, may investigate employee misconduct if the circumstances necessitate an investigation. At the conclusion of the investigation, the supervisor will determine whether disciplinary action is warranted. If disciplinary action is warranted in the form of an unpaid suspension, demotion or termination, then notice of disciplinary action must be provided to the employee before any final disciplinary action is issued.

B.

Notice of disciplinary action. Before an employee may be suspended (without pay), demoted, or terminated, the employee's supervisor shall provide the employee with notice of the disciplinary action. Human resources in conjunction with the supervisor shall prepare a notice of the disciplinary action, which shall include the basis for the recommended suspension (without pay), demotion, or termination.

C.

Employee response. The employee shall have two business days from the date of receipt the notice of disciplinary action to provide a written response to the human resources business partner (or designee). In emergency circumstances, this time period may be extended at the sole discretion of the director of human resources (or designee). If the employee fails to timely provide their response, the city will presume that the employee has accepted the disciplinary action and the director of human resources (or designee) shall approve the recommended disciplinary action, unless such recommendation is clearly erroneous.

D.

Final approval. If an employee response is provided, the human resources business partner (or designee) shall prepare a package for the department director and director of human resources to review. The package shall include a copy of the notice of disciplinary action, any relevant supporting documentation provided to the employee, and the employee's response. The department director, in conjunction with the director of human resources, within four business days, shall determine whether (1) disciplinary action is warranted, and the recommended discipline should be issued by the supervisor, (2) further investigation is required, or (3) different disciplinary action is warranted, in which case the department director may recommend another action. If further investigation is required, then the employee may be placed on suspension pending investigation (with or without pay). Notice of the final disciplinary decision shall be provided to the employee via electronic communication, certified mail or hand delivery. If further investigation is required or additional time is needed, human resources will provide the employee with a status update within the initial four business day timeline.

E.

Exceptions to providing notice of disciplinary action. Notice of disciplinary action is not required for documented verbal warnings or written disciplinary actions. Notice of disciplinary action is also not required where the employee's conduct raises a serious safety concern to the public and/or co-workers or if the employee abandons their job. Where there are safety concerns or where an employee abandons their job, an employee may be immediately terminated by the director of human resources (or designee) without an opportunity to provide a response.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
full_text:
A.

Disciplinary action is considered active discipline if the disciplinary action was issued in the previous 12 months. The date the disciplinary action was presented to the employee is the relevant date for which the 12-month period begins. For the purposes of performance improvement plans and return-to-work agreements, the 12-month period begins on the date that the performance improvement plan or the return-to-work agreement becomes effective (the start date). If 12 months or more have elapsed since the disciplinary action was issued or since the performance improvement plan or the return-to-work agreement began, the disciplinary action/performance improvement plan/return-to-work agreement is considered expired and may not thereafter be used as a basis for or in support of any subsequent disciplinary action, unless the terms of the employee's return-to-work agreement or performance improvement plan state otherwise. Active discipline will remain active for the relevant 12-month period even if an employee is demoted or transferred to another classified position during that time.

B.

If an employee is suspended (without pay), involuntarily demoted or terminated for disciplinary reasons, then the employee has a right to appeal as set forth in chapter 6.08, unless the employee is suspended, involuntarily demoted or terminated for disciplinary reasons related to discriminatory or harassing behavior, or terminated for failing to comply with the terms of a return-to-work/last chance agreement.

C.

Disciplinary actions are placed in the employees' personnel files. Within five business days of receiving disciplinary action, an employee may request to include in their personnel file a written statement of reasonable length in response to any disciplinary action.

D.

Once a disciplinary action has expired (i.e., is no longer active discipline), an employee may request the human resources department to visibly mark the disciplinary action in the personnel file as "inactive." Whether or not the employee requests this, the disciplinary action will be considered expired if 12 months have passed (unless the terms of a performance improvement plan or return-to-work/last chance agreement state otherwise). However, the disciplinary action shall remain in the employee's personnel file.

E.

If the civil service board reverses a disciplinary action (suspension without pay, demotion or termination) on appeal, then the disciplinary action will be removed and/or revised in accordance with the civil service board's decision.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
chapter: Chapter 6.08 - APPEALS TO THE CIVIL SERVICE BOARD
section_name: Chapter 6.08 - APPEALS TO THE CIVIL SERVICE BOARD

title: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES
chapter: Chapter 6.08 - APPEALS TO THE CIVIL SERVICE BOARD
section_name: Appeal rights to the civil service board.
citation: 6.08.010 - Appeal rights to the civil service board.
full_text:
A.

The civil service board has the authority to hear employee appeals on the following issues, which shall be considered receivable appeals:

1.

Discipline that consists of suspension (without pay), involuntary demotion or termination, with the following exceptions:

a.

The civil service board will not hear appeals if an employee is appealing the city's decision to either suspend, involuntarily demote or terminate them as a result of finding that the employee engaged in discriminatory or harassing behavior in violation of the city's anti-discrimination and/or workplace harassment policies.

b.

The civil service board will not hear an appeal based on the city's decision to terminate an employee for job abandonment.

c.

The civil service board will not hear an appeal based on the city's decision to terminate an employee as a result of the employee's failure to comply with a return-to-work/last chance agreement.

d.

The civil service board will not hear appeals on claims that the city engaged in discriminatory or harassing conduct in violation of state or federal laws (including, but not limited to N.R.S. 613.330, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Americans with Disability Act, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act and the Family Medical Leave Act). All complaints of unlawful discrimination and harassment should be made in accordance with the city's anti-discrimination and/or workplace harassment policies.

e.

The civil service board will not hear appeals where an employee is offered the opportunity to return to their former classification or a similar classification (i.e., demoted), as a result of being issued disciplinary action for failure to meet the performance standards during a qualifying period.

2.

If an employee was laid-off as a result of a reduction-in-force, the employee may appeal if the basis of the appeal is that the city did not follow the procedures for implementing reduction-in-force in accordance with section 6.05.030. However, the civil service board will not hear appeals regarding the basis for the city's decision to undertake a reduction-in-force. The appeal is limited to allegations that the city incorrectly followed the process set forth in these rules for implementing a reduction-in-force.

B.

The following provisions shall govern the conditions of an appeal:

1.

No employee shall bring an appeal before the civil service board until an action complained of has become final. An action is considered to be final on the date of the effective lay-off, suspension (for disciplinary reasons and unpaid), involuntary demotion (for disciplinary reasons) or termination (for disciplinary reasons).

2.

An employee must file a notice of appeal with the secretary of the civil service board (the director of human resources) within ten calendar days of the date the action became final. The notice of appeal must contain a statement specifying the action against which the appeal is made, the subsection or sections of the civil service rules under which the appeal is filed and a detailed statement justifying the appeal submission. Failure to submit a notice of appeal pursuant to this section will be grounds to deny the appeal.

3.

Unless the employee and the City agree in writing to waive the initial hearing, the secretary of the civil service board must schedule an initial meeting with the civil service board members (at least three members must attend) to take place within 14 calendar days from receipt of an employee's appeal to determine whether the issue complained of is a receivable appeal under these rules. If an employee's character, alleged misconduct, professional competence, or physical or mental health will be considered at the initial meeting, then the initial meeting will be conducted in a closed meeting unless the appellant waives the closure of the meeting. The employee must attend the initial meeting, and may bring their council at their own expense.

4.

If the issue complained of is not appealable under the civil service rules, then the secretary of the civil service board shall notify the appellant in writing via electronic communication or certified mail to the last known address of the appellant within seven calendar days of the initial meeting that their request for an appeal is denied because the rules do not allow for an appeal.

5.

If the issue complained of is a receivable appeal under these civil service rules, then an appeal hearing shall be set within 40 calendar days of the initial meeting. The parties may mutually agree to extend the hearing date for good cause. Notice shall be sent by electronic communication or certified mail to the last known address of the appellant at least 21 calendar days prior to the scheduled date of the appeal hearing. A notice to the appellant must include the time, place, scope of the hearing, a list of the administrative policy provisions or other rules that the appellant allegedly violated and the possible disciplinary or other adverse administrative actions that may be taken at the meeting. The hearing may be continued on a showing of good cause by either the appellant or the city.
