title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
chapter: Chapter 14.02 - WATER COMMITMENT AND ALLOCATION REGULATIONS
full_text:
A.

Purpose and policy. This chapter sets forth responsibility, authority, and provisions to ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local requirements for the protection of public health, safety and welfare.

B.

Scope. The provisions of this chapter shall apply to all residents of the city, a responsible party operating, maintaining, repairing, relocating, removing, and/or disconnecting the public water system and/or publicly owned treatment works, and/or users of city-provided utilities.

C.

Administration. Except as otherwise provided herein, the director shall administer, implement, and enforce the provisions of this chapter. Any powers granted or duties imposed upon the director may be delegated by the director to persons acting in the beneficial interest.

D.

Compliance. All provisions of this chapter are subject to compliance procedures as outlined in this title and the department service rules.

(Ord. 2676, § 2, 2008; Ord. 2536, § 3, 2006)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
chapter: Chapter 14.02 - WATER COMMITMENT AND ALLOCATION REGULATIONS
full_text:
A.

All water commitments shall be governed by and made in accordance with the requirements stipulated in the Henderson Municipal Code and the department service rules.

B.

Section 14.02.040 shall be effective for water committed by the City of Henderson through an executed water service contract. Water commitment associated with development that falls under a water service contract shall be addressed in accordance with this title and the applicable sections of the department service rules.

C.

Water commitment for all water service contracts that have expired, or have had their allocations relinquished or revoked, shall be governed by section 14.02.030 and made in accordance with the requirements stipulated in the department service rules.

D.

Approval of a water commitment shall not be deemed to prevent future exercise of the city's authority to protect health, safety and general welfare.

E.

All water committed to projects by the Victory Valley Land Company (VVLC), The Landwell Company, or any other subsidiary company of VVLC as determined by the city, which is under agreement with the City of Henderson, shall be governed by this chapter.

(Ord. 2536, § 4, 2006; Ord. No. 2951, § 2, 12-20-2011)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
chapter: Chapter 14.02 - WATER COMMITMENT AND ALLOCATION REGULATIONS
full_text:
A.

All developments requiring water service from the city shall obtain a water commitment in accordance with this chapter and procedures stipulated in the service rules.

B.

Exemptions. Any development not requiring water service from the city shall be exempt from this chapter; or any temporary activity that does not create a permanent water demand, or additional activities that do not create additional water demands from the property initiating such activities shall not be required to obtain a water commitment.

C.

A will serve letter is issued as a part of the city's duty to the general public and shall not constitute any obligation of the city, or entitlement of the developer to serve the development project with water, except to the extent that a valid water service contract has been approved and executed for the project, or conditional water commitment secured pursuant to this title.

D.

All water committed under this chapter shall be committed in a manner that is consistent with the recommendations set forth in the then-current SNWA Water Resource Plan, as approved by the City of Henderson and SNWA and on file with the State of Nevada, Division of Water Resources.

E.

Final issuance of a water commitment shall not be deemed to give rise to the accrual or vested development rights, equitable estoppel claims, or any right or guarantee to receive development approvals, building or grading permits. Nor does it relieve the recipient of such water commitment from complying with established rules or regulations governing the development of land, or the provision of payment for water facilities required under this title and the service rules.

F.

Final issuance of a water commitment does not create or imply water rights, or an automatic property interest in water service. Instead, issuance of a water commitment authorizes water service to be provided in accordance with the conditions set forth in this title and department service rules.

G.

Approval of a water commitment shall terminate and the conditional commitment shall be considered void if completion of any prerequisite item becomes delinquent or expires.

H.

The director reserves the right to deny any request for a water commitment if the city deems the property and/or premises requiring service to be non-compliant with any provisions of this Code.

I.

A water commitment must be obtained from the city prior to establishment of a new water service connection. Water service to a new water service connection will not be activated until all requirements for establishing such service have been satisfied.

J.

A new water commitment must be obtained from the city prior to expanding or upgrading any existing service connection. Any proposal to expand or upgrade an existing service must be coordinated with the department of utility services. Such proposal shall follow the requirements for the establishment of a new water service connection.

K.

Any expansion or addition of buildings or structures on a parcel of land presently served by the city, where such expansion or addition increases the water demands above the total water commitment established for such parcel of land, shall obtain a new water commitment for such additional demand.

L.

A water commitment is deemed conditional until all items identified in the service rules pertaining to water commitment have been satisfied. Notwithstanding any provision in the service rules, payment of applicable fees and construction of any water facilities (where applicable), a water commitment shall be deemed final upon the city's verification that all steps in the water commitment process as outlined in the service rules are complete. Nevertheless, the city may deny any request for a water commitment or request for a water service connection if the city determines there is an inadequate supply of water, or there are physical limitations in the system capacity to serve the developer or proposed customer and simultaneously maintain an adequate level of service to other customers, or if granting the request would compromise public health, safety and/or welfare. Developers shall proceed accordingly at their own risk.

M.

Water commitment cannot be traded, sold or transferred to another parcel of land. Recordation of a parcel map, final map or other map associated with the division of land shall not be interpreted as the city's authorization for, or commitment of water service. Final issuance of a water commitment shall occur only upon completion of the steps outlined in the service rules.

N.

Water commitment shall become void upon abandonment or removal of an existing service connection. Re-establishment of an abandoned or removed service connection shall require application for and issuance of a new water commitment.

O.

If a property owner requests water service from the city and such owner owns a permanent, non-revocable water right for diversion of groundwater from one of the hydrographic basins identified in the following sentence, then all or a portion of said non-revocable water right shall be donated and transferred to the city as a condition of provision of service. A person owning a permanent, non-revocable water right for diversion from the Las Vegas Valley, Black Mountain Area, Colorado River Valley, Eldorado Valley, Paiute Valley, and/or Ivanpah Valley hydrographic basin who donates and transfers the water rights to the city, pays all applicable fees and charges, and meets all other requirements of the city, may obtain a commitment from the city in an amount equal to the pumpage permitted to the city by the state engineer, but not to exceed the amount of water right donated. The water commitment shall become effective 31 days following the date the state engineer approves an application to change.

P.

Public water system service area.

1.

The city council recognizes that there are persons owning property outside of the city's public water system service area that desire to connect such property to the public water system because no existing facilities are readily available to provide service by that property's governing jurisdiction. In such cases, the city shall not permit a person to request, or a property to receive, a connection to the city's public water system to any extra-territorial property. The city shall continue to serve extra-territorial properties with its public water system if:

a.

Such properties were connected to the public water system prior to the effective date of the ordinance from which this subsection derives; and

b.

A property is connected to the public water system prior to the effective date of the ordinance from which this subsection derives pursuant to a service contract, and the properties and/or the parties to the service contract are in compliance with the terms of service contract.

2.

For purposes of this chapter, the service area for the public water system is designated as any and all real property located within the contiguous corporate boundaries of the City of Henderson as those boundaries may be amended from time-to-time. All other real properties located outside of the contiguous corporate boundaries of the City of Henderson are deemed extra-territorial properties, and explicitly not a part of the city's public water system service area. The city council may, by ordinance, amend the service area to include areas outside the corporate boundaries if the city council determines:

a.

That a public benefit will be served by such change; and

b.

A concurrent contract is provided by the property's jurisdictional governing body.

3.

Nothing in this section shall be deemed to preclude the city from discontinuing or interrupting service for any reason authorized by law or contract, and the city may terminate service for failure to comply with any service contract.

Q.

Revocable groundwater rights and domestic wells. A building or structure that currently receives water from a revocable groundwater right (and is required to connect to a municipal water purveyor because the right to use groundwater is revoked by the state engineer) or from a domestic well may be permitted to obtain a water commitment from the city for the building or structure, provided the existing well is abandoned in accordance with all local, state, and federal requirements.

R.

Water rights or rights to delivery of Colorado River water to SNWA for use by city. With approval of the director, a person can obtain a water commitment without donating the water right or assigning the right to delivery of Colorado River water directly to the city if that person assigns to SNWA the water rights or rights to delivery of Colorado River water, a percentage of which is for use by the city. SNWA and the city shall have the sole authority to evaluate the proposed acceptance of water rights and/or right to delivery of Colorado River water, including based upon water quality, quantity, assured availability, location, deliverability, and legal considerations, and shall determine if the offered water rights and/or right to delivery of Colorado River water may be used to obtain a water commitment under this process. If acceptable to SNWA and the city, the city may enter into a contractual arrangement with the person to provide for a present or future water commitment.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 2, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3322, § 1, 12-15-2015; Ord. No. 2909, § 5, 3-15-2011; Ord. 2536, § 5, 2006)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
chapter: Chapter 14.02 - WATER COMMITMENT AND ALLOCATION REGULATIONS
full_text:
A.

This section shall be effective for water allocated by the city through July 16, 1996, and verified by an executed water service contract. All existing water service contracts and future assignments from master plan and/or T-District water allocations shall continue to be governed by this section and the service rules, except that approvals by the city council shall be by the director.

B.

Existing water service contracts shall be administered in accordance with the stipulations of Ordinance No. 1259, as well as other ordinances previously codified and incorporated by reference associated with the city's water allocation program and shall be made a part of this section by reference.

C.

Expiration/revocation of water service contracts.

1.

All water service contracts that have expired and thus were relinquished or revoked shall reapply pursuant to section 14.02.030 and department service rules.

2.

Expiration and/or revocation of a water service contract shall be in accordance with the established procedures outlined in this title and department service rules.

3.

The city council may revoke a water service contract for any of the following reasons:

a.

Failure to commence construction on or before the date set forth in construction schedule contained in the water service contract;

b.

Failure to complete construction in strict accordance with the construction schedule required in the long form water service contract;

c.

Expiration or revocation of a building permit, unless extended by city council;

d.

Failure to complete construction by the final construction date set forth in the construction schedule contained in the water service contract; or

e.

Failure to comply with any other condition imposed in the water service contract or any other condition imposed as a condition of development.

4.

In the event the applicant is unable to comply with the terms and conditions of the water service contract that would result in expiration/revocation, the applicant may request an extension of the contract. Any such extension is at the sole discretion of the city council and shall require satisfaction of additional conditions not inconsistent with the original approval. Applicant shall have the burden of establishing that the reasons for extension are for acts or circumstances that were unforeseeable at the time of the original approval.

5.

The director shall initiate revocation proceedings under this section whenever it is determined that one of the following approvals has expired, whether expiration occurs on a particular date or by virtue of the terms and conditions imposed on the approval:

a.

Approval/issuance of a water service contract; or

b.

Any transitional approval.

6.

Upon a determination that an approval specified above has expired, the director shall refer the matter to the city council for a hearing or revocation proceedings. The city council shall notify the holder of an approval specified above, any persons to whom notices were mailed in the original proceedings, and any persons who have been designated interested parties in the initial application for approval, that the approval shall be revoked unless sufficient cause is shown to the city council within ten days from such notification that the approval should not be revoked.

7.

If the holder of an approval specified above, or any other person notified pursuant to subsection (c)(5) of this section requests, within ten days from the date of such notice, that a hearing be held concerning revocation, the city council shall schedule a hearing within a reasonable time after receiving such request. The city council may designate persons other than the holder of an approval as interveners in the proceedings. At the hearing the city council shall hear testimony of city staff, the holder of the approval, interveners and, if present, any other person alleging direct injury. The hearing may be continued without additional public notice.

8.

The city council shall revoke an approval upon making one or more of the following findings:

a.

That the approval was made on the basis of erroneous or misleading information or misrepresentation; or

b.

That the terms or condition(s) of the approval have been violated or that other laws or regulations have been violated.

Upon demonstration that extenuating circumstances exist which have prevented the satisfaction of conditions imposed on an approval specified in paragraph 4 above, the city council may allow an extension of an approval on satisfaction of additional conditions not inconsistent with the initial approval.

9.

Within a reasonable period of time, the city council shall render a decision and shall mail notice of such decision to the holder of the approval, and to any person who has filed written request for such notice.

10.

A decision to revoke an approval shall become final, ten days after the date of the decision.

11.

The city's right to revoke such approval specified in subsection (c)(4) of this section, shall be cumulative to any other remedy allowed in law or equity.

(Ord. No. 2909, § 5, 3-15-2011; Ord. 2536, § 6, 2006; Ord. No. 2951, § 2, 12-20-2011)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Purpose and policy. This chapter sets forth responsibility, authority, and provisions to ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local requirements for the protection of public health, safety and welfare.

B.

Scope. The provisions of this chapter shall apply to all residents of the city, a responsible party operating, maintaining, repairing, relocating, removing, and/or disconnecting the public water system and/or publicly owned treatment works, and/or users of city-provided utilities.

C.

Administration. Except as otherwise provided herein, the director shall administer, implement, and enforce the provisions of this chapter. Any powers granted or duties imposed upon the director may be delegated by the director to persons acting in the beneficial interest of the city.

D.

Compliance. All provisions of this chapter are subject to compliance procedures as outlined in this title and the department service rules.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

The city may, subject to the approval of the director, authorize the taking and receipt of water in accordance with this title and the department service rules. Where water is required for construction purposes or any other temporary use, the city must first authorize the location for use of such water, the service must be from a temporary connection and established in accordance with this title and the department service rules, and the city may reject a request for temporary service.

B.

Applicants requesting service shall pay applicable fees and charges in accordance with this title and department service rules.

C.

The city reserves the right to specify or restrict the location, time, and rate of water use to avoid interference with service to other customers.

D.

The customer is responsible for all plumbing, piping, and appurtenances from the service connection to the point of use.

E.

Service lines shall be installed in accordance with adopted standards. The director reserves the right to determine the service size, service line material, meter size, location, installation configuration, and service connection.

F.

The customer shall furnish all necessary equipment to convey the water from the service connection to the customer point of use. In the case of mixed use developments, service connections shall be established and billed in accordance with the adopted standards and department service rules. Those units that are a combined commercial-residential unit shall be billed as commercial.

G.

Temporary water service will cease when a permanent demand for potable water has been established, including but not limited to fire service, domestic supply and landscape irrigation.

H.

The customer shall not operate the service in a manner which may create an adverse condition such as, but not limited to, low pressure, pressure surges, reduction of flow, or compromised water quality within the city's public water system.

I.

The city will endeavor to provide its customers with a continuous and adequate supply of water within reasonable maximum and minimum pressures. However, varying pressures will normally prevail throughout the distribution system due to changes in elevation, use, and other factors.

J.

Where prevailing water pressures fall outside of prescribed operating limits, applicants for service shall be responsible for installation of pressure regulators, storage tanks, pumps, or other devices as the director may require.

K.

Unless otherwise approved by the director, all privately owned systems shall remain privately owned and maintained.

L.

Unless otherwise approved by the director, all properties shall be provided domestic service through a single service connection. Where multiple services to a single property are allowed, said services shall be established in accordance with this title, the department service rules, and adopted standards.

M.

The city reserves the right to authorize use of facilities prior to final acceptance. Exercising such right does not infer acceptance or release of responsibility for compliance with any and/or all requirements of this title, adopted standards, and/or the department service rules.

N.

It shall be the customer's responsibility to maintain and to not allow the loss, escape, or excess use of water through a break, leak, or other malfunction in the water distribution facilities on the property or premises, such as an irrigation pipe or tubing, the irrigation delivery system, or a water supply line. Any and all repairs necessary to correct a malfunction(s), including all costs associated with such repairs, shall be the sole responsibility of the customer whether performed at the customer's direction or at the city's direction in connection with the city taking corrective action.

O.

Out of valley area. If, after December 9, 2020, a customer wishes to receive water service from the city and all or a portion of the property or premises that will be served by the city are located in the out of valley area, wastewater service for the customer shall comply with the requirements stated within subsection 14.04.020.P of this title.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 3, 9-13-2022; Ord. 2676, § 3 (part), 2008; Ord. 2536, § 12, 2006)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Meters.

1.

A city-approved meter per adopted standards shall be installed on each service line to measure water usage.

2.

Each meter location shall be within the public right-of-way directly adjacent to the parcel being served. If street right-of-way is not available, the director may approve installation within an easement or alley adjacent to or on the parcel to be served. All meters shall be located where access by city personnel for operation and maintenance will not be restricted. The meter shall be located outside of travel lanes and driveways and shall be protected from vehicular traffic, unless otherwise approved by the director.

3.

Any single family residential combination fire and domestic water system installed after February 1, 2009, shall have a minimum one inch residential fire meter installed.

B.

Valves.

1.

For services with a three-inch meter or larger where the service has been discontinued or it becomes necessary to shut off a service connection for repair of piping on the customer's property, a valve as required by adopted standards shall be installed prior to restoration of the service with all costs to be borne by the customer. Should the customer fail to make such repairs or corrections to the service conditions and the city has performed its due diligence to notify the customer to make such repairs or corrections, the director may authorize the city to make the necessary corrections, with the customer being responsible for reimbursement to the city for all costs incurred in addition to any penalties in accordance with this title and the department service rules.

2.

Private property shutdowns conducted at the property owner's request shall be billed using the department's actual costs, with such costs being the responsibility of the property owner.

C.

Fire service connections. Fire service connections shall only be used for fire suppression unless otherwise approved by the director. Should any unauthorized connection be made, the city reserves the right to shut off the service or install a meter at the customer's expense and charge for it at regular domestic rates.

D.

Corrective actions. When, in the opinion of the director, an existing service line becomes inadequate and/or a customer/owner has not complied with adopted standards, the city may choose to install, upgrade, and/or repair the service line with prior notification and at the customer/owner's expense. This expense shall be billed using the department's actual costs.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 4, 9-13-2022; Ord. 2798, § 2, 1-20-2009; Ord. 2676, § 3 (part), 2008; Ord. 2536, § 13, 2006)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Unless otherwise approved by the director, all service connections shall be made to a main that is located immediately adjacent to the property requiring service. The director reserves the right to determine the main to which connection shall be made.

B.

Applicants requesting service to a property where no city main exists contiguous to the property must first arrange for a main extension in accordance with this title and department service rules. Where such main exists but does not extend across the full extent of the property frontage or is within 400 feet of the property as described in subsection 14.03.040.D, subsection 14.03.040.E, or subsection 14.03.040.F, the city may require the applicant to extend the main to such extent prior to obtaining utility service.

C.

All public mains shall be placed within a dedicated public street. Where no public street is available and upon approval by the director, a public main may be installed within a dedicated municipal utility easement. Said easement shall not be less than 20 feet in width and shall be contained within a single parcel of land. The easement shall increase by ten feet in width for each utility main added to the easement beyond a single main. All mains shall be centered in the available easement space. Unless otherwise allowed by the city, all utility easements in a subdivision, not within a public or private street, shall be within a common element. The easement width required may increase with a main deeper than standard. In such instance, the easement shall be perpetual in nature and unless otherwise approved by the director, shall be exclusive to the city. Proper access by city personnel to all areas within the easement must be provided. No building, structures, fences, trees, shrubs, or other improvements that interfere with its use by the city, can be placed within the easement. The city reserves the right to operate, maintain, repair, replace and/or change the size and/or number of mains and appurtenances within such easement. All such easements shall be granted to the city in a form and manner that is acceptable to the city.

D.

Unless otherwise approved by the director, a property shall cease obtaining water service through a private well if the property served by the well lies within 400 feet of the city's water system. The 400 feet length shall be measured from the closest point of that property to the point of connection from an existing, active and accessible city main and, generally, route through existing or future streets or, as determined by the department, other areas appropriate for a main.

If deemed in the best interest of the city, the director may require the owner of such property to abandon all private wells in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, perform a main extension and establish water service from the city in accordance with the city's requirements.

E.

Water service must be obtained from the city whenever an undeveloped property initiates development through the city and such property lies within 400 feet of the city's water system. In such instance, a main extension shall be required and must be made in accordance with the city's requirements. The 400 feet length shall be measured from the closest point of that property to the point of connection from an existing, active and accessible city main and, generally, route through existing or future streets or, as determined by the department, other areas appropriate for a main.

F.

In such instance where a parcel map is being proposed, a main extension shall be required whenever the city's water system lies within the resulting calculation of 400 feet multiplied by either the total number of lots created by recordation of such map of such parcel of land or the maximum number of lots that could be created based on then-current zoning, whichever number of lots is greater. Where consecutive parcel maps are being proposed, a main extension shall be required whenever the city's water system lies within the resulting calculation of 400 feet multiplied by either (1) the total number of lots created by the recordation of the initial and all consecutive parcel maps combined or (2) the maximum number of lots that could be created based on then-current zoning of the parcels of land in the initial and all consecutive parcel maps combined for those parcels of land, whichever number of lots is greater. However, final determination, including application of these requirements, shall be made by the director.

G.

In such instance where a tentative map or planned unit development is being proposed and no city main exists contiguous to the property, a main extension shall be required and must be made in accordance with the city's requirements.

H.

Unless otherwise approved by the director, not more than one lot or other parcel of subdivided land shall be served by a single service connection. A single customer shall be responsible for payment of water bills for each such service. Additionally, where the city provides water and sewer service to a single lot or other parcel of subdivided land, the same customer shall be responsible for payment of both the water and sewer bill.

1.

Exception: In the case of a commercial subdivision whereby a single service line or service lines provide service to multiple lots or other parcels of subdivided land, a single customer shall exist in the form of a property owner's association. Said property owner's association shall be responsible for payment of all water and sewer bills associated with such service(s). Additionally, the subdivision shall record a declaration of covenants, conditions and restrictions (CC&Rs) in the office of the Clark County recorder, which designates that all of the lot owners in the subdivision own an undivided interest in the private water facilities, and that all of the lot owners must participate in the cost of the operation and maintenance of such private systems.

I.

Where multiple services are provided to a single lot or other parcel of subdivided land, a single customer shall be responsible for payment of water and/or sewer bills for all such services.

J.

When a main extension is required, the director reserves the right to dictate the size, length and capacity of such main. The applicant may apply for partial cost reimbursement through the establishment of a refunding agreement, as outlined in this title and department service rules.

K.

When a connection is made to any main, the main frontage fee is assessed in accordance with this title and the service rules. A minimum charge shall apply to any parcel having less than 60 feet of chargeable frontage.

L.

All mains and main extensions must be designed and constructed in accordance with the city's adopted standards.

M.

Before a main, service line, or connection is allowed to be placed into service, it shall be tested to the satisfaction of the city.

N.

The granting of a certificate of occupancy does not relieve the developer of its obligations relative to the construction of the main extension; nor does it imply that the mains have been properly constructed or accepted by the city.

O.

Upon completion of a main extension by a customer or subdivider, the customer or subdivider shall furnish the department a valid bill of sale conveying title to the city for such main and appurtenances, to include service lines, rights-of-way, and/or easements. Upon transfer of such title, the city reserves the right to provide direct or indirect service to any customer through the use of such mains and appurtenances.

P.

The developer is responsible to correct any defects or failures that occur relative to the design and construction of the main extension, within a period of one year from the date of acceptance of the work by the city. The developer shall, at the developer's own expense, make good such defects and failures and make all replacements and adjustments required, in accordance with the city's requirements. All repairs shall be subject to the approval of the city. Furthermore, developer is at no time relieved of any obligation or responsibility it may have by law, including but not limited to damages for latent deficiencies, injury to real or personal property or injury to or wrongful death of a person.

Q.

The developer shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the city, its officers, agents, volunteers, and employees, against and from any and all liability, loss, damage, claims, fines, demands, causes of action, costs, expenses, and judgments of whatsoever nature, including but not limited to reasonable costs of investigation, reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses, all reasonable expert witness fees and expenses, and all court or arbitration or other alternative dispute resolution costs which result from injury to or death of any persons whomsoever, and/or against and from damage to or loss or destruction of property whatsoever when such injury, death, loss, destruction or damage is due to or arises in connection with or as a result of any work done by the developer, its contractors, agents and subcontractors in connection with the construction of the main and/or arises out of or in connection with developer's, or its contractors' and subcontractors' performance or failure to comply with the requirements of this title or the department's service rules.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 5, 9-13-2022; Ord. 2676, § 3 (part), 2008; Ord. 2536, § 14, 2006)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Extensions of backbone infrastructure.

1.

Unless otherwise approved by the director, construction and/or extensions of backbone infrastructure to support service to proposed developments, including all costs associated with such construction and/or extensions shall be the responsibility of the customer. Additionally, the design of such infrastructure, including the preparation of all applicable design reports shall be the responsibility of the customer, and shall be prepared in accordance with the city's requirements. By proceeding with the proposed development and associated backbone infrastructure required to support service to it, the customer acknowledges that they have gained a complete understanding of the city's requirements, and agree to comply with them accordingly.

2.

Where the director determines it is in the city's best interest for the city to assume the responsibility for the construction and/or extensions of backbone infrastructure to support service to developments, or to participate in a cost-sharing with the customer responsible for such construction and/or extensions, the director reserves the right to establish a special refunding agreement in order to establish a means of receiving proportional cost reimbursement from customers that benefit from the construction of such infrastructure. Said special refunding agreement shall be established in accordance with the requirements outlined in this title and the department's service rules.

3.

The granting of a certificate of occupancy does not relieve the customer of its obligations relative to the construction of the backbone infrastructure; nor does it imply that the backbone infrastructure has been properly constructed or accepted by the city.

4.

The customer is responsible to correct any defects or failures that occur relative to the design and construction of the backbone infrastructure, within a period of one year from the date of acceptance of the work by the city. The customer shall, at the customer's own expense, make good such defects and failures and make all replacements and adjustments required, in accordance with the city's requirements. All repairs shall be subject to the approval of the city.

5.

The customer, at all times, is not relieved of any obligation or responsibility it may have by law, including but not limited to damages for latent deficiencies, injury to real or personal property or injury to or wrongful death of a person.

6.

The customer shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the city, its officers, agents, volunteers, and employees, against and from any and all liability, loss, damage, claims, fines, demands, causes of action, costs, expenses, and judgments of whatsoever nature, including but not limited to reasonable costs of investigation, reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses, all reasonable expert witness fees and expenses, and all court or arbitration or other alternative dispute resolution costs which result from injury to or death of any persons whomsoever, and/or against and from damage to or loss or destruction of property whatsoever when such injury, death, loss, destruction or damage is due to or arises in connection with or as a result of any work done by the customer, its contractors, agents and subcontractors in connection with the construction of the backbone infrastructure, and/or arises out of or in connection with customer's, or its contractors' and subcontractors' performance or failure to comply with the requirements of this title or the department service rules.

B.

Sizing of backbone infrastructure. The director reserves the right to determine the size and capacity of the backbone infrastructure proposed for construction, taking into account projected service needs of the areas served and whenever it is deemed to be in the best interest of the city in order to provide for the orderly development of the city's public infrastructure system. Where said size or capacity of such backbone infrastructure is deemed to be in excess of the customer's needs to support their project, it shall be the customer's responsibility to comply with such requirement, with all costs associated with its compliance to be the sole responsibility of the customer. In such situations the customer may apply for a special refunding agreement in order to seek proportional cost reimbursement from other developers and/or landowners that benefit from the construction of such infrastructure. Said special refunding agreement shall be established in accordance with the requirements outlined in this title and the department service rules.

(Ord. 2536, § 15, 2006)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Upon dedication and/or acceptance of any part of the city's public water system, the city shall be responsible for its maintenance and repair, subject to any agreement covering the installation of such facilities.

Street pavement and sidewalk replacement conducted by the department in association with system repairs are limited to standard asphalt and concrete types. Where a non-standard pavement or sidewalk exists, the city shall not be responsible for the replacement of such non-standard material.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

The city will endeavor to notify customers in advance of any interruption in service due to repair, maintenance, or other causes. In emergency conditions, when notification is not possible or practical, service may be interrupted for indefinite periods. At no time shall the city be liable for loss and/or damages that may occur due to any interruption in service and/or due to system failure.

B.

In accordance with department service rules, written notification shall be provided to the director whenever persons are engaged in street work and/or onsite repairs, including but not limited to grading, directional boring, filling and trenching, and/or paving that may cause removal, displacement or modifications to any portion of the city's public water system, or any interruption of service to the city's customers. title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
Any person who fails or refuses to comply with any of the following provisions shall be deemed to be in violation of this title and shall be subject to discontinuance of service, subject to any penalties and charges assessed in accordance with this title and/or department service rules, and subject to all compliance procedures as prescribed within this title.

A.

Any person who negligently, recklessly or willfully introduces or causes to be introduced into the city's public water system, any pollutant or hazardous substance which such person knew, or with the exercise of reasonable due diligence would have known, could cause personal injury or system damage shall be deemed in violation of this chapter.

C.

Any person who, without prior authorization by the city, operates, maintains, repairs, relocates, cuts, changes, removes, disconnects, repairs or interferes in any manner with the city's public water system, is in violation of this chapter.

D.

Any person or party who, with or without authorization by the city, takes actions which result in damage to any portion of the city's public water system, either directly or indirectly, is in violation of this chapter.

E.

Any person who takes water without applying for and receiving approval from the department for a service connection is in violation of this chapter.

F.

With the exception of construction phase meter set up and testing, it is prohibited to utilize spacers for the purpose of providing water service to the property.

G.

Manifolding and/or meter banking multiple meters for the purpose of reducing or avoiding service connection fees is prohibited.

H.

Any entry into city property and/or premises by an unauthorized person is prohibited and subject to enforcement procedures as outlined in this title.

(Ord. 2536, § 19, 2006)

Purpose and policy. This chapter sets forth responsibility, authority, and provisions to ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local requirements for the protection of public health, safety and welfare.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

The city may, subject to the approval of the director, authorize service from a permanent wastewater connection in accordance with this title and the department service rules. Where wastewater is required for a temporary use, the director may authorize temporary service.

B.

The city reserves the right to specify or restrict the location, time, and rate of discharge to avoid interference with service to other customers.

C.

Wastewater service lines shall be installed in accordance with adopted standards. The director reserves the right to determine the service size, service line material, location, installation configuration, and service connection.

D.

The customer is responsible for all plumbing, piping, and appurtenances from the point of use to the service connection.

E.

The customer shall furnish all necessary piping and connections to convey wastewater from the point of use to the service connection.

F.

In the case of mixed use developments, service connections shall be established and billed in accordance with the department service rules. Those units that are a combined live-work unit shall be billed as commercial.

G.

Temporary wastewater service will cease when a permanent demand for service has been established.

H.

Septic tanks shall be disconnected and abandoned upon connection to the city's publicly owned treatment works. Abandonment shall be performed in such a manner as to meet the requirements of any federal, state, local and city requirements and/or standards.

I.

The customer shall not discharge waste in a manner which may create an adverse condition such as, but not limited to, reduction of flow, stoppage in the city's publicly owned treatment works, or compromised water quality within the city's publicly owned treatment works and/or public water system.

J.

The city will endeavor to provide its customers with uninterrupted wastewater service.

K.

Where service cannot be provided without the use of pumps or other equipment, said pumps and equipment shall remain privately owned and maintained. The city reserves the right to assume ownership and maintenance of such equipment if the director determines it is in the best interest of the city. Where assumptions of ownership and maintenance occur, the director may require said pumps and equipment to meet adopted standards.

L.

Unless otherwise approved by the director, all privately owned systems shall remain privately owned and maintained.

M.

All construction developments shall implement a means of protection against accidental discharges into the city publicly owned treatment works.

N.

The city reserves the right to authorize use of facilities prior to final acceptance. Exercising such right does not infer acceptance by the city or release of responsibility by the developer for compliance with all requirements associated with acceptance of said facilities.

O.

Wastewater service area.

1.

The city council recognizes that there are persons owning property outside of the city's wastewater service area that desire to connect such property to the city's wastewater system because no existing facilities are readily available to provide service by that property's governing jurisdiction. In such cases, the city shall not permit a person to request, or a property to receive, a connection to the city's wastewater system to any extra-territorial property. The city shall continue to serve extra-territorial properties with its wastewater system if:

a.

A person submitted all documents necessary to effect a connection for a property to the city's wastewater system prior to July 1, 2015, including, but not limited to, an executed annexation agreement and petition for annexation by the owner(s) of the property to be serviced; or

b.

A property is connected to the city's wastewater system prior to the effective date of this ordinance pursuant to a service contract, and the properties and/or the parties to the service contract are in compliance with the terms of service contract.

2.

For purposes of this chapter, the wastewater service area for the city's wastewater system is designated as any and all real property located within the contiguous corporate boundaries of the city of Henderson as those boundaries may be amended from time-to-time. All other real property located outside of the contiguous corporate boundaries of the city is deemed extra-territorial property, and explicitly not a part of the city's wastewater service area. The city council may, by ordinance, amend the wastewater service area to include areas outside the corporate boundaries if the city council determines:

a.

That a public benefit will be served by such change, and

b.

A concurrent agreement is provided by the property's jurisdictional governing body.

3.

Nothing in this section shall be deemed to preclude the city from discontinuing or interrupting service for any reason authorized by law or contract, and the city may terminate service for failure to comply with any service contract.

P.

Out of valley area.

1.

Notwithstanding the prohibition in section 14.03.020.O, if a proposed development is contemplated in the out of valley area, the developer has requested that the city provide water service to all or a portion of the property or premises on which that new development will be located, that development is not within the vicinity of a wastewater system operated by an SNWA member agency that will discharge that wastewater to the Las Vegas Wash (each, a "regional wastewater system"), and the developer wishes to use a septic system(s) for that development, then the director may approve - but is not required to approve or otherwise allow - the proposed development to receive water service from the city and allow the property(ies) within the proposed development to discharge wastewater to a septic system(s) if all of the following are met:

a.

A regional wastewater system that will serve the development is being designed and constructed contemporaneously with the design and construction of the cleanout and sanitary and sewer laterals for each unit within the proposed development.

b.

For each unit within the proposed development that will receive a separate water service from the city, a cleanout and sanitary sewer lateral is designed and constructed that complies with adopted standards and enables the unit to disconnect from the septic system or other temporary system approved by the department and connect to a future, regional wastewater system.

c.

The cleanout and sanitary sewer lateral described in subsection 14.04.020.P.1.b are shown on civil improvement plans for the development that are accepted by, and on file with, the city.

d.

The property owner of each unit signs and records in the office of the county recorder of Clark County, Nevada a declaration of special land use restriction wherein the property owner agrees that, within three months after the operator of the regional wastewater system assumes responsibility for operation and maintenance of that system, the property owner (at their cost) shall connect to the regional wastewater system in compliance with the requirements of the operator of that system and shall remove or abandon their septic system in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including Southern Nevada Health District regulations. 2.

The city shall not issue a building permit for a new structure in the out of valley area (with the exception of a grading permit) until after the developer provides documentation to the city that shows the cleanout and sanitary sewer lateral described in subsection 14.04.020.P.1.b are included in the applicable construction plans for the development.

The city shall not issue a certificate of occupancy for a new structure in the out of valley area until after the city inspects the property and confirms that the cleanout and sanitary sewer lateral were constructed in conformance with the requirements in subsection 14.04.020.P.1.b above and construction has commenced on the regional wastewater system to convey the wastewater generated from the property to the regional wastewater system.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES

Customer's responsibility. title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Unless otherwise approved by the director, all service connections shall be made to a wastewater main that is located immediately adjacent to the property requiring service. The director reserves the right to determine the wastewater main to which connection shall be made.

B.

Applicants requesting service to a property where no city wastewater main exists contiguous to the property must first arrange for a wastewater main extension in accordance with this title and department service rules. Where such wastewater main exists but does not extend across the full extent of the property frontage or is within 400 feet of the property as described in subsections 14.04.040.E, 14.04.040.F, or 14.04.040.G, the city may require the applicant to extend the wastewater main to such extent prior to obtaining utility service.

C.

All public wastewater mains shall be placed within a dedicated public street. Where no public street is available and upon approval by the director, a public wastewater main may be installed within a dedicated municipal utility easement. Said easement shall not be less than 20 feet in width and shall be contained within a single parcel of land. The easement shall increase by ten feet in width for each utility main added to the easement beyond a single main. All mains shall be centered in the available easement space. Unless otherwise allowed by the city, all utility easements in a subdivision, not within a public or private street, shall be within a common element. The easement width required may increase with a main deeper than standard. In such instance, the easement shall be perpetual in nature and unless otherwise approved by the director, shall be exclusive to the city. Proper access by city personnel to all areas within the easement must be provided. No building, structures, fences, trees, shrubs, or other improvements that interfere with its use by the city, can be placed within the easement. The city reserves the right to operate, maintain, repair, replace and/or change the size and/or number of wastewater mains and appurtenances within such easement. All such easements shall be granted to the city in a form and manner that is acceptable to the city.

D.

Unless otherwise approved by the director, a property shall not operate or otherwise use a septic system when such property lies within 400 feet of the city's wastewater system. The 400 feet length shall be measured from the closest point of that property to the point of connection from an existing, active and accessible city main and, generally, route through existing or future streets or, as determined by the department, other areas appropriate for a main. For any septic system installed on a property on or after January 1, 2023, a cleanout and sanitary sewer lateral shall be designed and constructed that complies with adopted standards and enables the property to disconnect from the septic system and connect to a city wastewater main and that cleanout and sanitary sewer lateral must be shown on civil improvement plans for the property that are accepted by, and on file with, the city. If deemed in the best interest of the city, the director may require the owner of such property to abandon all septic systems in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, perform a wastewater main extension and establish wastewater service from the city in accordance with the city's requirements.

E.

Unless otherwise approved by the director, wastewater service must be obtained from the city whenever an undeveloped property initiates development through the city and such property lies within 400 feet of the city's wastewater system. In such instance, a wastewater main extension shall be required and must be made in accordance with the city's requirements.

F.

In such instance where a parcel map is being proposed and offsite improvements are required as a condition of approval of such map, a wastewater main extension shall be required whenever the city's wastewater system lies within the resulting calculation of 400 feet multiplied by either the total number of lots created by recordation of such map of such parcel of land or the maximum number of lots that could be created based on then-current zoning, whichever number of lots is greater. Where consecutive parcel maps are being proposed, a main extension shall be required whenever the city's wastewater system lies within the resulting calculation of 400 feet multiplied by either (1) the total number of lots created by the recordation of the initial and all consecutive parcel maps combined or (2) the maximum number of lots that could be created based on then-current zoning of the parcels of land in the initial and all consecutive parcel maps combined for those parcels of land, whichever number of lots is greater. However, final determination, including application of this requirement, shall be made by the director.

G.

In such instance where a tentative map or planned unit development is being proposed and no city wastewater main exists contiguous to the property, a wastewater main extension shall be required and must be made in accordance with the city's requirements.

H.

Unless otherwise approved by the director, not more than one lot or other parcel of subdivided land shall be served by a single service connection. A single customer shall be responsible for payment of wastewater bills for each such service. Additionally, where the city provides wastewater service to a single lot or other parcel of subdivided land, the same customer shall be responsible for payment of both the water and wastewater bill.

1.

Exception: In the case of a commercial subdivision whereby a single service line or service lines provide service to multiple lots or other parcels of subdivided land, a single customer shall exist in the form of a property owner's association. Said property owner's association shall be responsible for payment of all water and wastewater bills associated with such service(s). Additionally, the subdivision shall record a declaration of covenants, conditions and restrictions (CC&Rs) in the office of the Clark County recorder, which designates that all of the lot owners in the subdivision own an undivided interest in the private water and wastewater facilities, and that all of the lot owners must participate in the cost of the operation and maintenance of such private systems.

I.

Where multiple services are provided to a single lot or other parcel of subdivided land, a single customer shall be responsible for payment of wastewater bills for all such services.

J.

When a wastewater main extension is required, the director reserves the right to dictate the size, length and capacity of such wastewater main. The applicant may apply for partial cost reimbursement through the establishment of a refunding agreement, as outlined in this title and department service rules.

K.

When a connection is made to any main, the main frontage fee is assessed in accordance with this title and department service rules. A minimum charge shall apply to any parcel having less than 60 feet of chargeable frontage.

L.

All wastewater mains and main extensions must be designed and constructed in accordance with the city's adopted standards.

M.

Before a wastewater main, service line, or connection is allowed to be placed into service, it shall be tested to the satisfaction of the city.

N.

The granting of a certificate of occupancy does not relieve the developer of its obligations relative to the construction of the wastewater main extension; nor does it imply that the mains have been properly constructed or accepted by the city.

O.

Upon completion of a wastewater main extension by a customer or subdivider, the customer or subdivider shall furnish the department a valid bill of sale conveying title to the city for such main and appurtenances, to include service lines, rights-of-way, and/or easements. Upon transfer of such title, the city reserves the right to provide direct or indirect service to any customer through the use of such wastewater mains and appurtenances.

P.

The developer is responsible to correct any defects or failures that occur relative to the design and construction of the wastewater main extension, within a period of one year from the date of acceptance of the work by the city. The developer shall, at the developer's own expense, make good such defects and failures and make all replacements and adjustments required, in accordance with adopted standards. All repairs shall be subject to the approval of the city. Furthermore, developer is at no time relieved of any obligation or responsibility it may have by law, including but not limited to damages for latent deficiencies, injury to real or personal property or injury to or wrongful death of a person.

Q.

The developer shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the city, its officers, agents, volunteers, and employees, against and from any and all liability, loss, damage, claims, fines, demands, causes of action, costs, expenses, and judgments of whatsoever nature, including but not limited to reasonable costs of investigation, reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses, all reasonable expert witness fees and expenses, and all court or arbitration or other alternative dispute resolution costs which result from injury to or death of any persons whomsoever, and/or against and from damage to or loss or destruction of property whatsoever when such injury, death, loss, destruction or damage is due to or arises in connection with or as a result of any work done by the developer, its contractors, agents and subcontractors in connection with the construction of the main and/or arises out of or in connection with developer's, or its contractors' and subcontractors' performance or failure to comply with the requirements of this title or the department's service rules.

It shall be prohibited for a person to negligently, recklessly or willfully introduce or cause to be introduced into the city's publicly owned treatment works any pollutant, waste, or hazardous substance which may:

Cause pass through;

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Purpose and policy. The purpose of this chapter is to set forth uniform requirements that protect the public water system from pollution and contamination through a connection to the public water system and to ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local requirements for the protection of public health, safety and welfare. "Contamination" has the meaning ascribed to the term "contamination" in Nevada Administrative Code, as amended, (the "NAC") 445A.65795. "Pollution" has the meaning ascribed to the term "pollution" in NAC 445A.6623.

B.

Scope. The provisions of this chapter shall apply to any person, governmental entity or property owner with a property or premise that has a commercial meter or commercial connection to the public water system, to any property or premise that has a commercial meter or commercial connection to the public water system, and to any backflow prevention assembly company or tester that provides, or wishes to provide, backflow prevention assembly testing in the city. The provisions of section 14.08.020.C shall apply to any person and governmental entity.

C.

Objectives. The objectives of this chapter are to:

1.

Prevent the introduction of pollution or contamination into the public water system;

2.

Regulate connections to the public water system; and

3.

Be a component of the city's cross-connection control program thereby enabling the city to comply with requirements in NAC 445A.67185 to 445A.67255, inclusive.

D.

Administration. Except as otherwise provided, the director shall administer, implement, and enforce the provisions of this chapter. Any powers granted or duties granted to or imposed upon the director or the department may be delegated by the director to other persons acting in the beneficial interest of the city.

E.

Compliance. All provisions of this chapter are subject to compliance procedures as outlined in this title.

F.

Property owner responsibility. If the customer and the property owner(s) are not identical, any reference to customer in this chapter shall also refer to and include the property owner(s). Accordingly, any right, obligation, requirement or prohibition applicable to a customer in this chapter shall also apply to the property owner(s).

(Ord. No. 3737, § 1, 12-15-2020)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

No person shall connect to the public water system unless the department authorizes the connection in advance, that person complies with all requirements in this title applicable to that connection and the city's cross-connection control program and that person protects the public water system from a cross-connection in accordance with all federal, state and local requirements.

B.

After water passes from the public water system through the point of connection, the customer shall ensure that such water does not reverse back into the public water system for any reason, including as a result of backsiphonage or backpresssure. "Backsiphonage" has the meaning ascribed to the term "backsiphonage" in NAC 445A.65615. "Backpressure" has the meaning ascribed to the term "backpresssure" in NAC 445A.6561.

C.

No person shall introduce any pollution or contamination into the public water system.

D.

If the department determines that a backflow prevention assembly or device is required to eliminate an actual or potential unprotected cross-connection between either a new water service or an existing water service and the public water system, the department shall notify the customer in writing that a department-approved backflow prevention assembly or device is required. The type of assembly or device shall be commensurate with the degree of hazard that exists on the property and premise. The department has the right to designate the required type of backflow prevention (including the minimum size, model, type and number of backflow prevention assembly(ies) or device(s)), designate the installation location for the backflow prevention assembly(ies) or device(s), prescribe milestones and milestone deadlines for installation of the backflow prevention assembly(ies) or device(s), and identify the date by when the assembly(ies) or device(s) must be placed into operation. The customer shall cause the backflow prevention assembly or device to be designed and installed in strict compliance with the requirements in that notice, in this chapter and in the city's cross-connection control program.

E.

The customer shall protect the service connection from sewage and reclaimed water with an air gap. "Air gap" has the meaning ascribed to the term "air gap" in NAC 445A.6553.

F.

The customer is responsible for designing and constructing the customer's water system (either a new water service or the retrofit of an existing water service) to accommodate pressure losses attributed to the installation of a backflow prevention assembly(ies) and device(s).

G.

The customer is responsible for ensuring the design, installation, testing, repair, maintenance, and replacement of the backflow prevention assembly(ies) and device(s) are performed at no expense to the city and in compliance with the following:

1.

Chapter 15.20 - Uniform Plumbing Code - of the code;

2.

American Water Works Association (AWWA) M14 manual "Recommended Practice for Backflow Prevention and Cross-Connection Control," as adopted by reference in NAC 445A.6663;

3.

The most recent edition of the University of Southern California (USC) "Manual of Cross-Connection Control," as adopted by reference in NAC 445A.6663, (the "USC Manual of Cross-Connection Control");

4.

Applicable federal, state and local requirements;

5.

The requirements in this chapter; and

6.

The requirements in the city's cross-connection control program.

H.

If at any time a federal, state or local requirement concerning backflow prevention or cross-connection is more stringent than a requirement imposed in this chapter or elsewhere in the city's cross-connection control program, the more restrictive requirement shall govern and the customer must comply, or otherwise be in compliance, with the more restrictive requirement.

(Ord. No. 3737, § 1, 12-15-2020)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

When the department has required the installation of a backflow prevention assembly(ies) or device(s), the customer is responsible for the installation of the assembly(ies) or device(s) at each point of connection on the customer's side of the water meter or the point of connection at the customer's property line, but in all cases, prior to the first branch line leading off the service line.

B.

Installation of the required backflow prevention assembly(ies) shall conform to and be in compliance with the requirements in section 15.70.010 of the code (also referred to as "UDACS"), adopted standards, and NAC chapter 445A.

(Ord. No. 3737, § 1, 12-15-2020)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

The customer shall have all backflow prevention assembly(ies) required under this chapter (1) tested by a person on the list of department-authorized testers and (2) have a test performed at the time of installation, after any maintenance, repair or relocation of the assembly(ies), and annually by the department-assigned anniversary date or more frequently than annually as required by the department pursuant to section 14.08.040.E.

B.

Within five business days after the department-authorized tester completes a test of a backflow prevention assembly after the assembly is installed, maintenance is performed on it, the assembly is repaired or the assembly is relocated, the customer shall ensure the department-authorized tester submits the test report(s) to city staff who administer the city's cross-connection control program ("CCC staff").

C.

Each backflow prevention assembly shall be assigned an anniversary date by the department for the scheduling of annual testing. The annual testing shall be performed in compliance with adopted standards no later than this date and may be performed up to 45 days prior to the department-assigned anniversary date. Any test performed prior to 45 days before the anniversary date will be considered invalid. Before the anniversary date, the customer shall ensure the department-authorized tester submits the test report(s) to CCC staff.

D.

If a backflow prevention assembly(ies) fails testing, then within seven days of failing the testing the customer must cause (1) that assembly to either be repaired with original equipment manufacturer ("OEM") parts or be replaced with a department-approved assembly and (2) the repaired or replaced assembly retested by a department-authorized tester.

E.

The department may, in those instances where the department determines there exists a greater risk of pollution or contamination of the public water system or the then-existing backflow prevention assembly(ies) or device(s) used on the property or premises is not commensurate with the then-existing degree of hazard, require testing more frequently than annually of backflow prevention assemblies.

F.

The department-authorized tester shall comply with the requirements in NAC 445A.67245 and perform the testing of the backflow prevention assembly in accordance with the provisions in the USC Manual of Cross-Connection Control.

G.

The customer shall maintain full and complete records relating to the installation, testing, repair, maintenance, and replacement of all backflow prevention assembly(ies) for a period of five years. The customer shall provide these records to the department or make them available for city inspection upon the city's request.

(Ord. No. 3737, § 1, 12-15-2020)
