A responsible person must not allow water from a water distribution facility, tank, or water feature on the real property water to flow onto, spray onto, pool on, or run off onto (a) non-irrigated or non-landscaped areas on the real property, (b) adjacent real property, or (c) private or public walkways, roadways, pavement, gutters, alleys, parking lots, or structures.

D.

A responsible person must not allow water from a tank or water feature on the real property to pool on an irrigated or landscaped area on the real property.

E.

A responsible person is exempt from the requirements in subsections 14.14.025.A and 14.14.025.B when performing, or causing to be performed, supervised testing. As used in chapter 14.14, "supervised testing" means supervised operation of an irrigation delivery system for testing, repair, adjustment, performance assessment, or efficiency assessment by an individual who is physically present on the real property and observing irrigation-delivery-system performance.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 12, 9-13-2022)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
section_name: Landscape watering restrictions; water budget; possible exemption from landscape watering restrictions for active/programmed recreation turf areas and athletic field turf areas.
citation: 14.14.030 - Landscape watering restrictions; water budget; possible exemption from landscape watering restrictions for active/programmed recreation turf areas and athletic field turf areas.
full_text:
A.

The landscape watering restrictions and schedules in subsections 14.14.030.B and 14.14.030.C apply to all real property in the city's corporate boundaries and to all real property to which the city provides water service. A customer, or the owner or manager of real property, with functional turf that is either active/programmed recreation turf or athletic field turf that meets certain conditions may seek an exemption to those landscape watering restrictions and schedules by following the process in subsection 14.14.030.G.

B.

During the period commencing May 1 and ending August 31, inclusive, of each calendar year, a responsible person must not water lawn grass, a garden, a tree, shrubbery, or other vegetation between the hours of 11:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m.

C.

Water schedule and watering group assignments.

1.

A responsible person must water lawn grass, a garden, a tree, shrubbery, or other vegetation in compliance with the schedule in Table 14.14.030a and the watering group assignment for the service location.

Table 14.14.030a
Water Schedule for Irrigation

Period Day-of-Week Watering
Schedule Restrictions
Winter (November—February) One assigned day per week*
Spring (March—April) Three assigned days per week*
Summer (May—August) Any day, except Sunday
Fall (September—October) Three assigned days per week*
*Days specified for the group by the city.

 

2.

A watering group assignment is based upon the service location, is assigned by the city, and is communicated by the city to each customer.

D.

The following are exemptions to the time-of-day and day-of-week watering schedule restrictions:

1.

Hand-watering using a hand-held container or positive shut-off nozzle for the purpose of preserving lawn grass, a garden, a tree, shrubbery, or other vegetation; and

2.

Irrigating new turf or re-seeding of existing turf, for a period of 30 days from the date of planting or installation, with prior notification to the department customer care center; and

3.

Irrigating newly installed lawn grass or irrigating existing lawn grass being overseeded or re-seeded, for a period of 14 days from the date of installation or date of overseeding/re-seeding, as applicable, provided the responsible person provides prior notification to the department customer care center and any overseeding/re-seeding is performed no more than twice each calendar year; and

4.

Irrigating commercial nursery stock at a commercial garden or plant nursery, provided that the commercial garden or plant nursery has a valid City of Henderson business license and the licensee or their representative is personally present on the real property at the time the irrigation is taking place to monitor the irrigation operation and maintain compliance with section 14.14.025; and

5.

Performing supervised testing.

E.

Each responsible person shall ensure compliance with the time-of-day and day-of-week watering restrictions. The department may require that landscape water distribution facilities be modified in a manner to assure compliance with this chapter. This shall include, but not be limited to, the removal of lawn grass or other non-drought tolerant landscaping, or the addition of metered connections to the irrigation system in order to reduce the timeframes for cycling through all irrigation stations. Where additional metered connections are required, such metered connections shall comply with all requirements in title 14 of the code applicable to a new metered service.

F.

A responsible person shall not use spray irrigation for any purpose other than to irrigate lawn grass.

G.

In addition to or in lieu of any provisions of this section 14.14.030, the department has the right to assign to customers - and a customer, or the owner or manager of the real property receiving water service from the city, may request that the department assign - specific water budgets for any specified period of time and the department may require customers to comply with certain conditions as part of that water budget, including, but not limited to, the amount of water used during a specified period of time, the type of water that can be used, what that water can be used for, compliance with one or more provisions in this section, and automatic or other termination of the water budget. A customer, or the owner or manager of the real property receiving water service from the city, may request that the department assign a water budget by submitting a signed application to the department on such form and in such format as the department shall require and must comply with all requirements in the department's process, such as providing all information required by the department and demonstrating that the customer made a good faith effort to comply with the requirements in this chapter and was not able to before the department assigns that customer a water budget. The department is not required to approve an application for a water budget. If the department grants an exemption, the customer must submit a signed acknowledgment agreeing to comply with all conditions in the water budget, and the department may terminate the exemption if the customer does not comply with all of those conditions. If a customer exceeds their water budget, that customer must pay for the additional volume of water used at the rate(s) in the department service rules and as outlined in this title. The customer must also pay a surcharge for any water used over the annual water budget amount.

H.

Possible exemption from watering restrictions and requirements for an active/programmed recreation turf area or athletic field turf area.

1.

A customer, or the owner or manager of real property, (the "applicant") may request that the department grant an exemption to the landscape watering restrictions and schedules in subsections 14.14.030.B and/or 14.14.030.C for the portion of their real property with functional turf that is either active/programmed recreation turf or athletic field turf, provided the applicant meets the following requirements (each, a "requirement"): (a) there is functional turf located on their real property that is either active/programmed recreation turf or athletic field turf; (b) there is no nonfunctional turf on that real property; (c) there are at least two acres of lawn grass within that active/programmed recreation turf area or athletic field turf area; and, (d) the applicant cannot consistently comply with all watering restrictions and sustain public use due to extraordinary public use of that area or to protect the health, safety, and well-being of the public. If the applicant meets all of the requirements, the applicant must submit a signed application to the department on such form and in such format as the department shall require. The applicant must comply with all requirements in the department's process, such as providing all information required to enable the department to evaluate the application. The department is not required to approve an application for an exemption.

2.

If the department grants an exemption, the department may require the applicant to comply with certain conditions, the applicant must submit a signed acknowledgment agreeing to comply with all conditions, and - for any reason and with 14 calendar days' written notice to the applicant - the department may terminate the exemption or modify one or more of the conditions in the exemption. Conditions in an exemption may include, but are not limited to:

a.

Obtaining and prominently displaying a sign(s) stating that an alternative watering schedule is in use. The city must approve the sign location(s), wording (language, font, and font size), and size.

b.

Submitting to the department for approval a spring and fall watering schedule for each active/programmed recreation turf area and athletic field turf area and adhering to the approved schedule. Scheduled spring and fall watering may not exceed seven days out of 14 consecutive days.

c.

Submitting to the department for approval a winter watering schedule for each active/programmed recreation turf area and athletic field turf area and adhering to the approved schedule. Scheduled winter watering may not exceed two days per week.

d.

Commencing irrigation no earlier than 9:00 p.m. the day prior to the designated day in any department-approved watering schedule for the active/programmed recreation turf area and athletic field turf area.

e.

Posting the watering schedule at the facility.

f.

Preparing a conservation plan that maximizes outdoor water use efficiency and reduces water use (the "CP") for approval by the department, adhering to the approved plan, submitting periodic reports to the department regarding plan execution, including any gaps and process improvements that could be made, and, at the department's request, modifying that CP.

I.

The landscape watering restrictions in section 14.14.030 do not apply to city operations or procedures to the extent variation from such restrictions is necessary to protect the health, safety, and well-being of the public or to preserve city property.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 13, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3413, § 1, 6-6-2017; Ord. No. 2909, § 1, 3-15-2011; Ord. 2798, § 5, 1-20-2009)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Golf courses using or taking water within the city's corporate boundaries, whether or not that water is supplied by city, and golf course customers shall comply with all requirements in this chapter. At the department's written request, a golf course property shall provide the department documentation regarding water used for irrigation on that property.

B.

Golf course properties shall be on a water budget and allocated a maximum of (1) through December 31, 2023, 6.3 acre feet of water (including potable, raw, reclaimed, and other non-potable water) for each irrigated acre, per calendar year and (2) as of January 1, 2024, 4.0 acre feet of water (including potable, raw, reclaimed, and other non-potable water) for each irrigated acre, per calendar year. To enable the city to determine the total amount of water used for irrigation on the golf course property each year, the department, in consultation with the golf course property's authorized representative, shall identify the means for achieving such determination, where such means shall involve commercially reasonable efforts, with the cost for implementation being the responsibility of the golf course. The department, in consultation with the golf course property's authorized representative, shall determine the irrigated acreage of the golf course. That irrigated acreage will include the golf course play turf, lakes and ponds then-existing within a golf course property, lakes and ponds serving, in total or in part, as a golf-course-property irrigation reservoir, and other outdoor areas on the golf course property that are landscaped, irrigated with an irrigation delivery system, and are not occupied by a structure, walkway, roadway, curb, gutter, pavement, or parking lot. The city may periodically review the area comprising the irrigated acreage at a particular golf course.

C.

If a golf course property contests the calculated irrigated acreage determined by the department, the golf course property may provide calculations supported by other methods acceptable to the department. The golf course property may hire an independent consultant, not affiliated with the golf course property, to calculate the irrigated acreage. In any case, however, the department shall make the final determination of the irrigated areas and the irrigated acreage for the golf course property.

D.

A golf course property is limited to the total square feet of the golf course play turf area that existed as of September 19, 2022 and shall not increase the golf course play turf area.

E.

Exemptions for golf courses.

1.

Budgeted water apportionments may be used on the golf course property to syringe golf course greens without time-of-day or day-of-week restrictions, provided (a)(1) one station at a time is run manually or (2) on large irrigation projects, stations are run using hand-held remote irrigation controllers or computerized central controls, and the individual operating the spray irrigation is present to monitor their operation and (b) water does not flow onto, spray onto, pool on, or run off onto a walkway, bike path, pavement, gutter, street, or drain.

2.

Budgeted water apportionments may be used on the golf course property to spray irrigate the golf course play turf without time-of-day or day-of-week restrictions, provided (a) the golf course property and/or golf course customer, as applicable, are in compliance with any and all applicable reclaimed water management plans (formerly referred to as effluent management plans) and reclaimed water use agreements and (b) water does not flow onto, spray onto, pool on, or run off onto a walkway, bike path, pavement, gutter, street, or drain. The foregoing exemption does not apply to other lawn grass or to other landscaped areas within the golf course property.

3.

If a golf course property wishes to re-seed or overseed all or a portion of the golf course play turf, the golf course property must stay within its budgeted water apportionment.

F.

If a golf course property exceeds their water budget, that customer must pay for the additional volume of water used at the rate(s) in the department service rules and as outlined in this title. The golf course property must also pay a surcharge for any water used over the annual water budget amount.

G.

The city will not serve and a responsible person shall not use potable, reclaimed, or raw water provided by the city for a golf course that was not in existence as of September 19, 2022.

(Ord. No. 3946, § 1, 3-7-2023; Ord. No. 3905, § 14, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 2909, § 1, 3-15-2011; Ord. 2798, § 5, 1-20-2009)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

As of September 19, 2022, lawn grass is prohibited in any newly-developed property in the city's corporate boundaries and any newly-developed property that is provided any utility service unless that lawn grass (1) is for a public park, a homeowner association-owned or -managed park approved as a park through the city's development process, a public school, a private school, or a cemetery and (2) is functional turf. The foregoing restrictions take precedence over any exception that allows lawn grass in subsection 14.14.050.B and subsection 14.14.050.C.

B.

Lawn grass is prohibited on all non-residential properties in the city's corporate boundaries and on all non-residential properties that are provided any utility service unless that lawn grass is functional turf. If nonfunctional turf has been installed on such a non-residential property, the owner of the non-residential property has until December 31, 2026 to remove that nonfunctional turf.

C.

The following landscape material restrictions apply to residential properties in the city's corporate boundaries and to residential properties that are provided any utility services:

1.

As of January 1, 2004, lawn grass is prohibited in the front yard of a residential property with a detached single-family residential dwelling unit unless lawn grass was installed in that front yard on or before December 31, 2003. If lawn grass was installed in the front yard on or before December 31, 2003, and on or after January 1, 2004 some or all of that lawn grass is removed or is dead, lawn grass is prohibited and cannot be replaced (or re-seeded) in the front yard except in the areas where the lawn grass was originally installed and, in compliance with subsection 14.14.050.G, and that lawn grass is replaced within one year of being removed and/or is re-seeded within one year, as applicable.

2.

At any residential property with a detached single-family residential dwelling unit for which a building permit for an occupied structure was issued before September 19, 2022, lawn grass is prohibited in the rear yard, in the courtyard(s), and in the side yards unless all of the following conditions are met: (a) the lawn grass area does not exceed 50 percent of the gross area of the rear yard, courtyard, and side yard areas (collectively, the "yard area") or 100 square feet, whichever is greater; (b) no lawn grass area dimension is less than ten feet; (c) the slope of the lawn grass area is less than 25 percent; and (d) the lawn grass area is graded to prevent runoff except in and to the designated drainage area(s). Based on these restrictions, it is possible that lawn grass cannot be installed in a rear yard, courtyard, and/or side yard.

3.

At any residential property with a detached single-unit dwelling for which a building permit for an occupied structure was issued before September 19, 2022 and provided that the property meets all applicable requirements in subsection 14.14.050, (a) as to any lawn grass installed on the property before September 19, 2022, the total lawn grass installed on the property shall not exceed 5,000 square feet, (b) if the total lawn grass installed on the property before September 19, 2022 is greater than 2,500 square feet, additional lawn grass shall not be installed on the property, and (c) if the total lawn grass installed on the property before September 19, 2022 is less than 2,500 square feet, additional lawn grass may be installed on the property up to a maximum of 2,500 square feet of lawn grass in total on the property. At any residential property with a detached single-unit dwelling for which a building permit for an occupied structure was issued on or after September 19, 2022, consistent with subsection 14.14.050.A, lawn grass is prohibited on the property.

4.

At any multifamily and single-family attached residential property in the city's corporate boundaries and at any multi-family and single-family attached residential property that is provided any utility service, lawn grass is prohibited unless it is resident area turf and is functional turf. If nonfunctional turf has been installed on such a residential property, the owner of the residential property has until December 31, 2026 to remove nonfunctional turf.

D.

As of December 9, 2020, if property is located in the out of valley area, then lawn grass may only be installed in a public park, a homeowner association-owned or -managed park approved as a park through the city's development process, a public school, or a private school and that lawn grass must be functional turf. However, the restrictions in the immediately preceding sentence do not apply to a property that, on December 9, 2020, (1) is in the city's corporate boundary and (2) is either (a) in a residential development or within residential zoning, or (b) subject to an approved developer-initiated master plan that includes residential properties. All lawn grass installations in the out of valley area must be in compliance with all applicable requirements in this chapter 14.14.

E.

Use of drought-tolerant landscaping in any landscaped area is encouraged. Other than in the yard area at a residential property with a detached single-family residential dwelling unit for which a building permit for an occupied structure was issued before September 19, 2022, drought-tolerant landscaping shall not be removed from a property for the purpose of installing lawn grass.

F.

Any person(s) or association(s) regardless of date of establishment is prohibited from imposing private covenants, conditions, restrictions, deed clauses or other agreements between the parties that require the installation of lawn grass, prevent the removal of lawn grass or prevent the use of drought-tolerant landscaping. In addition, such person(s) and association(s) may not prohibit landscaping materials and designs solely on the basis that they make use of drought-tolerant landscaping.

G.

In the instance where lawn grass is originally installed in an area in conformance with the code, all or a portion of the lawn grass in that area is dead, and lawn grass would otherwise be prohibited in that area by a provision in section 14.14.050, the lawn grass that is dead may be replaced with lawn grass or re-seeded only if such replacement or re-seeding occurs within one year of that lawn grass being dead. After that one-year period ends, replacement or re-seeding of that dead lawn grass is prohibited and lawn grass is no longer allowed in that area. For the purposes of determining the one-year period for re-seeding or replacement, such determination shall be at the sole discretion of the department.

H.

As used in chapter 14.14:

1.

"Building permit for an occupied structure" means a building permit to newly construct a structure that will be occupied after passing a building final inspection.

2.

"Courtyard" means an area on a residential property with a detached single-family residential dwelling unit that is open to the sky, is not part of the habitable structure, is unobstructed by a structure from the ground upward, and is not the front yard, side yard, or rear yard. An area is still a courtyard even if covered by a shade structure.

3.

"Drought-tolerant landscaping" means a plant that that can be adapted to the desert environment in the Southern Nevada area because it is tolerant of heat, cold and wind, water efficient, low-maintenance, noninvasive, pest and disease resistant, and can survive using (at most) only low-volume, drip irrigation. Examples of drought-tolerant landscaping can be found in the Water Smart Landscapes Program Plant List, as amended, developed by SNWA and Southern Nevada Regional Planning Coalition and are generally identified as "bulletproof" on that list.

4.

"Front yard" means the yard area extending along the entire length of the front property line and the depth between the street right-of-way line and the front façade or façades of the primary structure of a detached single-family residential dwelling unit.

5.

"Newly-developed property" means non-residential property or residential property that is being developed through the construction of a residential, commercial, or industrial structure(s) and that property either was not previously developed or is being redeveloped (i.e. a majority of the structure(s) is being removed or was otherwise destroyed and is being replaced with new construction).

6.

"Non-residential property" means a parcel of real property that does not meet the definition of residential property.

7.

"Rear yard" means the yard area extending along the entire length of the rear property line and the depth between the rear property line and the rear façade or façades of the primary structure of a detached single-family residential dwelling unit.

8.

"Residential property" means a parcel of real property on which a multi-family residential unit (such as apartment building), an attached single-family residential dwelling unit (such as a townhouse or condominium), or a detached single-family residential dwelling unit has been constructed.

9.

"Side yard" means the yard area extending from the front yard to the rear yard and between the side property line and the primary structure of a detached single-family residential dwelling unit.

I.

If all or a portion of lawn grass originally installed on or before December 31, 2026 does not meet the definition of functional turf, the responsible person may apply to SNWA for a waiver of a prohibition in subsection 14.14.050.B. By electronic mail, mail, or other delivery method specified by the department and by the deadline identified by the department, the responsible person shall provide the department: (1) a copy of that waiver application and documentation that shows the application was submitted to SNWA; (2) an update(s) regarding the status of the application; (3) a copy of SNWA's decision on the waiver application and any waiver granted by SNWA; (4) an update(s) regarding the status of any appeal of SNWA's decision on the waiver application; and, (5) a copy of the decision regarding any appeal. The foregoing waiver process does not apply to a residential property with a detached single-family residential dwelling unit. Except for a waiver granted by the SNWA that allows lawn grass where all or a portion of that lawn grass does not meet the definition of functional turf, there shall be no waivers, exemptions, or variances granted to the standards listed in this section 14.14.050 and any such request shall be considered a request to amend the requirements of this section.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 15, 9-13-2022; Ord. 2798, § 5, 1-20-2009; Ord. No. 2951, § 3, 12-20-2011)

full_text:
A.

A mist cooling system on real property in the city's corporate boundaries or on real property to which the city provides water service may only operate March 1 through October 31. In addition, a mist cooling system at a commercial property on such real property may only operate during hours in which the business is open to the public.

B.

Operation of a mist cooling system for animal safety is not restricted.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
section_name: Restrictions on surface, building, equipment, and vehicle washing; splash pads.
citation: 14.14.070 - Restrictions on surface, building, equipment, and vehicle washing; splash pads.
full_text:
A.

Surface, building, and equipment washing.

1.

Surface, building, and equipment washing (excluding motor vehicles) at a non-residential property in the city's corporate boundaries and on real property to which the city provides water service is prohibited unless (a) the water is contained on site (i.e. does not flow off that property) or is discharged to a municipal sewer system that has the ability to treat and discharge that treated water to Lake Mead (the "MSS") through approved methods as determined by the city and (b) there is no violation of any other applicable code requirement, such as a requirement in title 13 of the Code.

A responsible person shall not perform surface or building washing more often than once each calendar month other than to remediate a condition on the property for the protection of public health, safety, or welfare. If the responsible person is remediating a condition, then that responsible person must provide the city documentation of that condition, at the department's request.

2.

If a person performs surface, building, or equipment washing (including motor vehicles) at a residential property in the city's corporate boundaries or on residential property to which the city provides water service, that person must use a positive shut-off nozzle and comply with any other applicable code requirements, such as those in title 13 of the code.

B.

Vehicle washing.

1.

Washing a non-commercial vehicle at a residential property in the city's corporate boundaries or on real property to which the city provides water service is limited to one day per week with the use of a positive shut-off nozzle.

2.

A commercial vehicle may only be washed at a commercial facility (including a commercial car wash business) where water is contained on site or discharged to the MSS through approved methods, as determined by the city, and a high-pressure, low volume sprayer (or spray system) is used.

3.

A commercial car wash business (including mobile and stationary operations) with a valid City of Henderson business license may wash commercial and non-commercial vehicles and must use a high-pressure, low volume sprayer (or spray system) that uses less than ten gallons of water per vehicle.

4.

Charitable car washes performed by a nonprofit group, charity fund raiser, or school group are permissible only when:

a.

High-pressure, low volume sprayers (or spray systems) are used; and

b.

Less than ten gallons of water per vehicle is used; and

c.

Any other applicable code requirements, such as those in title 13, are complied with.

C.

Splash pads.

1.

A splash pad installed or modified after January 1, 2023, may only be operated if it meets the following requirements:

a.

The splash pad is designed and operated in a manner that prevents surface water run-on from the area adjacent to and surrounding the splash pad from entering the MSS; and

b.

The majority of the water dispersed in connection with operation of the splash pad is discharged into the MSS through an approved method (as determined by the city); and

c.

In compliance with any applicable requirement in title 13 and any other applicable code requirement, any other water, including surface water run-on from the area adjacent to and surrounding the splash pad, is diverted to the storm drain system; and

d.

The splash pad automatically shuts off after five minutes; and

e.

When the splash pad is not in use, the splash pad drainage area is covered to prevent stormwater and other substances from entering the MSS; and

f.

The splash pad is located in any of the following: a public park, a recreational water park, a homeowner association-owned or -managed property, a residential property (provided the splash pad is not located in the front yard), a school, a daycare, a recreation center, a senior center, a mixed-use development, a government facility, or a religious institution; and

g.

The method used to discharge splash pad water to the MSS is regularly maintained and replaced as necessary to maintain operational efficiency and pollutants (defined in section 14.09.010) are not discharged to the MSS through that connection.

2.

As used in chapter 14.14, "splash pad" means an outdoor water play area intended for human contact that has potable water typically dispersed by sprinklers, fountains, nozzles, or other devices that spray, mist, or dump that water and that diverts the dispersed water through an approved method (as determined by the city) into the MSS so that the play area is continuously drained and, as a result, has little or no standing water.

(Ord. No. 4062, § 1, 3-4-2025; Ord. No. 3905, § 17, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3413, § 3, 6-6-2017; Ord. 2798, § 5, 1-20-2009)

Editor's note— Ord. No. 3905, § 17, adopted September 13, 2022, changed the title of section 14.14.070 from "Other outdoor water use standards" to "Restrictions on surface, building, equipment, and vehicle washing; splash pads." The historical notation has been preserved for reference purposes.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

A water feature is prohibited on real property in the city's corporate boundaries and on real property to which the city provides water service, unless an exemption in subsection 14.14.080.B applies.

B.

The following water features are exempted from the prohibition in subsection 14.14.080.A:

1.

Swimming pools, spas, and hot tubs, provided, as to any residential property with an attached or a detached single-family residential dwelling unit:

a.

The swimming pool, spa, and/or hot tub is not located in the front yard; and

b.

For any swimming pool, spa, and hot tub issued a permit for construction by the city on or after September 19, 2022, the combined water surface area of the swimming pool, spa, and hot tub does not exceed 600 square feet of surface area of water; and

c.

For any swimming pool, spa, and hot tub issued a permit for construction by the city before September 19, 2022, the combined water surface area of the swimming pool, spa and hot tub cannot be increased beyond the surface area of water in the permit originally approved or beyond 600 square feet, whichever is greater; and

d.

There is at most one swimming pool and one spa or hot tub on that property.

2.

A water feature that is necessary and/or a functional component serving at least one of the following uses:

a.

An irrigation reservoir for a golf course; or

b.

An engineered component of a heat exchanger for a cooling system.

3.

A water feature within a climate-controlled, enclosed structure.

4.

Not including a swimming pool, spa, or hot tub, a single water feature of not more than 25 square feet of surface area of water upon a residential property with an attached or a detached single-family residential dwelling unit. Regardless of depth, a lazy river may be a separate water feature or be part of the swimming pool, spa, or hot tub. As used in chapter 14.14, "lazy river" means a channeled flow of water of near-constant depth in which the water is moved by pumps or other means of propulsion to provide a riverlike flow and is usually found in water parks, hotels, resorts, and recreation centers.

5.

Not including a swimming pool, spa, or hot tub, a single water feature of not more than 25 square feet of surface area of water within a common area of a residential property with a multi-family residential unit, provided that the feature is not located at an entryway to the property.

6.

A water feature that was installed and operating prior to June 9, 2017 or approved or otherwise authorized by the city in a contract with the city in accordance with title 19 of the Code prior to June 9, 2017.

7.

A lazy river in a recreational water park.

8.

Interactive water play features in a city-operated pool or in a privately owned and maintained pool that is open for general community use.

9.

A splash pad.

C.

For purposes of calculating the square feet of surface area of water, the square feet of the surface over which water continuously flows or falls, or is designed to continuously flow or fall, shall be included in the calculation of the surface area.

D.

As used in chapter 14.14, "water feature" means any artificially constructed or installed stream, lazy river, fountain, waterfall, reflective pool, pond, lake, body of water, waterfall, swimming pool, spa, hot tub, or other artificially constructed or installed feature using water that is located outdoors that:

1.

Contains water that flows, is recirculated, or is sprayed into the air; and

2.

Was constructed or is used, in whole or in part, for recreational, cooling-off, decorative, scenic, aesthetic, or landscape purposes.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 18, 9-13-2022)

No. 2798, § 5, adopted January 20, 2009; Ord. No. 2909, § 1, adopted March 15, 2011; Ord. No. 3020, § 1, adopted June 11, 2013, and Ord. No. 3413, §§ 4—6, adopted June 6, 2017.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
section_name: Swimming pool, spa, and hot tub draining.
citation: 14.14.090 - Swimming pool, spa, and hot tub draining.
full_text:
A.

When submitting an application for a swimming pool or spa permit, the applicant must show an onsite sewer lateral cleanout on the plans and that cleanout must be constructed. Except as otherwise provided in subsection B of this section 14.14.090, swimming pool, spa, or hot tub water shall only be discharged into the MSS through a private connection such as a sewer lateral cleanout, sink, toilet, or bathtub.

B.

Exemptions.

1.

Real property that is on a septic system may drain water from a swimming pool, spa, or hot tub into the storm drain system, provided the water is dechlorinated, prior notification has been given to the department's customer care center, and such discharge is permitted by and performed in compliance with title 13 of the Code.

2.

Where there is limited hydraulic capacity in the MSS, real property that is provided wastewater service by the city may drain water from a swimming pool, spa, or hot tub into the storm drain system, provided the water is dechlorinated, such discharge is allowed by and performed in compliance with title 13 of the Code, and such discharge is authorized by the department.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 19, 9-13-2022)

Note— See editor's note at section 14.14.080.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Any recreational water park that is on real property to which the city provides water service or on real property in the city's corporate boundaries and that, after September 19, 2022, changes a use at the recreational water park in relation to water used that requires a city-issued permit, license, or other city authorization must comply with the following:

1.

The recreational water park must submit to the department a water efficiency plan for review within three months of receiving City's approval of that use change, and, at least once annually thereafter, review its water efficiency plan and, as soon as practicable after its review is completed but not later than December 31 of each year, submit the results of its review and any additions or modifications to its water efficiency plan to the department, and incorporate any changes identified by the department into the water efficiency plan. The department must approve the original plan and any additions or modifications. The recreational water park must implement the approved water efficiency plan.

2.

The recreational water park must mitigate water use and, subject to the department's approval, identify methods to mitigate water use in their water efficiency plan. Methods to mitigate water use may include one or more of the following:

a.

Installing and maintaining drought-tolerant landscaping, instead of lawn grass, in the landscaped areas of the recreational water park; and

b.

Instituting measures to prevent water loss at water play areas at the recreational water park.

B.

As used in chapter 14.14:

1.

"Recreational water park" means a commercial amusement park with any combination of water play areas intended for human contact such as pools, water slides, splash pads, lazy rivers, artificial surfing, artificial bodyboarding, and/or water playgrounds, as well as areas for floating, wading, or swimming.

2.

"Water efficiency plan" means a comprehensive plan conforming to department guidelines that contains information related to a development's consumptive and non-consumptive water demand projections. The plan may include a summary of indoor and outdoor water uses, a description of water fixtures and appliances, cooling systems, misting systems and other water dependent applications, a summary of efficiency measures proposed on site, and methods to mitigate water use.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 20, 9-13-2022)

Note— See editor's note at section 14.14.080.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

As of September 19, 2022, an artificial lake is prohibited on real property in the city's corporate boundaries and on real property to which the city provides water service, unless an exemption in subsection 14.14.110.B applies.

B.

The following are exempted from the prohibition in subsection 14.14.110.A:

1.

An artificial lake that was installed and operating prior to June 9, 2017.

2.

An artificial lake that was approved or otherwise authorized by the city in a contract with city in accordance with title 19 of the Code prior to June 9, 2017.

3.

An artificial lake located on a golf course that is used for the purpose of storing irrigation water for the irrigated acreage at the golf course in conformance with section 14.14.040.

C.

As used in chapter 14.14, "artificial lake" means an outdoor body of water that is artificially constructed or installed, is privately owned, is used in whole or in part for a recreational, scenic, aesthetic, or landscape purpose, and is filled, or refilled, with potable water or non-potable water from any source, including lakes, ponds, lagoons, and reservoirs but excluding tank-type reservoirs that are fully enclosed and contained. The term "artificial lake" does not include a water feature or a recreational water park.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 21, 9-13-2022)

Note— See editor's note at section 14.14.080.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

The department is authorized to draft, modify, implement, and enforce a drought response plan. The department shall make that drought response plan publicly available on the city's website.

B.

All responsible persons shall comply with the requirements in that drought response plan.

C.

As used in chapter 14.14, "drought response plan" means a plan to mitigate the impacts of drought or low Lake Mead water level conditions by requiring customers to reduce, limit, or curtail their demand for and use of city-supplied water generally or through specific types of action (such as not filling a water feature), by prioritizing uses by different customers, and by prohibiting water use.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 22, 9-13-2022)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
section_name: Water use restriction in deed or other written instrument recorded against real property.
citation: 14.14.130 - Water use restriction in deed or other written instrument recorded against real property.
full_text:
An owner, and any lessee, renter, or occupant, of real property shall comply with all restrictions in a deed or other written instrument that limits, restricts, prohibits, or prescribes particular water use or landscaping materials at that real property, provided that the deed or other written instrument containing the restriction(s) is recorded against that real property in the office of the county recorder of Clark County, Nevada.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 23, 9-13-2022)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
Any person who commits an act or refuses to correct a condition that is not in compliance with a requirement in this chapter as set forth in any section above, and any responsible person who violates this chapter as set forth below, is subject to discontinuance of service, subject to any penalties and charges assessed in accordance with this title and/or department service rules, and subject to all compliance procedures as prescribed within this title. It is a violation of this chapter for a responsible person to commit water waste and/or allow water waste to occur on real property that the responsible person controls, has a property interest in or maintains by:

A.

Allowing the loss, escape, or excess use of water through a break, leak or other malfunction in the water distribution facilities on the real property for any period of time after such escape of water should have been reasonably discovered as determined by the department.

B.

Failing to repair a break, leak, or other malfunction in the water distribution facilities on the real property within 120 hours of knowing, or being notified, of the malfunction or by the deadline set by the city, whichever date is later.

C.

Allowing water from a water distribution facility, tank, or water feature on the real property water to flow onto, spray onto, pool on, or run off onto (1) non-irrigated or non-landscaped areas on the real property, (2) adjacent real property, or (3) private or public walkways, roadways, pavement, gutters, alleys, parking lots, or structures.

D.

Allowing water from a tank or water feature on the real property to pool on an irrigated or landscaped area on the real property.

E.

Watering lawn grass, a garden, a tree, shrubbery, or other vegetation at a time prohibited unless an exemption in section 14.14.030 or section 14.14.040 applies.

F.

Watering lawn grass, a garden, a tree, shrubbery, or other vegetation on a day that is not a day in the watering group assignment for the real property or service location unless an exemption in section 14.14.030 or section 14.14.040 applies.

G.

Using spray irrigation for any purpose other than to irrigate lawn grass.

H.

Failing to comply with a requirement in a water budget.

I.

Using landscaping materials other than as allowed in section 14.14.050 and/or imposing landscaping requirements that do not comply with the requirements in section 14.14.050.

J.

Using a mist cooling system at a time or on a day other than as allowed in section 14.14.060.

K.

Using water to perform surface, building, equipment, or vehicle washing other than as allowed in section 14.14.070.

L.

Failing to operate a splash pad installed or modified after January 1, 2023 in compliance with section 14.14.070.

M.

Having a water feature unless an exemption in subsection 14.14.080.B applies.

N.

Draining or emptying any water from a swimming pool, spa, or hot tub water into any component of the storm drain system other than as allowed in section 14.14.090.

O.

Failing, as a recreational water park, to comply with the requirements in section 14.14.100.

P.

Having an artificial lake unless an exemption in subsection 14.14.110.B applies.

Q.

Failing to comply with a requirement in the drought response plan.

R.

Failing to comply with a restriction in a deed or other written instrument that limits, restricts, prohibits, or prescribes particular water use or landscaping materials on real property, provided that the deed or other written instrument containing the restriction(s) is recorded against that real property in the Office of the County Recorder of Clark County, Nevada.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 24, 9-13-2022)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Purpose and policy. This chapter sets forth responsibility, authority, and provisions to provide a mechanism for the orderly development of the utility system through refunding of costs associated with the design and construction of utility infrastructure.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Standard refunding agreements.

1.

The city may enter into an agreement which provides for repayment of a portion of the cost of the main extension lying between the original point of supply and the customer's property from main frontage fees collected from other properties frontage to the main extension covered by such agreement during the term provided in the agreement or until the amount advanced by the customer has been satisfied, as determined in accordance with the provisions of this title and/or the department's service rules.

2.

The following items may be eligible for standard refunding:

a.

Water, sewer, and reclaimed water main extensions to a project;

b.

Water, sewer, and reclaimed water main extensions adjacent to a project; and/or

c.

Water, sewer, and reclaimed water mains replacing existing mains.

3.

The period during which refunds are due shall be 20 years, commencing on the date when the infrastructure covered by the agreement is completed, tested, and accepted by the city.

4.

Construction shall be deemed to be complete when the utility infrastructure is constructed according to the approved plans and satisfies all applicable testing and acceptance criteria.

5.

The city council shall grant the director the authority to enter into and execute any standard refunding agreement in which the city is not a participant. Should the city be a participant in a standard refunding agreement, such agreement must be approved according to city standard operating procedures and policies.

B.

Standard refunding conditions.

1.

Application for standard refunding agreement shall be submitted to the department in writing accompanied by documentation as required by the city from customer(s) constructing such infrastructure covered by the agreement. This application shall be submitted within 90 days of date of acceptance by the city of the infrastructure to be covered by such agreement.

2.

All customers entering into any refunding agreement with the city shall pay all fees as outlined in this title and/or the department service rules. These fees are due and payable at the time of the execution of the agreement.

3.

Customers may be eligible for a refund of main frontage fees collected by the city from other properties in accordance with this title.

4.

All standard refunding calculations shall be rounded to the nearest foot and shall be assessed based on the frontage of the applicant's property, as indicated by the most current data in the Clark County assessor office records, adjacent to the right-of-way or easement where the existing water, sewer, or reclaimed water main is located in accordance with this title and/or the department's service rules.

5.

After execution of a valid standard refunding agreement, all main frontage fees collected in accordance with this title and/or department service rules shall be paid within 60 days from the date of collection.

6.

In the event any expense is incurred by the city within a period of one year after acceptance of the infrastructure installed by the customer covered by a standard refunding agreement due to defective materials or workmanship the amount of such expense shall be deducted from any refund(s) that may become due to the customer thereafter.

(Ord. 2536, § 87, 2006)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Special refunding agreements.

1.

The city may enter into a special refunding agreement which provides for repayment of a portion of the cost of that backbone infrastructure lying between the original point of supply and the customer's property from special refunding fees to be collected by the city from other customers obtaining direct or indirect service from the backbone infrastructure during the term provided in the special refunding agreement, pursuant to this title, or until the proportional cost of design and construction advanced by the customer has been repaid, whichever is earlier.

2.

Any special refunding agreement entered into by the city must be based upon a refunding report completed in accordance with the department service rules and adopted by the city council.

3.

The term of any special refunding agreement shall be 20 years, which will commence on the date the infrastructure covered by the special refunding agreement is completed, tested and accepted by the city.

4.

Application for special refunding agreement shall be submitted to the director in writing accompanied by documentation as required by the city within 90 days of the date of acceptance of the pre-design report by the city for the infrastructure to be covered by such agreement. All final costs are subject to verification by the city.

5.

The amount subject to repayment under a special refunding agreement shall be the amount of the actual cost of the work as verified by the city. The final cost of the work shall be the basis for the determination and calculation of refunds under the special refunding agreement. Final costs that are eligible for inclusion in the special refunding agreement are:

a.

Actual construction costs (including administration and safety and traffic control measures);

b.

Design engineering costs and inspection costs not to exceed an aggregate 15 percent of item 5 of this section;

c.

Permits and fees;

d.

Performance and related bond costs to the extent not included in item 5 of this section;

e.

Actual financing costs related to subsections (A)(5)(a) through (A)(5)(d) of this section. Said financing costs shall be computed through the date of final acceptance of the backbone infrastructure by the city; and

f.

All fees and expenses reasonably incurred concerning the preparation of the special refunding agreement shall be added to the refunding amount.

6.

Construction shall be deemed to be complete when the utility infrastructure is constructed according to the approved plans and satisfies all applicable testing and approval criteria.

B.

Special refunding conditions.

1.

Customers entering into any special refunding agreement with the city shall pay all fees as outlined in this title and/or the department service rules. These fees are due and payable upon execution of the agreement.

2.

After execution of a valid special refunding agreement, special refunding fees collected in accordance with this title and/or department service rules shall be paid to the customer within 30 days from the last business day of the quarter in which such fees were collected and will be issued in accordance to the procedures outlined in the department service rules.

3.

Special refunding fees collected by the city shall be computed as follows:

a.

As to the portion of cost attributable to the holder of the special refunding agreement, advances shall be accrued quarterly with interest equal to one-fourth the prime rate plus two percentage points with a maximum of ten percent per year. The prime rate that is published in the Wall Street Journal or a similar publication approved by the city's finance director for utilization in the refunding report and being the prime rate published at the last business day of each calendar quarter for the subsequent quarter.

b.

As to the portion of cost attributable to city, advances shall be accrued quarterly with interest equal to one-fourth the Merrill Lynch Bond Index for tax-exempt 30-year A-rated revenue bonds as printed in the Wall Street Journal or a similar publication approved by the city's finance director for utilization in the refunding report with a maximum of ten percent per year. The rate shall be based upon the index rate published the last business day of each calendar quarter for the subsequent quarter.

c.

The amount that makes up the actual final cost of work shall be depreciated annually over 40 years using the straight-line method of depreciation or such time line as recommended and approved in the refunding report. The net book value of the infrastructure shall become the base for purposes of calculating amounts to be refunded and of computing the addition of accrued interest.

4.

Special refunding fees, as allocated in the refunding report to a customer, will only be made for utility infrastructure that service areas not only of the customers but areas designated in the approved refunding report.

5.

Special refunding fees will be made from fees collected from other customers or the city whose properties are served by the backbone infrastructure and paid prior to final issuance of a certificate of occupancy.

6.

In the event two or more customers have designed the same backbone infrastructure, those eligible costs, or an applicable portion thereof, paid by the customer who has submitted a performance bond to the city for construction of the relevant system or facility and has completed said construction shall be refunded.

7.

In the event any expense is incurred by the city within a period of one year after acceptance of the infrastructure installed by the customer covered by a special refunding agreement due to defective materials or workmanship on, the amount of such expense shall be deducted from any refund(s) that may become due to the customer thereafter.

(Ord. 2676, § 11 (part), 2008; Ord. 2536, § 88, 2006)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Applications for service.

1.

The property owner or owner's representative shall make application to the department and obtain approval from the city prior to connection to or use of a permanent and/or temporary service. The applicant shall agree to pay for all services used and to abide by all rules and regulations of the city, this title, and the department service rules. Applications for temporary service shall be renewed on an annual basis.

2.

The city reserves the right to refuse any request for utility service from any applicant for any of the following reasons:

a.

An account in their name at the same or any other location is delinquent;

b.

The applicant fails to provide any and all requested information;

c.

When the department determines that the purpose of the request is to circumvent discontinuance of service in another name because of non-payment of bill(s), fees, fines, reimbursements or other charges owed to the utility or other violations of the regulations; and/or

d.

When the department determines that the applicant has failed to comply with any provisions of this title.

3.

A single customer shall be responsible for payment of utility bills for each service connection. When more than one building or parcel of land is served by a single service connection, a single customer must be responsible for payment of the utility bill.

4.

The city is not responsible for damage to customer's property and/or piping due to activation of service. Customer shall ensure piping is in good repair and that all interior and exterior fixtures are in the "off" position prior to requesting activation of water service.

(Ord. No. 3023, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. 2536, § 92, 2006)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

A customer desiring to discontinue service shall provide advance notice to the department and provide a mailing address to which the closing bill shall be mailed. Service and charges will cease as of the discontinuance date provided.

B.

Failure to notify the department of discontinuance of service shall not relieve the customer of responsibility for payment of any existing billings, or any charges due prior to notifying the department.

C.

The city reserves the right to discontinue service if there is running and/or leaking water on the customer's property during service activation.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Meters shall be read monthly or as reasonably possible.

B.

Customers are responsible for payment of all water that passes through the meter, regardless of whether such water was put to beneficial use.

C.

Should a meter be inaccessible at the time of regular reading time, or should it be found to be stuck or damaged so that a reading cannot be obtained, or in cases of emergency as the city deems necessary, the city reserves the right to estimate the water consumption for the billing period and to compute the charges on the basis of the estimated consumption. Should the city determine that a succeeding reading indicates a material error in the estimated reading, an appropriate adjustment shall be made.

D.

Meter accuracy shall be maintained to the fullest extent practicable for any meter installed within the city's service area. If there is a dispute, the city may test the meter using the procedures identified in department service rules.

E.

At the customer's request, a meter testing fee as outlined in the department service rules will be charged to the customer and the meter will be tested. If the meter is found to register more or less than the actual water flow, the city will, as reasonably practical, make the appropriate billing adjustment. Additionally, if the meter is found to register more than the actual water flow, the meter testing fee will be returned to the customer.

(Ord. 2536, § 94, 2006)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

The city shall establish regular billing periods subject to adjustment at the city's discretion.

B.

Failure to receive or accept a bill does not relieve a customer of liability for payment of such bill.

C.

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Bills shall be due and payable upon the applicable due date. When any bill becomes delinquent, the city may discontinue utility service pursuant to notification and termination procedures. Utility service may not be re-established until the delinquent bill and/or all succeeding bills which may have become due, and any applicable charges have been paid.

B.

Should any customer fail or refuse to pay for service furnished and charged for in accordance with this title, the city may not provide service to the customer at the same or any other location until all delinquent utility bills, applicable fees and charges have been paid.

C.

Until paid, all fees, rates, and charges imposed by title 14 for water service, wastewater service, reclaimed water service, raw water service, or any combination of those services, shall constitute a debt owing to the city by the customer of record and by the owner of such property as shown on the records of the county assessor, if such record owner is someone other than the customer of record. Under subsection 2.280.1(c) of the Charter, such delinquent fees, rates, and charges shall be a lien upon the property to which the service is rendered.

1.

The city may collect such delinquent fees, rates, and charges (a) in accordance with NRS 268.043 by having them collected at the same time as, together with and not separately from, Clark County's general taxes by having the city through a designee in its department comply with the requirements in NRS 268.043.1; (b) by perfecting the city's lien upon the property to which service is rendered by filing/recording in the office of the county recorder a notice of lien signed by the city clerk, or the city clerk's designee, that identifies the amount due and unpaid, the name of the record owner(s) of the property, and a description of the real property subject to the lien; (c) through a collection agency, as defined in NRS Chapter 649; (d) directly; (e) through a civil action in any court of competent jurisdiction; and/or (f) through any other means available to the city under applicable law.

2.

If the city chooses to collect such delinquent fees, rates, and charges under subsection 1(a) of this section, the city shall have the right to collect all penalties allowable under NRS 268.043 and NRS 361.483.7 from the owner(s) of the real property with respect to which the fees, rates, and charges are delinquent at the time such delinquencies became a lien against that property.

3.

If the city chooses to collect such delinquent fees, rates, and charges under subsection 1(b) of this section, no notice of lien shall be recorded against the property by the city unless written notice of the delinquency has been mailed or personally delivered to the record owner of the property at the last mailing address shown by the records of the county assessor and the record owner of the property has been given 15 days to pay the delinquent amount in full. If there is more than one record owner, failure to send a copy of that notice to a particular owner does not invalidate a notice if properly sent to another record owner. An error or mistake in the name of the record owner contained in any notice of lien does not defeat the lien, unless a correction of the notice of lien in a particular instance would prejudice the rights of an innocent bona fide purchaser or encumbrancer for value, but then only with respect to the bona fide purchaser or encumbrancer for value who was prejudiced. The owner(s) of record and/or customer(s) of record must pay the city a service charge, in an amount approved by city council and identified in the department service rules, for a release of the lien filed with the office of the county recorder and any and all recording costs incurred by the city in recording the release of lien. After the delinquency is fully satisfied or discharged, at the written request of the owner(s) of record or customer(s) of record, and after that owner or customer pays the required fees, the city will cause to be recorded a notice of discharge or release of the notice of lien. After recording the required notice of lien and unless the delinquency is fully satisfied or discharged, the city may foreclose said lien against such property by following the process identified in NRS 108.239, as amended, for the foreclosure of mechanic's liens. Pursuant to section 2.280.1 of the Charter, the lien is coequal with the latest lien thereon to secure the payment of general taxes, the lien is not subject to extinguishment by the sale of any property on account of the nonpayment of general taxes, and the lien is prior and superior to all liens, claims, encumbrances and titles other than the liens of assessments and general taxes. The lien is not extinguished if the city does not commence a foreclosure action.

D.

When a customer receiving service at multiple locations allows a bill for one or more locations to become delinquent, and the service for which the bill is delinquent is shut off, then all of the other service locations may be shut off and subject to all applicable fees and charges in accordance with this title and department service rules.

E.

When a customer's utility bill is not paid in full on or before the due date, it will be considered delinquent in accordance with the provisions of this title and any and all charges shall be subject to the assessment of late charges as established in the department service rules.

(Ord. No. 3442, § 1, 9-19-2017; Ord. No. 2909, § 2, 3-15-2011; Ord. 2536, § 96, 2006)

full_text:
A.

Per article II, section 2.280(c) of the Henderson City Charter, the Henderson city council shall fix charges and rates for water and wastewater services.

B.

Fees, rates and charges shall be billed in accordance with this title and shall be applied as outlined in this title and the department service rules.

C.

Final determination of a customer's use or billing category shall be made by the director. All applicable fees and charges shall be assessed accordingly.

D.

The assessment and collection of all fees and charges shall be made in accordance with the established procedures of the city, relative to the assessment and collection of those fees and charges. Notwithstanding this requirement, the director reserves the right to determine the manner through which all fees and charges are collected.

E.

All fees and charges shall be paid to the city prior to issuance of the certificate of occupancy.

F.

Basic service and usage charges.

1.

Service connections shall be considered in use and appropriate charges shall be assessed commencing with the date of installation unless the customer has provided advance notice that the connection shall not be used until such time as it is needed. If the customer has provided such advance notice, charges shall commence on the date the service is first turned on by the city.

2.

Any service turned on without advance authorization from the city shall be assessed charges based on the date of installation in addition to any other charges or fees.

3.

Charges for usage shall be based upon the volume of flow based upon either readings from city approved water meters, approved wastewater flow monitoring equipment or other methods that may be approved by the city.

4.

All users shall be charged a monthly basic service charge in addition to any monthly usage charges accrued.

5.

Exemptions from basic monthly water and sewer service charge.

a.

Upon application to the department, a low-income or permanently disabled person may have their own private residential account exempted from all or a portion of the basic monthly water and sewer service charge, as determined by the department, by qualifying in accordance with the Nevada Energy Assistance Program, or similar program criteria as established by the department.

b.

All customers who received an exemption based on income must re-qualify annually to continue receiving that exemption and provide information required by the department to support that exemption.

c.

Residents who are senior citizens, received the senior exemption on or before November 1, 1996, and have not changed their place of residence from the residence they were in as of the date they began receiving the senior exemption continue to be eligible to receive an exemption from the basic monthly water and sewer service charge until such time as the customer changes their place of residence.

d.

The applicant shall furnish such information as the city may require, supporting their application for an exemption.

G.

The city reserves the right to inspect any facility to determine the actual equivalent residential units (ERUs) being contributed to the collection system. Additional sewer system development charges and regional fees may be assessed as a result of the findings. Fees will be based on the current rate in place at the time of verification. Regional fees will be charged if applicable at the time of permit issuance.

(Ord. No. 3831, § 1, 1-4-2022; Ord. No. 2951, § 4, 12-20-2011; Ord. 2798, § 6, 1-20-2009; Ord. 2536, § 101, 2006)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
section_name: West Henderson 2630/2760 PZ water backbone infrastructure rates.
citation: 14.18.045 - West Henderson 2630/2760 PZ water backbone infrastructure rates.
full_text:
A.

Planning and design of water backbone infrastructure for the West Henderson 2630 Pressure Zone and the West Henderson 2760 Pressure Zone, construction of that infrastructure, and financing of that construction are required to support water service to existing and future developments in the West Henderson area. The director has the right to determine the size and capacity of the water backbone infrastructure, timing of construction of the water backbone infrastructure, and method of financing the construction, taking into account projected service needs of the West Henderson area served and the need for the orderly and efficient development of the city's public infrastructure system. The West Henderson 2630 Pressure Zone ("2630 PZ") and the West Henderson 2760 Pressure Zone ("2760 PZ") are located in West Henderson. A depiction of the 2630 PZ and the 2760 PZ is available on the city's website.

B.

Through December 31, 2022, the rate charged to projects that the city determines will receive a benefit from the water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for (1) a portion of the 2630 PZ is referred to as the "phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate" and (2) a portion of the 2760 PZ is referred to as the "phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate." These rates are addressed in this section 14.18.045. The amount charged for the phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate (collectively, "phase 1A 2630/2760 PZ rates") shall be in addition to system development, regional connection, and other applicable charges for water service.

C.

Effective January 1, 2023, the rate charged to projects that the city determines will receive a benefit from the water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for (1) a portion of the 2630 PZ is referred to as the "WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate" and (2) a portion of the 2760 PZ is referred to as the "WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate." These rates are addressed in this section 14.18.045. The amount charged for the WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate (collectively, "WH 2630/2760 PZ rates") shall be in addition to system development, regional connection, and other applicable charges for water service.

D.

Effective January 1, 2023, all new projects that the city determines will receive a benefit from existing or future water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for the 2630 PZ or for the 2760 PZ shall be charged and pay the WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and/or the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate, as the city determines is appropriate. The amount(s) charged shall be based upon the total EDUs proposed for the project, as reflected in the civil improvement plans for the project approved by the city, and the rate(s) used will be the one(s) in effect on the date the city processes the building permit for the project or, if a project is not required to obtain a building permit from the city, at the rate in effect on the date the city approves the civil improvement plans for the project.

E.

Any project that was initiated at the city before January 1, 2023, and either was required to pay the rate(s) established (or other amount charged by the city) for existing or future water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for the 2630 PZ or for the 2760 PZ or whose approval was conditioned on the city being paid such rate(s) shall be charged and pay, as the city determines is appropriate, (1) if the building permit is issued prior to January 1, 2023, the phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and/or the phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate or (2) if the building permit is issued on or after January 1, 2023, the WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and/or the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate. The amount(s) charged shall be based upon the total EDUs proposed for the project, as reflected in the civil improvement plans for the project approved by the city, and the rate(s) used will be the one(s) in effect on the date the city processes the building permit for the project or, if a project is not required to obtain a building permit from the city, at the rate in effect on the date the city approves the civil improvement plans for the project.

F.

All projects that proceed with additional improvements to a property that result in an increase in water usage above the usage previously proposed - as reflected in the civil improvement plans approved by the city, in the building permit issued by the city, or by other means of receiving official city approval for such additional improvements (each, a "city approval") - and that the department determines will receive a benefit from existing or future water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for the 2630 PZ or for the 2760 PZ shall be charged and pay, as the department determines is appropriate, (1) if the city approval is issued prior to January 1, 2023, the phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, and/or phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate and (2) if the city approval is issued on or after January 1, 2023, the WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and/or the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate. Whether there is an increase in water usage shall be determined by the director in their sole discretion. The rate(s) charged shall be based upon the increase in total additional EDUs associated with the property improvements and at the rate in effect on the date the city processes the building permit for the proposed improvements or, if a project is not required to obtain a building permit from the city, at the rate in effect on the date the city approves the civil improvement plans for the proposed improvements or provides its approval of the additional improvements by other means.

G.

As provided for in this title, equivalent dwelling unit (EDU) is defined as "a measure of water demand equivalent to the amount of water used annually by an average single-family residential dwelling unit. One EDU is equivalent to 0.55 acre-feet of water per year." For the purpose of calculating the total EDUs attributable to each project being assessed a rate under this section 14.18.045, the EDU calculation table in subsection 14.18.045.L shall apply. However, where it is determined by the director that the "EDU Calculation Factor" or "EDU %" reflected in that table does not adequately reflect the water demands placed upon the city's water system by a proposed project, then the city shall not use that table and instead shall use an alternate method in order to determine the appropriate amount to charge that project for its equitable share of the water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for 2630/2760 PZ. Final determination of such alternate method shall be made by the director.

H.

The phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate shall be $3,067.00 per EDU, and the phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate shall be $5,145.00 per EDU. The initial WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate shall be $3,527.00 per EDU, and the initial WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate shall be $5,660.00 per EDU. These rates are based upon actual and estimated costs for the city to fund the planning, design, construction, and/or financing of the water infrastructure for the 2630 PZ and the 2760 PZ. The city manager may adjust the WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and/or the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate once each calendar year by an amount that (1) for the WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, is no more than 15 percent of the WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate in effect in the immediately preceding period; and (2) for the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate, is no more than ten percent of the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate in effect in the immediately preceding period. The city will identify the phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, the phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate, the then-current WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, and the then-current WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate in the department service rules. Unless otherwise approved in writing by the director in their sole discretion, the rate(s) assessed shall be paid to the city when the city issues a building permit, prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy, or prior to commencement of temporary or permanent water service, whichever date is earliest.

I.

For five years after a certificate of occupancy is issued for a project or an improvement is made to a project, the city has the right to audit that project to confirm that the project's average annual water usage is substantially the same as the total EDUs proposed for the project or project improvement. If the city determines the project is using more EDUs than proposed, the city may require the original developer of the project or project improvement, as applicable, to pay the difference between the total EDUs charged the project and total EDUs actually used at the property at the phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate, WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, and/or WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate, as appropriate, in effect on the date the city prepares a bill for the additional payment.

J.

If the phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate, WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, or the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate is adjusted after the city receives a payment, the city is not obligated to true-up the payment received or to refund/collect any difference.

K.

If a customer requests to design, construct, and pay for all or a portion of the WH water backbone water infrastructure for the 2630 PZ and/or for the 2760 PZ, the city may enter into a special refunding agreement acceptable to the city and in accordance with applicable provisions in section 14.16.050 that provides for repayment of a portion of those costs from WH rates collected, or to be collected, by the city from customers that will receive a benefit from existing or future water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for the 2630 PZ or for the 2760 PZ.
