title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
section_name: West Henderson-Bermuda wastewater backbone infrastructure rates.
citation: 14.18.047 - West Henderson-Bermuda wastewater backbone infrastructure rates.
full_text:
A.

Planning and design of wastewater backbone infrastructure for West Henderson, construction of that infrastructure, financing of that construction, and phasing of that construction are required to support wastewater service to existing and future developments in the West Henderson area. The director has the right to determine the size and capacity of that wastewater backbone infrastructure, phasing of construction of that wastewater backbone infrastructure, and method of financing the construction, taking into account projected service needs of the West Henderson area served and the need for the orderly and efficient development of the publicly-owned treatment works.

B.

The rates charged to projects that the city determines will receive a benefit from segment 1, segment 2, segment 3 or segment 9 of the wastewater backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for the Bermuda Sewer Basin within West Henderson are referred to as the "segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate," "segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate," "segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate" and "segment 9 wastewater infrastructure rate," respectively, and, collectively, as the "WH-Bermuda backbone wastewater infrastructure rates." The WH-Bermuda wastewater backbone infrastructure rates shall be in addition to system development and other applicable charges for wastewater service.

C.

Effective November 25, 2019, all new projects that the city determines will receive a benefit from existing or future wastewater backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for the Bermuda Sewer Basin within West Henderson shall be charged and pay the segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate and/or the segment 9 wastewater infrastructure rate, as the city determines is appropriate. The amount(s) charged shall be based upon the total ERUs proposed for the project, as reflected in the civil improvement plans for the project approved by the city, and the rate(s) used will be the one(s) in effect on the date the city processes the building permit for the project or, if a project is not required to obtain a building permit from the city, at the rate in effect on the date the city approves the civil improvement plans for the project.

D.

Any project that was initiated at the city before November 25, 2019 and whose approval was conditioned on the city being paid the rate(s) established or other amount charged by the city for existing or future wastewater backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for West Henderson shall be charged and pay the segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate and/or the segment 9 wastewater infrastructure rate, as the city determines is appropriate. The amount(s) charged shall be based upon the total ERUs proposed for the project, as reflected in the civil improvement plans for the project approved by the city, and the rate(s) used will be the one(s) in effect on the date the city processes the building permit for the project or November 25, 2019, whichever is later.

E.

Effective November 25, 2019, all projects that proceed with additional improvements to a property that result or might result in an increase in the amount of wastewater discharged to the publicly owned treatment works above that previously proposed - as reflected in the civil improvement plans, in the building permit or by other means of receiving city approval for such additional improvements - and that the city determines will receive a benefit from existing or future wastewater backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for West Henderson shall be charged and pay the segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate and/or the segment 9 wastewater infrastructure rate, as the city determines is appropriate. Whether the improvements result or might result in an increase in the amount wastewater discharged to the publicly-owned treatment works above that previously proposed shall be determined by the director in his or her sole discretion. The rate(s) charged shall be based upon the increase in total additional ERUs associated with the property improvements and at the rate in effect on the date the city processes the building permit for the proposed improvements or, if a project is not required to obtain a building permit from the city, at the rate in effect on the date the city approves the civil improvement plans for the proposed improvements or provides its approval of the additional improvements by other means.

F.

The initial segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate shall be $31.52 per ERU. The initial segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate shall be $79.45 per ERU. The initial segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate shall be $131.39 per ERU. The initial segment 9 wastewater infrastructure rate shall be $270.83 per ERU. Initially, these rates have been based upon actual and estimated costs for the city to fund the planning, design, construction, and/or financing of the West Henderson wastewater backbone infrastructure. After construction of the particular segment is completed, the city manager may adjust the rate for that segment to reflect the actual costs to plan, design, construct, and finance the West Henderson wastewater backbone infrastructure in that segment. The city will identify the then-current segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate and/or the segment 9 wastewater infrastructure rate in the department service rules. Unless otherwise approved in writing by the director at his or her sole discretion, the rate(s) assessed shall be paid to the city when the city issues a building permit, prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy or prior to commencement of permanent wastewater service, whichever is earliest.

G.

For five years after a certificate of occupancy is issued for a project or an improvement is made to a project, the city has the right to audit that project to confirm that the project's average annual wastewater discharge to the publicly owned treatment works is substantially the same as the total ERUs proposed for the project or project improvement. If the city determines the project is using more capacity of the West Henderson wastewater backbone infrastructure than proposed, the city may require the original developer of the project or project improvement, as applicable, to pay the difference between the total ERUs charged the project and total ERUs actually used at the property at the segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate and/or the segment 9 wastewater infrastructure rate, as appropriate, in effect on the date the city prepares a bill for the additional payment.

H.

If the segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate or the segment 9 wastewater infrastructure rate is adjusted after the city receives a payment, the city is not obligated to true-up the payment received or to refund/collect any difference.

(Ord. No. 3638, § 2, 11-19-2019)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
section_name: Clean Water Coalition regional sewer connection charge and regional sewer user charge.
citation: 14.18.060 - Clean Water Coalition regional sewer connection charge and regional sewer user charge.
full_text:
The Clean Water Coalition (CWC) consists of four member agencies, the City of Henderson, the City of Las Vegas, Clark County Water Reclamation District, and the City of North Las Vegas. The CWC is tasked to implement the systems conveyance and operations program (SCOP) to improve our community's water quality through construction of a 17-mile pipeline that will carry high quality treated wastewater deep into Lake Mead. The SCOP project is funded through a combination of sewer connection and user charges. All member agencies of CWC have implemented these charges.

The regional sewer connection charges for wastewater became effective October 1, 2006. The regional sewer user charges for wastewater became effective July 1, 2007. At its meeting of February 23, 2010, the CWC voted to stop levying assessments to its member agencies based on regional connection and sewer user charges, effective March 1, 2010. With formal termination of the Clean Water Coalition imminent, the city ceased assessment of regional connection fees effective March 1, 2010, and regional sewer user charges effective May 1, 2011.

(Ord. No. 2915, § 1, 5-3-2011; Ord. No. 2857, § 1, 6-1-2010; Ord. 2592, § 1, 2007; Ord. 2536, § 105, 2006; Ord. No. 2951, § 4, 12-20-2011)

citation: 14.18.110 - Charge for taking water without authorization.
full_text:
A.

If a person takes water from the city's water system in violation of a provision of chapter 14.03, chapter 14.05, or chapter 14.06 of the Code, that person and/or the owner(s) of the equipment used to transport the water taken shall be charged and shall pay the estimated water usage at 12x the highest rate per 1,000 gallons in the highest rate block for the potable water volume charge or other rate authorized by council and set forth in the department service rules, whichever rate is higher, and the cost of any damage to city facilities. The department may estimate the amount of water taken, including, but not limited to, based on the use to which that water was apparently put, the equipment used to take or apply that water, the estimated length of time the person was taking the water, and the container or tank used to transport or store that water. The applicable rate shall be based on the rates, fees and charges in this title and/or the department service rules that the department determines is appropriate. Using a container or tank to store that water shall constitute a rebuttable presumption that the container or tank was empty before the person took water from the city's water system and that the container or tank was completely filled after that person took the water.

B.

In addition to being responsible for the charges described in subsection 14.18.110.A, the person who took water from the city's water system in violation of a provision of chapter 14.03, chapter 14.05, or chapter 14.06 of the Code and/or the owner(s) of the equipment used to transport that water is subject to all compliance procedures as prescribed within this title and is subject to all penalties imposed by applicable law.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 27, 9-13-2022)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Purpose and policy. This chapter 14.21 sets forth provisions and authority to ensure compliance with title 14 of the Code and all federal, state, and local requirements enforceable by the city for the protection of public health, safety and welfare.

B.

Scope. The provisions of this chapter 14.21 shall apply to (1) all residents of the city, (2) a person that operates, maintains, repairs, relocates, removes, and/or disconnects to or from the city's water system and/or publicly owned treatment works, (3) a person that violates a provision of title 14 of the Code, (4) a person with a property interest in or control over real property in the city's corporate boundaries or with a property interest in or control over real property to which the city provides any type of water or wastewater service (such as a homeowners association), (5) a user, and (6) a customer. The operation or administration of this chapter 14.21 shall in no way change or diminish the effect of other provisions in this Code dealing with like or similar matters.

C.

Administration. Except as otherwise provided herein, the director shall administer, implement, and enforce the provisions of title 14 of the Code. The director may delegate any powers granted to or duties imposed upon the director, the city, or the department to a person acting in the beneficial interest of the city.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 28, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A person who willfully, knowingly, or negligently violates a provision of chapter 14.03, chapter 14.04, chapter 14.05, chapter 14.06, chapter 14.08, and/or chapter 14.14 of the Code is guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punishable by imprisonment in the Henderson Detention Center for not more than six months and/or by a fine of not more than $1,000.00 per day for each violation. In lieu of all or part of the foregoing punishment which may be imposed, the convicted person may be sentenced to perform a fixed period of community service pursuant to the conditions prescribed in NRS 176.087 and, as applicable, to pay restitution in accordance with NRS 176.033. If a corporation is convicted of a violation, the corporation is punishable by a fine not exceeding $1,000.00 and, as applicable, shall pay restitution in accordance with NRS 176.033, unless otherwise provided by law or the code. With respect to violations that are continuous with respect to time, each day that the violation continues is a separate offense. With respect to violations that are not continuous with respect to time, each prohibited act and/or each failure to perform a required act is a separate offense.

(Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

General.

1.

An enforcement official has the authority to determine whether a violation of title 14 of the Code exists and to take appropriate action to gain compliance with the provisions of title 14 of the Code. These powers include the power to impose administrative fines, to issue notices of violation, to have the city take corrective action, to issue notices and orders, to order and conduct a show cause hearing, to inspect public and private property, to order abatement of a violation, and to use any remedy that is available in title 14 of the Code, in another provision of the Code, and in Nevada law. "Enforcement official" shall mean the director and any director designee.

2.

The enforcement official is authorized to grant minor variations from the strict application of specific provisions of title 14 of the Code where, in the opinion of the director, the corrective work or compliance measures are in substantial compliance with the intent of the applicable provision.

B.

Administrative fine.

1.

The enforcement official may impose, as an alternative to criminal prosecution, administrative fines identified in section 14.21.050 for a violation of a provision of chapter 14.02, chapter 14.03, chapter 14.04, chapter 14.05, chapter 14.06, chapter 14.08, and/or chapter 14.14 of the Code by issuing a notice of violation and shall impose a fine(s) as outlined in this chapter 14.21 and any department enforcement response plan. Payment of an administrative fine shall not relieve the person(s) responsible from their obligation to correct, abate, or stop the violation nor shall it bar further enforcement action by the city or an enforcement official.

2.

Before issuing a notice of violation and imposing a fine for violation of chapter 14.14 of the Code, the enforcement official may (but is not required to) send one or more warning letters to the person(s) alleged or deemed to have violated that chapter or otherwise potentially responsible for the violation. If the enforcement official sends a warning letter, that letter must notify them of the violation and, if applicable, provide a deadline to correct the violation. The enforcement official may have that letter delivered by email, mail, courier service, personal delivery, or any other method of delivery the enforcement official determines is appropriate.

3.

If an administrative fine amount is due and owed to the city by a person cited, the person cited is a customer and the violation relates to utility service to the customer, the city may add that fine amount to the person cited's utility bill as a charge for utility service if:

a.

The person cited did not timely request a hearing before the DUS hearing officer and did not file a timely request for reconsideration; or

b.

The person cited timely requested a hearing before the DUS hearing officer, the DUS hearing officer identified a deadline that fine amount was due, the person cited did not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the DUS hearing officer in the Hearing Officer Decision and (1) the person cited did not file a timely request for reconsideration of the Hearing Officer Decision or (2) the person cited filed a timely request for reconsideration of the Hearing Officer Decision, the director identified a deadline the fine amount was due, the person cited did not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the director and the person cited did not file a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager or (3) the person cited filed a timely request for reconsideration of the Hearing Officer Decision, the director affirmed or modified the fine amount, the person cited filed a timely written appeal to the city manager, the city manager identified a deadline that amount was due and the person cited did not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the city manager; or

c.

The person cited did not timely request a hearing before the DUS hearing officer, the person cited filed a timely request for reconsideration, the director identified a deadline the fine amount was due, the person cited did not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the director and the person cited did not file a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager; or

d.

The person cited did not timely request a hearing before the DUS hearing officer, the person cited filed a timely request for reconsideration, the director identified a deadline the fine amount was due, the person cited did not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the director, the person cited filed a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager, the city manager identified a deadline the fine amount was due and the person cited did not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the city manager.

However, if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and accordingly the city delivered the notice of violation to the property owner in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.4, the city may only add an administrative fine amount due and owed to the city to the customer's utility bill as a charge for utility service if, as to that fine amount, (w) the property owner did not timely request a hearing before the DUS hearing officer and did not file a timely request for reconsideration, or (x) the property owner timely requested a hearing before the DUS hearing officer, received a Hearing Officer Decision and did not file a timely request for reconsideration of that order, or (y) the property owner timely requested a hearing before the DUS hearing officer, received a Hearing Officer Decision, filed a timely request for reconsideration of that Hearing Officer Decision, received a decision from the director and did not file a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager, or (z) the property owner timely requested a hearing before the DUS hearing officer, received a Hearing Officer Decision, filed a timely request for reconsideration of that Hearing Officer Decision, received a decision from the director, filed a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager and received a decision from the city manager.

4.

If an administrative fine amount is due and owed to the city and the person who owes the city that amount holds a city-issued license or city-issued permit, has applied for a city-issued license or city-issued permit, has requested a city inspection, is seeking renewal or transfer of a city-issued license or city-issued permit, or is seeking a city approval, the city may take one or more of the following actions until that person pays the city the amount owed:

a.

Revoke the city-issued license and/or city-issued permit;

b.

Deny, or condition the city's approval of, that person's application for the city-issued license and/or city-issued permit;

c.

Refuse to schedule or perform the city inspection;

d.

Deny, or condition the city's approval of, a renewal or transfer of the city-issued license or city-issued permit; or

e.

Refuse to provide, or impose conditions on, the city approval being sought.

C.

Corrective actions.

1.

When a person, with or without prior authorization from the department, operates, maintains, repairs, relocates, cuts, changes, removes, disconnects, interferes with or damages in any manner the city's public water system, reclaimed water system, raw water system and/or publicly owned treatment works, the department may choose but is not obligated to repair the damages to the city facilities, replace the city facilities, repair some or all damages to any real property or personal property, perform any other remediation work the city determines is necessary and invoice that person for the actual costs of the work. The person invoiced may file a request for reconsideration in accordance with section 14.21.120. The city may add the invoiced amount, as modified by the director or the city manager in accordance with section 14.21.120, to the customer's utility bill as a charge for utility service if the person invoiced is a customer and:

a.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice and did not file a timely request for reconsideration; or

b.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice, the customer filed a timely request for reconsideration and the director affirmed or modified the invoiced amount and identified a deadline that amount was due, the customer did not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the director, and the customer did not file a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager; or

c.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice, the customer filed a timely request for reconsideration, the director affirmed or modified the invoiced amount, the customer files a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager, the city manager affirmed or modified the invoiced amount and identified a deadline that amount was due, and the customer did not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the city manager.

2.

If, under another provision in title 14 of the Code, the city takes corrective action and issues an invoice for the services or work performed, the person invoiced may file a request for reconsideration in accordance with section 14.21.120. The city may add the invoiced amount, as modified by the director or the city manager in accordance with section 14.21.120, to the customer's utility bill as a charge for utility service if the person invoiced is a customer and:

a.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice and did not file a timely request for reconsideration; or

b.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice, the customer filed a timely request for reconsideration, the director affirmed or modified the invoiced amount and identified a deadline that amount was due, the customer did not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the director, and the customer did not file a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager; or

c.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice, the customer filed a timely request for reconsideration, the director affirmed or modified the invoiced amount, the customer filed a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager, the city manager affirmed or modified the invoiced amount and identified a deadline that amount was due, and the customer did not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the city manager.

D.

Termination of service. With or without prior notice and in accordance with any applicable requirements in this title, in the department service rules, and in the department's written procedures, the city may shut off, stop, prevent turn-on of utility service and any associated equipment, and otherwise terminate water, wastewater, reclaimed and/or raw water service without the customer's permission. The city is not obligated to resume or re-establish service until after all violations are corrected to the director's satisfaction, all delinquent fees, rates and charges are paid to the city, and all administrative fine amounts due and owed to the city are paid.

E.

Denial and revocation of permits, licenses and inspections. The city may deny, revoke or withhold city-issued permits, city-issued licenses, and/or inspections for any facility or person associated with the premises.

F.

Notice of violation(s). The city may issue a notice of violation(s).

1.

The notice of violation must contain, at a minimum, the following information:

a.

The name and address (if known) of the person or customer responsible for the violation (referred to as the "person cited");

b.

A brief description of the violation(s) and a reference to the applicable ordinance or code citation(s);

c.

The location, date and (when known) time of the violation;

d.

Where appropriate, the action required to correct the violation(s) and the deadline by when the violation(s) must be corrected;

e.

The name of the person issuing the notice of violation;

f.

The amount of the administrative fine(s) imposed for the violation(s); and

g.

Information advising of the manner and time for responding to the notice of violation.

2.

No error concerning, or omission of, any of the above-described information is grounds for the dismissal of a proceeding relating to a notice of violation unless the person requesting the dismissal demonstrates substantial prejudice from the error and/or omission.

3.

The notice of violation may be issued by any peace officer employed by the city or by an enforcement official. Any notice of violation issued pursuant to this subsection 14.21.040.F shall constitute a declaration that is subject to the penalty of perjury.

4.

An original notice of violation, or a copy thereof, must be filed with and retained by the department. A notice of violation is prima facie evidence of the facts that are alleged therein. The department must deliver the notice of violation personally, by courier service, or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested to the person cited, the property owner (if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property) and, if the person cited is an entity, to an officer, key employee, manager in charge, or registered agent of that entity. That notice of violation will be deemed to have been received by the person to whom it was addressed on the date of delivery if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail or the date of the last delivery attempt if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail and delivery was refused or otherwise unsuccessful.

5.

Where the notice of violation data is entered into and stored in a computer or similar device, any printout or other output readable by sight that accurately reflects such data is an original notice of violation for purposes of a proceeding under this chapter 14.21. Any such data entry that is moved or copied into another computer or similar device is intended to constitute an additional or replacement of the record of the data by the issuing officer or employee and is also an original notice of violation for purposes of a proceeding under this chapter 14.21.

6.

The person cited must respond to a notice of violation within the time prescribed in that notice in one of the following ways:

a.

Admit responsibility for the commission of the violation and liability by paying the amount of any administrative fines; or

b.

Dispute the notice of violation by requesting a hearing before the DUS hearing officer or filing a request for reconsideration. A hearing may be requested by sending a written request to the department with the following information:

(1)

The name of the individual on the notice of violation;

(2)

The current address of the individual; and

(3)

The violation(s) and any administrative fines identified in the notice of violation the person wishes to dispute at the hearing.

7.

If the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property and accordingly the department delivered the notice of violation to the property owner in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.4, that property owner may (a) admit responsibility in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.a and correct the violations in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.8, or (b) dispute the notice of violation by requesting a hearing in accordance subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b.

8.

If the person cited (and any property owner as allowed under subsection 14.21.040.F.7) admits responsibility, that person must correct the violation(s) identified in the notice of violation by the deadline in that notice or, if approved in writing by the director, by a different deadline(s).

9.

If the person cited (and any property owner as allowed under subsection 14.21.040.F.7) fails to admit responsibility or dispute the notice of violation within the time prescribed in that notice and in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6, such failure shall constitute an admission of all matters and facts contained in the notice of violation, each such person is deemed to admit responsibility for the commission of the violation(s) and any administrative fine amounts imposed, any administrative fine amounts imposed are immediately due and owed to the city by each such person and each such person must correct the violation(s) identified in the notice of violation by the deadline(s) in that notice. If the violation(s) are not corrected by such deadline(s), the department (after providing written notice to that person and the property owner - if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property - and at that customer's and that property owner's expense) may choose but is not obligated to perform the abatement or take other action(s) to correct or address the violation(s).

The city shall invoice the person cited and the property owner (if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property) for the actual costs of that work.

10.

If the person cited requests a hearing in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b (or the property owner requests a hearing pursuant to subsection 14.21.040.F.7 and in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b), the department shall schedule a hearing at which each such person that requested the hearing shall be required to appear to dispute the notice of violation(s). The scheduling of the hearing, its conduct and other procedures of the administrative hearing shall be governed by section 14.21.110.

G.

Show cause hearing. The enforcement official may order a person who has violated a provision of title 14 of the Code to appear before the enforcement official and show cause why a proposed enforcement action or additional enforcement action should not be taken.

1.

The notice of the show cause hearing must specify the time and place for the hearing, the proposed enforcement action(s) or additional enforcement action(s), the reasons for such action(s), and a request that the person who has violated a provision of title 14 of the Code show cause why the proposed or additional enforcement action(s) should not be taken.

2.

An original notice of the show cause hearing, or a copy thereof, must be filed with and retained by the department. A notice of the show cause hearing is prima facie evidence of the facts that are alleged therein. The notice must be delivered personally, by courier service, or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested to the person responsible for the violation, the property owner (if the person ordered to appear for the show cause hearing is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property) and, if the person responsible is an entity, on an officer, key employee, manager in charge, or registered agent of that entity. A show cause hearing shall not be a bar against, or prerequisite for, taking any other enforcement action. That notice of show cause hearing will be deemed to have been received by the person to whom it was addressed on the date of delivery if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail or the date of the last delivery attempt if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail and delivery was refused or otherwise unsuccessful.

3.

After the director's designee has reviewed the evidence, the enforcement official may issue one or more orders and notices of violation as are necessary and appropriate to correct and address the violation and bring the person who has violated a provision of title 14 of the Code into compliance with title 14 of the Code.

H.

Administrative orders and consent orders.

1.

When an enforcement official finds that a person has violated, or continues to violate, any provision of title 14 of the Code or an order or decision issued under this chapter, the enforcement official may issue an administrative order to that person that directs that person to come into compliance within a specific time and contains other requirements to address the noncompliance and bring that person into compliance with title 14 of the Code. Issuance of an administrative order shall not be a bar against, or a prerequisite for, taking any other action against that person.

2.

After a notice of violation has been issued, the city may enter into a consent order, assurances of voluntary compliance, or other similar documents establishing an agreement with any person who has violated, or is responsible for noncompliance with, a provision of title 14 of the Code. Such documents shall include specific actions to be taken by the person to correct the noncompliance within a time period specified by the document. A consent order may address administrative fines, corrective action to be taken, and/or other conditions and requirements as agreed to by the city and that person.

I.

Continuous violations. With respect to violations that are continuous with respect to time, each day that the violation continues is a separate violation. With respect to violations that are not continuous with respect to time, each prohibited act and/or each failure to perform a required act is a separate violation.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 29, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
The remedies provided for in this chapter 14.21 are not exclusive of any other remedies that the city may have under the Code, state law, or federal law, and the administrative fines and penalties in this chapter 14.21 may be imposed in addition to any other fine, penalty, fee, charge, notice of violation, or any other remedy provided for in this Code, the laws of the state of Nevada, or the laws of the United States of America. title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

This section 14.21.110 establishes the procedures governing administrative hearings requested in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b. Any hearing conducted pursuant to this section 14.21.110 shall be presided over by the director's designee and such person is referred to as the "DUS hearing officer."

B.

The DUS hearing officer shall issue a notice of hearing that specifies the date, time, and place for the administrative hearing. An original notice of the hearing, or a copy thereof, must be filed with and retained by the department. The department must deliver the notice personally by courier service, or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested to the person cited, the property owner (if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property) and, if the person cited is an entity, on an officer, key employee, manager in charge, or registered agent of that entity. That notice of hearing will be deemed to have been received by the person to whom it was addressed on the date of delivery if delivered personally by courier service, or by mail or the date of the last delivery attempt if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail and delivery was refused or otherwise unsuccessful. The DUS hearing officer may continue the hearing to a different date and/or time at the written request of a party if the DUS hearing officer determines good cause for the continuance exists and the requestor makes such a request before the date and time then scheduled for the hearing.

C.

The person cited, and/or a property owner as allowed under subsection 14.21.040.F.7, that timely requested a hearing in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b is referred to as the "defendant." The city and each defendant are each referred to as a "party."

D.

A party may not serve any interrogatories or other written discovery, take any depositions or conduct other discovery. Affidavits or declarations made under penalty of perjury may be received in evidence at the hearing. The party wishing to use such affidavit or declaration shall, not less than 11 days prior to the date set for the hearing, deliver to the opposing party, either personally or by mail, a copy of the affidavit or declaration which that party proposes to introduce in evidence.

E.

A properly filed notice of violation shall constitute a claim of liability and a claim for relief and no other such claim shall be required. Prima facie evidence of the violation alleged shall be established by the city providing the DUS hearing officer with either a copy of the notice of violation or the data stored in a computer or other device as described in subsection 14.21.040.F.5. No formal appearance by the city attorney's office is required at the hearing.

F.

The DUS hearing officer shall call the hearing to order and otherwise conduct the hearing proceedings. At the request of the hearing officer, city or defendant, a city police officer or marshal shall be present at the hearing to provide security and help maintain order.

G.

At the hearing, each party shall have the opportunity to present witnesses, cross-examine witnesses and present other evidence in support of the party's case. Every witness shall declare, by oath or affirmation, that he or she will testify truthfully. The hearings and dispositions of all such hearings shall be informal, with the DUS hearing officer receiving photographs, testimony and other evidence for the sole purpose of dispensing a fair and speedy resolution between the parties. The DUS hearing officer may exclude irrelevant, immaterial or unduly repetitious evidence. The DUS hearing officer is not bound by the technical rules of evidence, and no informality in any proceeding or in the manner of taking testimony or receiving evidence will invalidate any Hearing Officer Decision.

H.

The DUS hearing officer may question a witness at any time during the hearing. If a witness is questioned by the DUS hearing officer, the party who called the witness may request permission to ask further questions, limited to the area addressed by the DUS hearing officer. When the party who called the witness has asked those questions, the other party may request permission to ask further questions, limited to the area addressed by the DUS hearing officer. The DUS hearing officer may use the experience, technical competence and specialized knowledge of the city's departments, divisions and personnel to evaluate the evidence.

I.

The city has the burden of proof in any such hearing to establish the existence of a violation of title 14 of the Code. The standard of proof to be used by the DUS hearing officer in deciding the issues at such a hearing is by a preponderance of the evidence. The burden of proving any defense shall be upon the party raising that defense.

J.

At the hearing, the DUS hearing officer shall only consider evidence that is relevant to the following issues:

1.

Whether the conditions listed in the issued notice violate title 14 of the Code;

2.

Whether the city afforded the person cited and the property owner (if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property) due process by adhering to the notification procedures specified in subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b and subsection 14.21.110.B;

3.

Whether administrative fine(s) in the issued notice is(are) appropriate;

4.

Whether the action(s) required to correct or abate the violation(s), deadline(s) by when the violation(s) must be corrected or abated, and the consequences of failing to comply are reasonable; and

5.

If a defendant asserts that the violation(s) have been corrected or abated, whether the violation(s) have been adequately corrected or abated.

K.

The hearing may be reported stenographically and/or recorded by audio record, as determined appropriate by the DUS hearing officer. If any party desires the hearing reported stenographically and transcribed by a certified court reporter, that party must make the necessary arrangements and bear the costs thereof and any other party is entitled to purchase a copy of that transcription.

L.

After the DUS hearing officer has reviewed the information presented at the hearing and within 45 days of the hearing (unless the DUS hearing officer extends that 45-day period for good cause), the DUS hearing officer shall issue a written decision, deciding for the defendant(s) and/or the city, entitled "Hearing Officer Decision":

1.

Deciding for the defendant if the DUS hearing officer finds that a violation did not occur or that the defendant should not be held liable; or

2.

Deciding for the city if the DUS hearing officer finds that a violation occurred and that either the person cited or the property owner (if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property) should be held liable and, as part of that Hearing Officer Decision:

a.

Affirm or modify the action(s) required to correct or otherwise abate the violation(s);

b.

Modify the deadline by when the violation(s) must be corrected or abated;

c.

Affirm, increase or reduce the administrative fine(s);

d.

Establish specific deadlines by when the administrative fine(s) must be paid; and/or

e.

If the defendant fails to comply with the Hearing Officer Decision, confirm that the city may perform the abatement or take other action(s) to correct or address the violation(s) and require the person cited and any property owner (if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property) to pay the city's actual costs of that work within 30 days of receiving an invoice from the city; or

3.

Deciding for the city if the DUS hearing officer finds that a violation occurred, that the defendant did not attend the hearing, that the defendant was given sufficient legal notice of the hearing and that the defendant should be held liable and, as part of that Hearing Officer Decision:

a.

Affirm or modify the action(s) required to correct or otherwise abate the violation(s);

b.

Confirm that the city may perform the abatement or take other action(s) to correct or address the violation(s) and require the person cited and any property owner (if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property) to pay the city's actual costs of that work within 30 days of receiving an invoice from the city;

c.

Affirm, increase or reduce the administrative fine(s); and/or

d.

Provide that those administrative fine amounts are deemed to be immediately due and owed to the city.

M.

The DUS hearing officer shall include a certification in the Hearing Officer Decision substantially conforming to the following form: "I certify that the foregoing is a correct reflection of the decision entered in the proceeding properly brought for my consideration pursuant to section 14.21.110 of the Henderson Municipal Code." The original Hearing Officer Decision, or a copy thereof, must be filed with and retained by the department. The department must deliver a copy of the Hearing Officer Decision personally, by courier service, or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested to the person cited, the property owner (if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property) and, if the person cited is an entity, on an officer, key employee, manager in charge, or registered agent of that entity. That Hearing Officer Decision will be deemed to have been received by the person to whom it was addressed on the date of delivery if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail or the date of the last delivery attempt if delivered, personally, by courier service, or by mail and delivery was refused or otherwise unsuccessful.

N.

If the administrative fine amounts are not paid by the deadline(s) established in a Hearing Officer Decision, the unpaid amounts are deemed to be immediately due and owed to the city by the person cited and the property owner (if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property).

O.

The city attorney may petition the Henderson municipal court or such other court of competent jurisdiction for the entry of a civil judgment against each defendant in an amount equal to that stated in the Hearing Officer Decision if the city attorney determines this action to be necessary to enforce the Hearing Officer Decision. Service of such petition on each defendant must be made by certified mail, return receipt requested, restricted delivery, addressed to the defendant at the defendant's last known address, or in any other manner that is authorized by law. An affidavit or declaration of mailing, a signed, returned receipt, or other evidence of service of the civil judgment shall be filed upon such service of the petition.

P.

If the person that timely requested a hearing in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b does not attend the hearing, that person is deemed to admit responsibility for the commission of the violation(s), be responsible for correction or abatement of the violation(s), be responsible for any administrative fine(s), be responsible for the city's actual costs to correct or abate the violation(s), and unpaid amounts are deemed to be immediately due and owed to the city by the person cited and the property owner (if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property).

Q.

The Hearing Officer Decision shall be the final administrative action unless a timely request for reconsideration of that decision is filed under subsection 14.21.120.A.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 31, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

title: Title 14 - UTILITY SERVICES
full_text:
A.

Any resident of the city, a responsible party operating, maintaining, repairing, relocating, removing, or disconnecting the public water system and/or publicly owned treatment works, a person that violates a provision of title 14 of the Code, or a customer directly aggrieved by an enforcement action taken by the city under section 14.21.040 may file a request for reconsideration. Any defendant aggrieved by a Hearing Officer Decision under section 14.21.110, may also file a request for reconsideration. All requests for reconsideration (1) shall be made by that aggrieved person submitting a written request for reconsideration to the director that identifies the action taken or decision made by the department, enforcement official, or city that the aggrieved person would like reconsidered, sets forth in detail the facts supporting the request for reconsideration, and identifies any relief requested; (2) shall be delivered personally, by courier service, or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the director; and (3) must be received by the director, if delivered personally, by courier service, or must be postmarked, if delivered by registered or certified mail, on or before the 11th day after the city takes the action or makes the decision that the aggrieved person would like reconsidered.

B.

After the director receives a request for reconsideration that complies with the requirements in subsection 14.21.120.A, the director may modify or affirm the action taken or decision made and, as part of that decision-making process, may review any information the director determines is relevant and request that the department or the aggrieved person provide additional information. If a request for reconsideration is not timely or fails to provide the information required in subsection 14.21.120.A(1), then the director shall dismiss the request for reconsideration on the grounds that it was untimely and/or insufficient. The director's decision must be in writing, be made within 30 days of the director's receipt of that request for reconsideration and delivered to the aggrieved person that made the request personally, by courier service, or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested. In the director's discretion, the director may extend the time for the director to issue that decision. The director's decision will be deemed to have been received by the person to whom it was addressed on the date of delivery if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail or the date of the last delivery attempt if delivered by mail and delivery was refused or otherwise unsuccessful. The director's decision to modify or affirm the action taken or decision made, or to dismiss the request for reconsideration, shall be deemed to be the city's final administrative action and decision unless timely and sufficiently appealed to the city manager in accordance with subsection 14.21.120.C. Unless otherwise ordered by a court of competent jurisdiction, the director's decision shall remain in effect during the pendency of any judicial appeal or other judicial review of that decision sought pursuant to and in accordance with applicable law.

C.

If a decision made by the director in accordance with subsection 14.21.120.B is unsatisfactory to the aggrieved person requesting reconsideration, the aggrieved person may, within 11 days after receiving the director's decision, appeal that decision to the city manager. All appeals (1) shall be made by that aggrieved person submitting a written request to the city manager that identifies the director's decision that the aggrieved person wishes to reverse or modify, sets forth in detail the facts supporting the appeal, and identifies any relief requested; (2) shall be delivered personally, by courier service, or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the city manager and to the director; and (3) must be received by the city manager and the director, if delivered personally or by courier service, or must be postmarked, if delivered by registered or certified mail, on or before the 11th day after the aggrieved person receives the director's decision. An appeal that complies with the foregoing requirements shall be decided by the city manager within 30 days from the date it is received by the city manager unless the city manager, in the city manager's discretion, extends the time for the city manager to issue that decision. As part of that decision-making process, the city manager may review any information city manager determines is relevant and request that the department or the aggrieved person provide additional information. If an appeal is not timely or does not provide the information required in item (1) in this subsection, the city manager shall dismiss the appeal. The city manager's decision to modify or affirm the action taken or decision made, or to dismiss the appeal, shall be deemed to be the city's final administrative action and decision. The director's decision shall remain in effect during the pendency of any appeal to the city manager. Unless otherwise ordered by a court of competent jurisdiction, the city manager's decision shall remain in effect during the pendency of any judicial appeal or other judicial review of that decision sought pursuant to and in accordance with applicable law.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 32, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

citation: 15.01.035 - Existing buildings, structures, and building service equipment.[2]
full_text:
Existing buildings, structures and building service equipment shall comply with the provisions of this section.

A.

Additions, alterations or repairs. Buildings, structures and building service equipment to which additions, alterations and repairs are made shall comply with all the requirements of the technical codes for new facilities, except as specifically provided in this chapter.

Additions, alterations and repairs may be made to any building, structure and building service equipment without requiring the existing building, structure or building service equipment to comply with all the requirements of the technical codes provided the addition, alteration or repair conforms to that required for a new building, structure or building service equipment.

Additions, alterations or repairs shall not be made to an existing building, structure or building service equipment that will cause the existing building or building structure service equipment to be in violation of any of the provisions of the technical codes, nor shall such additions, alterations or repairs cause the existing building, structure or building service equipment to become unsafe. An unsafe condition shall be deemed to have been created if an addition, alteration or repair:

1.

Causes the existing building to become structurally unsafe;

2.

Does not provide adequate means of egress in compliance with the provisions of the building code;

3.

Creates a fire hazard as determined by the Henderson fire marshal;

4.

Reduces required fire resistance;

5.

Causes building service equipment to become overloaded or exceed its rated capacity;

6.

Creates a health hazard as determined by the Health District of Southern Nevada or otherwise creates conditions dangerous to human life and safety.

Any addition, alteration or repair of a building which involves a change in use or occupancy shall not exceed the height, number of stories or area permitted by the building code for new buildings. Any building plus new additions shall not exceed the height, number of stories or area permitted by the building code for new buildings. All fire systems required by chapter 9 of the Building and Fire Safety Administrative Code because of the area of the addition or the area of the addition plus the existing building area shall be extended throughout the building or structure or separated per the fire code.

New additions and alterations shall comply with the code in effect at the time of construction of the addition or alteration. Additions and alterations may not be made to an existing building or structure where such building or structure is not in full compliance with the provisions of the applicable building code in effect at the time of construction of the building unless the proposed addition or alteration includes work to bring the existing building into compliance with the applicable code.

Alterations and repairs to an existing building or structure which are nonstructural and do not adversely affect a structural member or system, or a part of the building having required fire resistance, may be made with the same materials as the building or structure, subject to the approval of the building official. The installation or replacement of glass shall be as required for new installations.

Additions or alterations shall not be made to an existing building or structure which is in violation of other provisions of the Henderson Municipal Code unless such additions or alterations include work to bring the building into compliance with the applicable provisions of the Henderson Municipal Code. This limitation does not apply to lawful non-conforming buildings or uses as determined by the Henderson community development department.

B.

Existing building service equipment installations. Building service equipment lawfully in existence at the time of adoption of the technical codes may have its use, maintenance or repair continued if such building service equipment is in accordance with its original design and does not pose a hazard to life, health or property. Minor additions, alterations and repairs to existing building service equipment may be made in accordance with the technical codes in effect at the time of original installation, subject to approval of the building official, and provided such additions, alterations and repairs will not cause the existing building service equipment to become unsafe, unsanitary or overloaded.

C.

Existing occupancy. Buildings in existence at the time of the adoption of the building code may have their use or occupancy continued if such use or occupancy was legal at the time of the adoption of the building code and provided such continued use is not dangerous to life, health or safety. Any change in the use or occupancy of an existing building shall require that the building be made to conform to all current technical code requirements based upon the new use or occupancy, including upgrade of the building's structural system. In addition, any fire safety system required by the codes because of the occupancy change shall be extended throughout the building or structure or separated per the fire code.

D.

Maintenance. All existing and new buildings, structures, signs, and building service equipment and all parts thereof shall be maintained in a safe working condition and in accordance with the provisions of the adopted technical codes and City of Henderson Property Maintenance Code as adopted in chapter 15.12 of the Henderson Municipal Code. All devices and safeguards which are required by the technical codes shall be maintained in conformance with the technical code in effect at the time of installation. The owner or his designated agent shall be responsible for the maintenance of buildings, structures, building service equipment and assuring that all required fire and life safety systems are maintained in an operable condition at all times. To determine compliance with the requirement of this section, the building official may cause any building, structure or building service equipment to be re-inspected.

(Ord. 2736, § 1 (part), 2008)

title: Title 15 - BUILDINGS AND CONSTRUCTION
chapter: Chapter 15.01 - BUILDING AND FIRE SAFETY ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF HENDERSON, NEVADA
full_text:
For the purposes of this chapter, certain terms, phrases, words and their derivatives shall be defined as specified in this section or other adopted technical codes. Where words and terms are not defined, they shall have their ordinary accepted meanings within the context with which they are used. The latest edition of Webster's Third New International Dictionary of the English Language, Unabridged, shall be considered as providing ordinary accepted meanings. Words used in the singular include the plural, and the plural the singular. Words used in the masculine gender include the feminine, and the feminine the masculine.

Alter or alteration means any construction or renovation to an existing building, structure or building service equipment other than repair or addition.

Amusement and transportation system (ATS) is any ride, device, building or structure that is used primarily for human entertainment and enjoyment, either moving or stationary. The final determination whether a ride, device or structure shall be classified under this definition shall be made by the building official. For the purposes of this chapter, slot machines, electronic gaming devices, pinball games, electronic arcade games, and non-motorized playground equipment are not amusement and transportation systems.

Amusement system or transportation system permit means permits issued by the building official authorizing construction and installation of an ATS. At the option of the building official, an amusement and transportation system permit may include in its scope any subsidiary permits for supporting or enclosing structures and buildings, associated and accessory structures, utility permits, and other building service equipment.

Approved, as to materials, types of construction, equipment and systems refers to approval by the building official as the result of investigation and tests, or by reason of accepted principles or tests by recognized authorities, technical or scientific organizations.

Approved agency is a quality assurance agency that has been approved and listed by the building official pursuant to this chapter.

Approved construction documents are construction documents that have been reviewed and approved for permit by the building official pursuant to this chapter.

Approved fabricator means a company that constructs or assembles standardized building components into assemblies in an approved manner based on submittal of specified documentation and successful periodic evaluation for conformance to standard operating procedures and tests such that the company is listed on the published approved fabricators list.

Approved products are products that are included on product listings from testing and listing agencies approved by the building official.

Approved special inspector is a special inspector who has been approved and listed by the building official pursuant to this chapter.

Area acceptance report is a report to the building official that states all required activities for special inspection item(s) are complete and acceptable for a portion of the work authorized by a permit.

ATS means "amusement and transportation system" as defined in this chapter.

Building means any structure used or intended for supporting or sheltering any use or occupancy.

Building code means that edition of the International Building Code and amendments thereto adopted by the City of Henderson and referenced in chapter 15.08 of the Henderson Municipal Code.

Building, existing. "Existing building" means a building erected prior to the adoption of the currently adopted technical codes or one for which a legal, unexpired building permit has been issued by the building official.

Building official means the City of Henderson building official and the building official's designee(s).

Building service equipment means the plumbing, mechanical, electrical and elevator equipment including piping, wiring, fixtures and other accessories that provide potable water, sanitation, lighting, heating, ventilation, cooling, refrigeration, fire-fighting and transportation facilities essential for the habitable occupancy of a building or structure for the designated use and occupancy.

Building service equipment, existing. "Existing building service equipment" means building service equipment lawfully installed prior to the adoption of the currently adopted technical codes or for which a legal, unexpired permit has been issued by the building official.

Certificate of operation means a document issued by the building official on an annual basis certifying that an amusement and transportation system (ATS) has been inspected and found to be in compliance with the manufacturer's requirements for operation and maintenance, the approved operations and maintenance manual(s), and approved plans and any other requirements of this chapter.
